# UBS's AI Strategy: Analysis of Dominance in Finance

This report by Dany Kitishian (Klover.AI) provides a comprehensive analysis of UBS Group AG's artificial intelligence strategy, which is positioned as a C-suite-driven strategic mandate to become an "AI-first" institution. The analysis covers UBS's philosophical framework, investment strategy, technological foundation, and competitive positioning.

## Core Philosophy: "AIm high" – Augmentation Over Automation

UBS's AI strategy is founded on the "AIm high" philosophy, which frames AI as a "general purpose technology" focused on augmenting human intelligence rather than replacing employees. The firm explicitly acknowledges AI limitations including "bias and explainability issues," privacy concerns, and hallucination risks. CEO Sergio P. Ermotti has publicly endorsed AI as a core pillar of the firm's future.

## Three-Layer Value Chain Framework

UBS's Chief Investment Office developed a structured framework for AI investment:

1. **Enabling Layer** (USD 185B projected value by 2027): Semiconductor design, cloud infrastructure, data centers, power supply
2. **Intelligence Layer** (strongest growth trajectory): LLM developers, proprietary data owners
3. **Application Layer** (USD 395B addressable market by 2027): Where tools are embedded into monetizable use cases

The firm projects the total AI industry will grow from USD 28 billion (2022) to USD 420 billion (2027), a 72% CAGR.

## Post-Merger Advantage: Credit Suisse Acquisition

The 2023 Credit Suisse acquisition accelerated UBS's growth trajectory by 7-10 years, creating a wealth management giant with over USD 5 trillion in invested assets. The integration targets USD 13 billion in gross savings by 2026, which will fund technology investments. By end of 2024, all major legal entity mergers were completed.

## Technological Foundation

- **Microsoft Partnership**: Deep strategic collaboration on Azure platform, providing secure access to Azure OpenAI Service and AI Search. Goal: run 50%+ of applications on Azure.
- **Data Mesh Architecture**: Decentralized approach treating data as a product, breaking down silos between divisions.
- **UBS Evidence Lab**: Proprietary primary research team with 45+ practice areas, covering 5,000+ companies, producing 3,000 research reports annually. Ranked #1 for Alternative Data by Greenwich Associates. Generates unique datasets including "Global AI Developer & Model Tracker" and "Global Cloud GPU Chips Price Monitor."
- **AI Factory Model**: Industrialized, repeatable process for AI solution delivery.
- **UBS Next**: Strategic venture arm investing in AI companies (Synthesized, Shield, BigPanda, Droit, Ethic).

## Internal AI Ecosystem

- **UBS Red (STAAT)**: AI assistant deployed to 30,000 employees across key divisions. Saves advisors 3-4 hours per client meeting, provides proactive insights, and identifies growth opportunities.
- **AI Analyst Clones**: Lifelike digital avatars of research analysts using OpenAI + Synthesia technology. Goal: increase video output from 1,000 to 5,000 videos annually. All content requires human analyst approval with AI transparency disclaimers.
- **50,000 Microsoft Copilot licenses** deployed by Q1 2025.

## Competitive Data Moat

UBS is the world's second-largest wealth manager with USD 6.087 trillion in invested assets (end of 2024). The firm's 160-year history provides longitudinal data. The data creates a self-reinforcing "flywheel": better data → better AI models → better service → more assets → more data.

## Comparative Analysis

- **vs. JPMorgan Chase**: JPM spends USD 18B on technology vs. UBS's ~USD 1.1B, but UBS's investment is highly concentrated on wealth management
- **vs. Goldman Sachs**: GS focuses on developer productivity; UBS has dual focus on internal efficiency AND client-facing innovation
- **vs. Morgan Stanley**: MS relies on singular OpenAI partnership; UBS has diversified, vertically integrated ecosystem
- **vs. Bank of America**: BofA's "Erica" excels at retail banking scale; UBS focuses on UHNW complexity

## Monetization and Risks

Monetization flows through two channels: (1) enhanced operating leverage through advisor efficiency, and (2) direct asset growth through superior client experience. Key targets: USD 200 billion in Net New Assets annually by 2028, cost-income ratio below 70% by 2026.

Key risks include regulatory concerns (bias, privacy, cybersecurity), AI governance challenges, and most critically, the execution risk of integrating 114 petabytes of data from Credit Suisse (total integration cost: USD 14 billion).

## Final Thesis

UBS's AI dominance rests on three synergistic forces: a coherent strategy focused on wealth management augmentation, unmatched proprietary data assets (deepened by Credit Suisse acquisition), and a purpose-built industrialized engine (Microsoft partnership, data mesh, AI factories). This creates an "unassailable flywheel" that competitors will find difficult to replicate.

# Innovation and AI at UBS

We are investing in advanced technology and in our people to drive better business outcomes.

*   [Responsible AI](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai.html#responsible-ai)
*   [AI in action](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai.html#aiinaction)
*   [Talent](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai.html#talent)
*   [Investing in the future](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/investing-in-the-future.html)

We are also embedding artificial intelligence across our operations to foster innovation. This lets us provide smarter, more efficient, and highly personalized services, ultimately enriching the overall client experience.

## Our approach

![Image 4: Girl looking at phone](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai/_jcr_content/root/contentarea/mainpar/toplevelgrid_copy_co/col_1/textimage_1804627360/image.580.jpg/1784709970426.jpg)

### AI at UBS

We aim to become an AI enabled financial institution where all our stakeholders such as clients, employees, and shareholders benefit from AI-powered tools, and where we build AI-driven capabilities to maximize our impact in a responsible and sustainable way.

Building on more than a decade of experience in AI, our strategy is focused on reshaping business capabilities for clients and boosting daily productivity for employees.

We operate in a Hub and Spoke model. The Chief AI Office (CAIO), as part of the Group Chief Operating Office, sits at the center of this effort, bringing together strategy, governance, and execution whilst the Business Divisions and Group Functions own delivery and outcomes. CAIO provides firmwide coordination, with dedicated accountability for AI governance, regulatory engagement, and AI Capabilities enablement.

We are consolidating AI platforms into a single strategic UBS AI platform, providing shared AI capabilities and a common foundation that business divisions and functions can extend to address specific needs. The platform, named UBS Claves, offers a range of models, from lightweight to frontier, with automated routing that optimizes performance and token costs. We are also strengthening AI evaluation capabilities to support consistent governance, measurement, and value tracking.

## Responsible AI

### Our AI Principles

Trust is at the heart of everything we do, and this has never been more critical in the era of artificial intelligence (AI). We develop, adopt, and operate AI based on clear principles: respect for human autonomy, prevention of harm, and a commitment to fairness and transparency, all underpinned by our risk-aware[culture](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/our-culture.html), [Code of Conduct and Ethics](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/our-culture.html#code).

### AI Policy framework

We support our AI initiatives with robust governance and control frameworks designed to safeguard the interests of our clients, employees, and all stakeholders. Our Group AI policy defines clear standards and requirements for developing, adopting, and operating AI responsibly. Dedicated AI governance bodies, including the AI Operating & Risk Committee, have accountability for overseeing the execution of our AI strategy, enabling the integration of AI across the firm while ensuring strict adherence to our AI risk framework, regulatory and compliance requirements, internal policies, and ethical guidelines.

All employees receive mandatory annual training in the responsible use of AI, with ongoing additional training for specialists.

![Image 5: A man giving presentation](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai/_jcr_content/root/contentarea/mainpar/toplevelgrid_copy_co_1733652519/col_2/textimage/image.580.jpg/1784825681384.jpg)

## AI in action: real-world case studies

Expand all

 AI-powered Global Research tools 

![Image 6: Businesswoman with laptop against London financial district](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai/_jcr_content/root/contentarea/mainpar/gridcontrol_12705256/col_1/accordion/accordionsplit/textimage_copy/image.580.jpg/1785251296447.jpg)

### Scaling high-quality research content with AI

AI is transforming UBS research workflows – boosting productivity, increasing engagement, and enabling analysts to deliver high-quality insights faster and at scale.

By embedding AI directly into the tools analysts already use, teams can now draft, refine, translate and distribute research content more efficiently and consistently.

The award-winning* initiative began with simple yet high-impact features such as AI-assisted titles and email hooks. These tools have now been used more than 15,000 times, and have increased email open rates by 16 percent.

Work then expanded into developing a broader analyst toolkit that now supports nearly 1,000 Global Research professionals. Our CoAuthor tool, used more than 30,000 times, helps strengthen clarity, consistency and overall content quality.

And we didn’t stop there. AI has also reshaped video production, moving from standard studio production to a more scalable model, using AI-generated analyst avatars and automated script generation. This enables us to produce significantly more video content at scale, helping meet strong and growing client demand for insights delivered in video format, while continuing to drive high engagement.

**Client impact:** Faster, more scalable research production, delivering measurable improvements in client experience, engagement and reach.

*Our work in this space has been recognized with a 2026 Celent Model Sell Side Award for GenAI Automation.

 AI-powered insights, advisor-led relationships 

![Image 7: Diverse team having meeting in open workspace](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai/_jcr_content/root/contentarea/mainpar/gridcontrol_12705256/col_1/accordion/accordionsplit_1767200162/textimage_copy/image.580.jpg/1785320445404.jpg)

### AI-powered insights, advisor-led relationships

At UBS Global Wealth Management, we are harnessing artificial intelligence to help advisors deliver greater value to clients–more efficiently, more proactively, and with greater confidence. By transforming vast amounts of data into timely, actionable intelligence, AI enables advisors to focus less on information gathering and more on what matters most: building meaningful client relationships and delivering personalized advice.

**Equipping advisors with timely client intelligence**

One of our flagship AI solutions, **STAAT Insights***, provides more than 5,000 UBS financial advisors in the US with highly personalized intelligence at the moments it matters most. The platform analyzes thousands of internal and external signals to identify relevant client opportunities– from significant life events and property transactions to late–stage business funding activity.

Advisors receive concise, AI-generated briefings directly in their inboxes ahead of client meetings and can access insights on demand throughout the day.

**Client impact:** These insights help advisors prepare more efficiently and engage clients with timely, relevant, and data-driven conversations. Nearly 90 percent of advisor teams actively use the platform, saving an estimated 1,200 hours of meeting preparation each week. In 2025, STAAT Insights generated more than 20 million AI-identified client opportunities - a 50 percent increase year over year.

**Delivering global intelligence with local relevance**

In Hong Kong and Singapore, our **Conversational Insights*** solution brings similar capabilities to more than 200 client advisors. By consolidating client, portfolio, and activity data into clear, actionable intelligence, the platform helps advisors quickly identify meaningful opportunities and service needs.

Whether highlighting upcoming maturities, cash-flow events, client milestones, or portfolio changes, Conversational Insights enables advisors to engage clients at the right time and with greater context. The result is a more proactive approach to client servicing and more personalized client interactions. Since launch, advisors in these markets have reported meaningful reductions in preparation time, while gaining greater confidence in delivering tailored, timely and relevant client conversations.

**Client impact:** These AI-powered insights help advisors spend less time searching for information and more time delivering advice. By surfacing the most relevant opportunities and priorities, these solutions enable advisors to prepare faster, engage more proactively, and deepen client relationships through more personalized interactions.

*Our leadership in AI-enabled wealth management has been recognized globally, **with 2026 Celent Model Wealth Manager Award** for Data, Analytics and AI, **Best Wealth Management Firm for Use of AI in the US**, Financial Times PWM Wealth Tech Awards, **Best International Private Bank for AI Adoption and Digital Innovation**, Asian Private Banker Awards for Distinction 2025, **Asia’s best for digital solutions 2026** | Euromoney Private Banking Awards 2026

 In-house AI Assistant ‘Red’ 

![Image 8: Businesswoman using AI assistant on smartphone](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai/_jcr_content/root/contentarea/mainpar/gridcontrol_12705256/col_1/accordion/accordionsplit_437667254/textimage_copy/image.580.jpg/1784857069736.jpg)

### Making enterprise knowledge instantly accessible

Red, UBS’s in-house AI assistant, helps employees access trusted internal knowledge quickly and complete knowledge-intensive tasks more efficiently. It brings together curated UBS content and generative AI capabilities in one place, making it easier to find information, draft content and move work forward.

By combining official UBS sources – including CIO research, process and product information, and factsheets – with capabilities such as summarization, drafting and translation, Red simplifies how employees find information and carry out everyday tasks. This reduces time spent searching across fragmented sources and supports faster, more consistent execution.

The solution has been rolled out to around 100,000 employees and has supported more than 25 million queries since launch, demonstrating broad adoption across the firm.

Based on user feedback, Red **saves employees an average of 80 minutes per week**,freeing up time for more meaningful client interactions and deeper engagement with clients' individual needs.

**The outcome**: Improved productivity and faster access to trusted information across the organization.

 Powering the employee journey with AI 

![Image 9: Two colleagues discussing in front of computer](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai/_jcr_content/root/contentarea/mainpar/gridcontrol_12705256/col_1/accordion/accordionsplit_444717803/textimage_copy/image.580.jpg/1785320512646.jpg)

### Faster, simpler and more personalized HR services for employees

AI is helping UBS reimagine the employee journey across Human Resources – from everyday support and onboarding to recruiting and performance management. By embedding generative AI and automation into the tools and processes employees and managers already use, we are making HR services faster, simpler and easier to access.

**AskHR, our GenAI-powered HR assistant** – Around 100,000 employees can now book vacation, review leave plans and access policies, as well as get guidance 24/7directly through Microsoft Teams. With close to an 80 percent in-app resolution rate, AskHR is improving the employee experience and reducing operational workload.

**Candidate experience (AI-enabled onboarding)**– We are automating key steps in the hiring and onboarding process to make the experience faster for candidates and HR teams alike. In multiple countries, automated contract generation for many hires has reduced time to contract from 24 hours to approximately 20 minutes, with built-in consistency, compliance and human oversight.

**Performance management (GenAI-assisted evaluation summaries)**– Generative AI helps line managers turn large volumes of structured and unstructured feedback into clear, high-quality year-end evaluation summary drafts. While managers remain fully accountable for the final assessment, the solution reduces manual effort and improves consistency, quality and compliance. It is already saving over 32,000 hours of line manager time each year.

**The outcome**: A more seamless, AI-powered employee experience that helps our people complete HR tasks faster, freeing up time for higher-value activities and supporting greater consistency and additional automated compliance checks.

 Driving productivity and efficiency in global functions 

![Image 10: Employees having conversation in corridor at UBS Paris](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai/_jcr_content/root/contentarea/mainpar/gridcontrol_12705256/col_1/accordion/accordionsplit_925690108/textimage_copy/image.580.jpg/1784891545028.jpg)

### Using AI to simplify complex work across Sourcing, Communications, Legal, Finance and Compliance

Across global functions, UBS is applying artificial intelligence, generative AI and automation to accelerate and simplify complex, knowledge-intensive work. From financial data sourcing and procurement automation to media intelligence and legal workflows, AI is helping teams reduce manual effort, improve consistency and deliver faster outcomes at scale.

**Speeding up sourcing**– Our Group Real Estate and Supply Chain (GRESC) team introduced a GenAI-enabled solution, ‘Front Door’, that guides employees through creating sourcing requests and assessing risk applicability. By simplifying inputs and automating guidance, the required manual entry fields have been reduced by almost 40 percent, and processing sourcing initiatives is now up to 60 percent faster.

**Embedding AI into our Legal workflows**– The purpose-designed platform ‘Harvey’ within Group Legal enables high-quality drafting, summarization, and review of complex legal content, powered by models trained specifically on legal language and structures. The tool has direct access to jurisdictional knowledge, enables large-scale document processing via a secure vault, and automates sophisticated workflows through reusable prompt chains. It seamlessly integrates with day-to-day applications, embedding AI directly into the core legal workflow. The increased efficiency delivers direct cost savings of at least USD 1 million. It also enables the insourcing of external legal work, generating an additional USD 1 million in savings in 2026 alone, while significantly improving decision-making and risk anticipation. Through our Legal translation tool, teams have direct access to professional-grade, context-aware translations across core languages, reducing reliance on external services and accelerating cross-border collaboration – saving an estimated USD 1 million annually through efficiency gains and reduced spend.

**AI‑powered live event translation**–so clients and audiences can follow UBS events along in their own language – enhancing accessibility and enabling real‑time multilingual experiences for a truly global audience, used at flagship events such as the UBS Greater China Conference 2026 and the UBS Asian Investment Conference 2026.

**Accelerating our Finance transformation**– The ledger is the backbone of Finance, essential to our financial and regulatory reporting. Modernizing our ledger requires sourcing and transforming large volumes of data from hundreds of business systems and thousands of data feeds – a significant task. But, through applying AI, we have been able to accelerate this work by around 50 percent.

**MyPolicies AI assistant** transforms how employees access governance information by replacing manual document searches with a personalized, AI-powered assistant that delivers natural-language answers with cited sources tailored to user roles and locations. Since its launch in August 2024, the solution has supported more than 288,000 conversations (around 418,000 questions), helping employees find accurate guidance faster while reducing time spent navigating complex policy documents. With access to over 1,100 policies and guidelines and more than 110,000 users across the bank, the tool demonstrates strong and sustained adoption at scale. Based on an average saving of 10 minutes per conversation, the solution has delivered approximately 48,000 hours saved since launch, while improving consistency in how employees access policy information.

**The outcome**: Faster, more scalable execution across global functions, with AI helping employees reduce manual effort and speed up delivery, improve insights, strengthen quality and unlock measurable productivity and efficiency gains.

 Developer productivity 

![Image 11: Computer programmer at work](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai/_jcr_content/root/contentarea/mainpar/gridcontrol_12705256/col_1/accordion/accordionsplit_349476317/textimage/image.580.jpg/1784891012959.jpg)

### Bringing AI into everyday work

Within technology, GitHub Copilot has become a cornerstone of the AI-augmented engineering strategy.

The AI-powered coding assistant is available across approved development environments and supports engineers throughout the software development lifecycle. Common use cases include code generation, refactoring, debugging, documentation, testing and application modernization.

The rollout has been supported by structured onboarding, training resources and active communities of practice designed to help engineers maximize the value of AI-assisted development. As a result, AI is becoming an increasingly embedded part of day-to-day engineering work across UBS.

Adoption has continued to grow, with approximately 18,000 engineers enabled on GitHub Copilot across the firm. Usage data also points to strong engagement, with around 89 percent of licensed users actively coding and consuming available tokens, exceeding both current targets and expectations. This level of participation demonstrates the growing confidence engineers have in AI-assisted development and the value they are seeing from these tools in their daily work.

**The outcome:** Increased productivity for employees and faster and secure software development through AI-powered assistance.

## Open Source at UBS

Open source plays an important role in UBS’s technology strategy. Across the firm, engineering teams contribute to open-source projects, participate in industry foundations, and collaborate with technology communities to help advance the tools and platforms used across financial services and the wider technology ecosystem.

[Read more about how Open source plays an important role in UBS](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/open-source.html)

## Talent

 Building AI capability at scale 

![Image 16: Man working on computer](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/our-firm/what-we-do/technology/innovation-and-ai/_jcr_content/root/contentarea/mainpar/toplevelgrid_copy_co_982297806/col_1/textimage/image.580.jpg/1784859360148.jpg)

UBS is building AI capability at scale through a coordinated upskilling program that combines foundational AI learning for all employees with role-specific specialist training for leaders, managers and technical professionals.

Foundational learning is available to all employees through a mix of offerings such as the AI Citizen and AI Enabler learning journeys, Global Learning Weeks, AI Power Hour and online AI courses. Adoption is tracked enterprise-wide: more than **38,000 employees** have completed AI learning journeys; since 2024, more than **49,000 employees** have enrolled in AI-related online courses; and 2026 Global Learning Weeks included **56 AI sessions**, more than **45,000 enrollments** and **12,000 employees** participating in role-specific AI training programs. By July 2026, more than **21,000 employees** had earned the AI Citizen badge (**28 percent of employees**) and more than **96 percent of managers** had completed the initial AI Enabler stages, with outcomes validated through assessments and digital badging.

Role-specific specialist training is delivered through targeted pathways, including a completed senior leadership AI program with reported adoption metrics. For senior leaders, the AI Senior Leadership Journey covers responsible AI leadership, strategic decision-making and enterprise adoption; approximately **1,300 senior leaders**, including the Group Executive Board, have completed it.

The AI Enabler learning journey supports managers in applying AI to team practices and people leadership. For technical employees, the AI Builder learning journey is being established within the Certified Engineers (CE) program, which enrolls over **19,000**employees, as a **10-badge** pathway covering AI-assisted requirements engineering, automated testing, prompt engineering, custom AI agents, responsible AI and applied product development.

UBS also develops advanced AI capability through hands-on AI challenge programs built around real business challenges, curated datasets and production-grade AI environments. Adoption metrics are reported for these programs. The inaugural 2024 challenge engaged approximately 800 participants across 15 countries and generated nearly 300 AI solutions, while the 2025 Agentic AI challenge attracted more than 1,000 participants within the first 10 days and produced hundreds of solution submissions. These challenge-based programs along with our yearly hackathons complemented formal learning journeys by providing practical, role-specific technical learnings with some winning solutions deployed into business workflows.

We have also established the UBS – IDSIA AI Lab, a group-wide research and innovation network that brings together 20 of IDSIA’s top researchers with 100 UBS business domain specialists.

args.summary:
This webpage outlines UBS's comprehensive strategy and initiatives around artificial intelligence (AI) and innovation as of mid-2026. UBS aims to become an AI-enabled financial institution, building on over a decade of AI experience. The strategy is organized under a Hub and Spoke model, led by the Chief AI Office (CAIO), which provides firmwide coordination for governance, regulatory engagement, and AI capabilities. UBS is consolidating AI platforms into a single strategic platform called UBS Claves, which offers a range of models with automated routing for performance and cost optimization.

**Responsible AI:** UBS develops AI based on principles of respect for human autonomy, prevention of harm, fairness, and transparency, supported by a Group AI policy and governance bodies like the AI Operating & Risk Committee. All employees receive mandatory annual AI training.

**AI in Action - Real-World Case Studies:**
- **Global Research:** AI tools (e.g., CoAuthor) support nearly 1,000 research professionals. AI-assisted titles/email hooks have been used 15,000+ times, increasing email open rates by 16%. AI-generated analyst avatars enable scalable video content. Awarded a 2026 Celent Model Sell Side Award.
- **Wealth Management:** STAAT Insights provides 5,000+ US financial advisors with personalized client intelligence, saving an estimated 1,200 hours of meeting prep per week. It generated 20M+ AI-identified client opportunities in 2025. Conversational Insights serves 200+ advisors in Hong Kong and Singapore. Awarded 2026 Celent Model Wealth Manager Award and multiple other industry awards.
- **In-house AI Assistant 'Red':** Rolled out to ~100,000 employees, supporting 25M+ queries since launch, saving users an average of 80 minutes per week.
- **HR Services:** AskHR (GenAI assistant) serves ~100,000 employees with ~80% in-app resolution. AI-enabled onboarding reduced contract generation time from 24 hours to ~20 minutes. GenAI-assisted performance evaluation summaries save 32,000+ hours of manager time annually.
- **Global Functions:** AI is applied in Sourcing (60% faster processing), Legal (Harvey platform, saving ~$2M+), Finance (50% acceleration in ledger modernization), and policy access (MyPolicies, 288K+ conversations, 48,000 hours saved).
- **Developer Productivity:** GitHub Copilot enabled for ~18,000 engineers, with ~89% active usage.

**Open Source:** UBS actively contributes to open-source projects and collaborates with industry foundations.

**Talent & Upskilling:** UBS is building AI capability at scale. Over 38,000 employees completed AI learning journeys; 49,000+ enrolled in AI courses since 2024; 21,000+ earned the AI Citizen badge by July 2026; ~1,300 senior leaders completed the AI Senior Leadership Journey. The AI Builder pathway is a 10-badge program within the Certified Engineers program (19,000+ employees). Hands-on AI challenges (e.g., 2025 Agentic AI challenge with 1,000+ participants) complement formal learning.

**Partnerships:** UBS has launched the Oxford-UBS Centre of Applied AI and the UBS-IDSIA AI Lab. It maintains strategic partnerships with Microsoft Azure and other leading technology companies and fintechs.

[Mark Whitcroft](https://uk.linkedin.com/in/mark-whitcroft-8a48a534?trk=public_post_feed-actor-name)

* [Report this post](/uas/login?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fposts%2Fmark-whitcroft-8a48a534_behind-ubs-ai-strategy-to-win-wallet-share-activity-7401602705757982721-5KGZ&trk=public_post_ellipsis-menu-semaphore-sign-in-redirect&guestReportContentType=POST&_f=guest-reporting)

UBS is saving 10,000+ adviser hours a month with AI. That’s not a future goal - it’s happening right now. Joe Cordeira, Chief Data & Analytics Officer at UBS, recently shared how their wealth management teams are using AI today - and there’s a lot to take in: 🔹 Client meeting prep: AI auto-generates briefing sheets so advisers walk in ready 🔹 Prospecting: Relationship-mapping from public data identifies new warm leads 🔹 Portfolio alerts: Automated insights detect concentration risk or life events 🔹 Chatbots: 20,000+ prompts a month from advisers answered instantly 🔹 Meeting summaries & CRM updates: Automated, saving 20–30 mins per meeting 🔹 Copilot rollout: All global staff now use it as their day-to-day productivity tool But this is the line that really stuck with me: “We worked backward. We looked at the best advisors… and codified that process in a set of AI models.” That’s the mindset more firms need: Start with what great advisers already do well - then scale it with AI. At [PlannerPal](https://www.linkedin.com/company/plannerpal?trk=public_post-text), we’re doing the same. Not building AI in a vacuum. Not chasing buzzwords. But creating tools rooted in real adviser workflows - built to reduce admin, not relationships. Because the more complex the client, the more valuable the human. UBS knows that. Their strategy isn’t to replace advisers - it’s to empower them. And it’s working. If you’re using - or even just considering using - AI in wealth management or financial planning, this interview is worth a read It’s a clear reminder: 🔸 Start with the adviser 🔸 Build with real-world workflows 🔸 Empower, don’t replace AI isn’t about less human - it’s about better supported human. The post received several comments agreeing that AI amplifies the human touch in financial advice.

# Top AI Co-Pilots for Wealth Management Teams

* 05 Aug 2026
* 8min

Author Igor Sydorenko | CEO & Co-Founder | Neurons Lab

![Igor Sydorenko | CEO & Co-Founder | Neurons Lab](https://neurons-lab.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/au-9.webp)

Relationship managers at wealth advisory institutions spend up to 70% of their daily schedules compiling market reports, checking client portfolios across systems, and fulfilling regulatory requirements.

This heavy administrative burden limits advisor capacity and leaves private clients waiting for personalized guidance. To solve these operational friction points, firms are adopting specialized digital advisor assistants, ranging from off-the-shelf wealth platforms to custom agentic systems built alongside specialized consultancies like Neurons Lab.

Read more: [How relationship managers can leverage AI co-pilots](https://neurons-lab.com/article/ai-for-relationship-managers/)

## **Comparison of AI Co-Pilots for Wealth Management Teams**

The table below summarizes how the leading wealth management co-pilots compare across deployment models, primary capabilities, and key advisory use cases.

Here’s how the top AI advisor tools for financial professionals compare in key areas of wealth management support.

| Platform | Category | Primary Focus | Key Use Cases Covered |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Neurons Lab | Custom-Built AI Co-Pilot | Client-owned AI operating system architecture & custom agentic workflows | Meeting prep, proposal generation, compliance auditing, portfolio messaging |
| TIFIN.AI | AI-Native Wealth Platform | Coordinated multi-agent workflow operating system | Growth workflows, investment ideas, back/middle-office automation via AXIS |
| Envestnet (Gen BI & Insights AI) | AI-Native Wealth Platform | Natural-language analytics and data visualization | Advisor decision-making, real-time reporting, dashboard analytics |
| InvestCloud | AI-Native Wealth Platform | Privacy-centric onboarding and client meeting automation | Automated due diligence, risk screening, meeting prep |
| additiv (Advisor Copilot) | AI-Native Wealth Platform | Embedded digital wealth orchestration | Real-time Q&A, proposal generation, compliant client conversations |
| RavenPack (via Bigdata.com) | Research & Monitoring Agents | Autonomous market and portfolio surveillance | Real-time news monitoring, watchlist alerts, quant research |
| Microsoft 365 Copilot & Copilot Studio | Enterprise / Horizontal Platform | Extensible enterprise productivity suite | Analyst research integration (Morningstar MCP), document drafting, agent governance |

## **Custom-Built AI Co-Pilots**

Custom-built co-pilots are engineered directly on an institution’s private infrastructure, connecting bespoke business logic with internal databases.

### **Neurons Lab**

Since we are the authors of this guide, we start by introducing our approach to advisor automation.

Neurons Lab designs custom agentic AI systems that run directly on your own cloud infrastructure, databases, and tech stack. This approach gives your firm complete ownership of the underlying software without model lock-in, scaling over time into a dedicated AI operating system.

* Custom agentic AI solutions engineered on client-owned systems of record, databases, and cloud environments, ensuring full code ownership with zero vendor lock-in.
* Modular AI Operating System architecture featuring unified data access, governance controls, and a shared business context layer that enables specialized AI agents to understand your firm’s data, terminology, and operational rules.
* Embedded delivery through Forward Deployed Engineers who capture tacit domain knowledge from top performers and transfer technical capabilities to internal teams.
* Pragmatic enablement programs that help advisory teams adopt existing AI tools safely while driving measurable workflow improvements.

For example, an ASEAN wealth management bank implemented a custom relationship intelligence co-pilot. By integrating market research directly with internal client portfolio data, the bank automated meeting preparation and portfolio analysis. This allowed advisors to expand their client capacity from 250 to 300 accounts per manager while increasing assets under management.

Best for: Mid-market wealth management institutions seeking custom agentic AI integrated directly into their private cloud infrastructure with full ownership.

Custom-built AI co-pilots provide maximum flexibility, but wealth management teams can also evaluate several off-the-shelf and enterprise alternatives as shown below.

## **AI-Native Wealth Platforms**

AI-native wealth platforms offer licensed, off-the-shelf software designed specifically for financial advisory workflows.

### **TIFIN.AI**

TIFIN.AI operates as TIFIN Group’s flagship agentic operating system for wealth management. Rather than acting as a standalone tool, the platform coordinates specialized AI agents across growth, investment, and operational workflows within a single shared context.

AXIS serves as the back and middle-office agent layer within TIFIN.AI. FactSet partnered with TIFIN.AI in June 2026 to expand workflow AI capabilities across its wealth management tools.

Best for: Large wealth and asset management enterprises seeking one multi-agent system.

### **Envestnet (Gen BI and Insights AI)**

Envestnet builds AI tools focused on augmenting advisor decision-making across its wealthtech ecosystem. Its Generative Business Intelligence (Gen BI) and Insights AI products allow advisors to ask natural-language questions to generate real-time reports, dashboards, and investment analytics.

These features function like co-pilots by simplifying complex data interpretation for faster decisions. While Envestnet avoids calling these tools co-pilots, their contextual insights directly support daily advisory workflows.

Best for: Wealth management firms seeking AI-powered data analytics without deploying full-scale digital co-pilots.

### **InvestCloud (Intelligent Screening and Intelligent Meeting)**

InvestCloud is integrating AI across the advisor workflow, particularly in onboarding and meeting preparation. Through products like Intelligent Screening and Intelligent Meeting, they enable wealth managers to automate due diligence, risk screening, and client prep tasks.

These solutions are powered by partnerships with smartKYC and Zocks, allowing for privacy-centric and compliance-aware AI assistance. While InvestCloud’s AI tools do not yet form a full advisory copilot, they provide automation and productivity gains across key client interactions.

Best for: Advisory teams looking to streamline client onboarding, due diligence, and pre-meeting preparation.

### **additiv (Advisor Copilot)**

additiv integrates its Advisor Copilot directly into its digital wealth orchestration platform. This gives advisors instant recall of client context, investment positions, and market perspectives in a compliant environment.

The tool supports real-time Q&A, proposal generation, and client meetings grounded in regulatory standards. Embedding AI into daily advisory routines helps firms deliver consistent client experiences across every touchpoint.

Best for: Wealth institutions seeking a compliance-focused advisory co-pilot embedded within a broader digital wealth orchestration platform.

Read more: [Understanding the cost of AI development for financial institutions](https://neurons-lab.com/article/the-cost-of-ai-for-financial-services/)

## **Research and Monitoring Agents**

Research and monitoring agents focus on market surveillance and data analysis rather than direct client communication.

### **RavenPack (via Bigdata.com)**

Bigdata.com, built by RavenPack, is a market-monitoring and research tool designed for analysts and quants rather than client-facing advisor teams.

Three autonomous agents (Watchlists, Briefs, and Workflows) deliver continuous portfolio and market monitoring, drawing on over 20 years of RavenPack financial data. Launched in April 2025, the platform is used by over 100 institutional clients today.

Best for: Research-focused teams including quant funds, hedge funds, and analysts needing real-time market surveillance rather than a client-facing advisor co-pilot.

## **Enterprise and Horizontal Platforms**

Enterprise horizontal platforms supply broad productivity suites that financial institutions configure for specific wealth workflows.

### **Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio**

Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio allow financial institutions to build custom agents, using templates like Financial Insights for rapid data retrieval across internal portfolios and research.

Morningstar connected its investment research via Model Context Protocol (MCP), letting advisors pull analyst insights directly into Excel and Copilot Chat in minutes.

Microsoft also introduced Agent 365, a governance layer priced at $15 per user monthly, signaling a clear shift toward enterprise agent management.

Choosing the right AI assistant for wealth managers involves balancing regulatory compliance, customization, and workflow compatibility. When evaluating AI co-pilots for your advisory or relationship management teams, consider these core selection factors:

* Workflow integration. Verify whether the system connects directly with your CRM, core banking systems, product catalogs, and [compliance frameworks in banking](https://neurons-lab.com/article/ai-for-compliance-in-banking/).
* Compliance readiness. Confirm that all AI outputs are fully auditable, traceable, and aligned with internal regulatory policies.
* Level of customisation. Determine whether the co-pilot can be trained on your private data, internal terminology, and unique advisory approach.
* Explainability. Check if the tool reveals the exact logic behind each portfolio recommendation to maintain client and advisor trust.
* Productivity impact. Evaluate whether the platform automates entire end-to-end workflows or merely assists with isolated tasks.
* Human collaboration. Ensure the software is designed to augment human advisors rather than replace them, fitting naturally into existing daily routines.
* Build versus buy. Decide whether your firm requires a licensed platform to configure or a custom-built solution engineered around your stack.

## **Frequently Asked Questions About AI Co-Pilots in Wealth Management**

### **1. What Is an AI Co-Pilot in Wealth Management?**

An AI co-pilot in wealth management is an intelligent software assistant designed to support financial advisors and relationship managers. These tools assist with client meeting preparation, market analysis, proposal generation, and compliance workflows. By automating routine administrative tasks, co-pilots augment human expertise and allow advisors to deliver more personalized client service.

### **2. How Do AI Co-Pilots Improve Advisor Productivity?**

AI co-pilots improve productivity by automating time-consuming research, gathering client context from multiple systems, and drafting investment proposals. They supply real-time market insights during client preparation, allowing relationship managers to handle larger account volumes while spending more time on strategic planning.

### **3. Are AI Co-Pilots Compliant With Financial Regulations?**

Leading AI co-pilots are built to satisfy strict financial regulations. Custom co-pilots built for wealth management and platforms like Neurons Lab’s custom copilots and additiv’s Advisor Copilot provide auditable, explainable outputs that maintain an explicit trail of logic. These compliance-ready tools help firms adhere to regulatory standards set by bodies like MiFID II, FINRA, and the FCA.

### **4. Which AI Co-Pilot Is Most Customisable for Wealth Management Firms?**

The most customisable option is a custom-built co-pilot, such as Neurons Lab’s custom builds, which can be engineered around a firm’s specific databases, internal workflows, and advisory style. Among pre-packaged software, additiv’s Advisor Copilot offers high configurability within an established digital wealth platform.

### **5. Is AI Replacing Human Advisors in Wealth Management?**

AI is not replacing human advisors. Instead, it serves as a digital assistant that handles repetitive data processing, documentation, and routine reporting. Human advisors remain essential for building trust, managing complex client emotions, and providing final judgment on financial strategies.

AI in wealth management is the use of machine learning, generative AI, and automation to improve how firms research investments, serve clients, support advisors, run operations, and supervise regulated activity.

In 2026, the important distinction is not whether a firm “uses AI,” but where the system operates, whose decisions it influences, and what controls surround it. This guide separates four commonly blurred categories, documents live deployments, and explains the governance questions that determine whether a use case can move from pilot to production.

The operating model

## What AI in wealth management actually means in 2026

AI in wealth management now spans four distinct operating layers: advisor copilots, client-facing engagement, back-office automation, and research and analytics.

Treating them as one category hides different users, risks, data requirements, and supervisory obligations. Generative AI can appear in every layer; the useful classification is who receives the output, what action could follow, and whether a human remains accountable.

01

Employee-facing

### Advisor copilots

Search approved knowledge, prepare meetings, summarize conversations, draft follow-ups, and update systems.

02

Client-facing

### Client engagement

Answer investor questions and personalize communication, with grounding, suitability, disclosure, logging, and escalation around the output.

03

Process-facing

### Operations automation

Support document processing, onboarding, reporting, reconciliation, and control workflows.

04

Decision-support

### Research and analytics

Retrieve evidence, summarize filings and research, surface portfolio patterns, and support proposals or scenario analysis.

Named deployments

## Real examples of AI in wealth management

Real deployments show wealth firms moving from experimentation to bounded production workflows, with the clearest public examples still concentrated on advisor productivity and controlled information access.

The recurring pattern is a narrow job, controlled data, defined users, and visible accountability. The differentiator is rarely the model alone; it is the surrounding workflow, permissions, supervision, and evidence.

By function

## AI use cases in wealth management

The main use cases are client engagement, research, reporting and operations, compliance, and growth. Each creates value differently—and each fails differently when its controls are weak.

01

### Client engagement and communication

AI can answer routine questions, explain portfolio movements, tailor educational content, and identify intent between reviews. POEMSGPT is a public example of AI embedded in a client trading environment.

**Limitation:** Once a response becomes personalized or could be interpreted as advice, the institution needs clear boundaries, suitability controls, disclosure, logging, and human escalation.

02

### Investment research and proposals

AI can search approved research, summarize filings, compare securities, draft proposal narratives, and surface portfolio concentrations. Morgan Stanley's Assistant demonstrates controlled knowledge retrieval with links to source documents. See the [best investment research platforms](/resources/blog/best-investment-research-platforms).

**Limitation:** Fluent synthesis is not audit-grade reproducibility. Analysts and advisors still need to inspect evidence and own the conclusion.

03

### Reporting and operations

AI can turn meeting notes into tasks, draft reports, classify documents, reconcile data, and prepare CRM updates. Morgan Stanley Debrief and Merrill's Meeting Journey both reduce the work around a client meeting.

**Limitation:** A good summary that cannot update approved systems, preserve consent, or produce a reliable record remains another disconnected tool.

04

### Compliance and supervision

AI can review communications, triage alerts, test controls, and make supervision more risk-based. FINRA specifically points firms toward testing, prompt/output monitoring, retained logs, model-version tracking, and human review.

**Limitation:** Automation can support supervision, but it does not transfer accountability away from the firm.

05

### Prospecting and growth

AI can prioritize leads, detect life-event or engagement signals, prepare prospect briefs, and suggest relevant outreach. UBS describes using proprietary analytics to surface opportunities advisors might otherwise miss. See [digital tools for financial advisors](/resources/blog/digital-tools-financial-advisors-2026).

**Limitation:** Teams need to know why a person was prioritized and avoid sensitive or poor-quality data that could create unfair outcomes.

Regulated deployment

## What regulators expect: deploying AI under supervision

Regulators do not treat AI as an exemption from existing conduct, suitability, supervision, disclosure, or recordkeeping obligations.

Across MAS, ESMA, and FINRA guidance, the common pattern is accountable ownership, risk-based controls, testing, transparency, ongoing monitoring, and a human path for review or escalation.

MAS's FEAT principles emphasize internal accountability, disclosure, review channels, and explanations. ESMA states that MiFID II duties—including acting in the client's best interest and suitability—continue when AI supports investment services. FINRA highlights supervision, testing, prompt/output monitoring, recordkeeping, model tracking, and human review. Read more about [compliant AI for regulated wealth institutions](/compliant-ai-for-regulated-wealth-institutions).

A practical operating model

These controls translate recurring regulatory obligations into an implementable system. They are an operating pattern, not a claim that every regulator uses identical terminology.

01

### Advice classification

Determine whether an output is factual information, contextual explanation, a personal recommendation, or a case that must be handed to a human.

02

### Suitability gating

Do not cross into personalized recommendations without the client information and controls required for suitable advice.

03

### Auditability and reproducibility

Retain the question, response, sources or grounding context, model version, approvals, and subsequent action. A citation is useful; a reproducible record is stronger.

04

### Human escalation

Give clients and employees a clear route to review, correct, appeal, or take over a decision or conversation.

Platforms and approaches

## The AI wealth management landscape

AI tools for wealth management fall into four broad approaches, and there is no single best platform for every institution.

The right category depends on the job: research retrieval, meeting productivity, workflow automation, prospect intelligence, or client engagement. Evaluate data permissions, source traceability, integration, supervision, model governance, and what happens when the system is uncertain—not only demo quality.

### Advisor copilots

TIFIN, Envestnet, additiv, and institution-built systems

Best suited to employee productivity, approved knowledge access, meeting workflows, and decision support.

### Engagement layers

Nextvestment

Designed for governed client conversations and the signals those conversations create for advisors. This guide is published by Nextvestment, so that category emphasis is disclosed.

### Horizontal CRM AI

Salesforce and other enterprise platforms

Adds AI to CRM, service, communications, and workflow where the institution already runs core relationship operations.

### Custom builds

In-house teams and consultancies

Useful when deep control, proprietary data, or differentiated workflows justify greater implementation and governance effort.

Explore [wealth-management solutions](/solutions/wealth-management) or the [Nextvestment platform](/platform).

## Will AI replace wealth managers?

AI is more likely to change the division of labour than remove the advisor.

It can absorb search, summarization, documentation, monitoring, and routine explanations. Human advisors remain accountable for judgment, suitability, trade-offs, trust, and action in complex or high-stakes situations.

The strongest deployments reflect that model. Morgan Stanley, Merrill, and UBS position AI around advisor capacity and client service rather than autonomous replacement. Client-facing AI can extend availability, but uncertainty, advice, and consequential decisions should move to an accountable person.

FAQ

## Questions, answered.

What are examples of AI in wealth management?

Examples include Morgan Stanley's advisor knowledge assistant and meeting Debrief, Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank's AI-Powered Meeting Journey, UBS's STAAT advisor analytics, and Phillip Securities' client-facing POEMSGPT capability. They cover knowledge retrieval, meeting workflows, opportunity detection, and client engagement.

What are the main use cases of AI in wealth management?

The main use cases are client engagement, investment research and proposals, reporting and operations, compliance and supervision, and prospecting and growth. The controls required depend on who receives the output and whether it could influence a regulated decision.

What is the best AI for wealth management?

There is no single best platform. Advisor copilots suit meeting and knowledge workflows; research platforms suit evidence retrieval and analysis; CRM AI suits service operations; engagement layers suit governed client conversations. Compare data permissions, source traceability, integration, supervision, and escalation—not only model quality.

How is generative AI used in wealth management?

Generative AI is used to search and summarize approved knowledge, prepare meetings, draft follow-ups, explain portfolio information, create reports, and support client service. Production systems bound those tasks with permissioned data, review, monitoring, and records.

Is AI in wealth management compliant with regulations like MAS and MiFID II?

AI can be used compliantly, but no technology receives a blanket exemption or approval. Firms remain responsible for applicable suitability, conduct, supervision, disclosure, governance, testing, monitoring, recordkeeping, and human-review obligations under frameworks such as MAS guidance and MiFID II.

Will AI replace wealth management advisors?

AI is more likely to change the division of labour than remove advisors. It can handle search, summarization, documentation, monitoring, and routine explanations; advisors remain accountable for judgment, suitability, trust, and high-stakes decisions.

args.summary: This webpage is a practical guide for regulated wealth institutions on deploying AI in wealth management, published by Nextvestment and updated as of July 2026. It distinguishes four operating layers of AI: advisor copilots (employee-facing), client engagement (client-facing), operations automation (process-facing), and research & analytics (decision-support). The guide documents real, named deployments including Morgan Stanley's AI Assistant and Debrief (adopted by 98% of advisor teams), Merrill's AI-Powered Meeting Journey (2026 full-scale rollout), UBS's STAAT (production use), J.P. Morgan's Spectrum copilot (testing with equity portfolio managers), Bank of Singapore's KYC source-of-wealth tool (reduced report prep from 10 days to 1 hour), and Phillip Securities' POEMSGPT (live since November 2025 with classified/logged responses). The main use cases covered are client engagement, investment research, reporting/operations, compliance/supervision, and prospecting/growth. The guide emphasizes that regulators (MAS, ESMA, FINRA) do not exempt AI from existing conduct, suitability, supervision, disclosure, and recordkeeping obligations. A practical operating model is outlined: advice classification, suitability gating, auditability/reproducibility, and human escalation. The guide concludes that AI is more likely to change the division of labour than replace advisors, with human advisors remaining accountable for judgment, suitability, trust, and high-stakes decisions.

This webpage is the Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central release plan for features planned from April 2025 through September 2025 (2025 release wave 1). It covers new and planned functionality across multiple categories, with delivery timelines noted as subject to change. Features are listed with their public preview and general availability dates.

Key categories and highlights include:

**Application**: Features like Field Service integration, price list editing in Excel, SecretText support, and cost adjustment troubleshooting improvements.

**Copilot and Agents**: AI-powered features including a Sales Order Agent (GA Nov 2025), Payables Agent (GA Nov 2025), Copilot chat for add-on apps, summarization, purchase order line matching, autofill, and test automation tools.

**Country and Regional**: Localization updates for Czechia, Italy, Germany, Australia, and New Zealand, including Peppol PINT A-NZ format, ZUGFeRD format for Germany, and VAT reporting improvements.

**Development**: AL developer productivity enhancements such as JsonObject overloads, YAML read/write, multiline strings, new AL project templates for Copilot, mock HttpClient testing, Power BI embedding, and app symbol context for GitHub Copilot.

**Ecommerce**: Shopify connector updates including B2B data import/export, metafield support, sales channel activation, and troubleshooting improvements.

**Electronic Documents**: New service providers (B2B Router, Logiq, ExFlow, Continia), PEPPOL attachments, two-step e-document processing, and incoming invoice preview capabilities.

**Financial Management**: Subscription billing Power BI reports, Intrastat classification requirements, and purchase amount checks.

**Governance and Administration**: MultiSubnetFailover support, flexible environment updates, IPv6 support, sandbox preview updates, and Copilot Studio integration.

**Reporting and Data Analysis**: Enhanced analytics for inventory, sales, purchasing, projects, finance, manufacturing, and sustainability. PDF post-processing, report layout validation, and related table field additions in analysis mode.

**Service and Platform**: Visible FlowField value calculation optimization.

**Supply Chain Management**: Production order rescheduling, cancellation, reopening, barcode printing, warehouse pick omission, subscription billing features, and project item receipts.

**Sustainability Management**: Default sustainability values, water/waste management, Scope 3 value chain for assembly, transfers, manufacturing, and purchase, carbon equivalent data, and demo data updates.

**User Experiences**: PDF preview, screen estate optimization, FactBox pane width adjustment, and UI enhancements.

  📝 Day 5 of [#30DaysOfAI](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Ffeed%2Fhashtag%2F30daysofai&trk=public_post-text): "LinkedIn Post Generator" - Building a Dual-Output AI Content Engine Diving into [Chanin Nantasenamat](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chanin-nantasenamat?trk=public_post-text)'s [#30DaysOfAI](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Ffeed%2Fhashtag%2F30daysofai&trk=public_post-text) Day 5 challenge, I've built a powerful LinkedIn Post Generator that does more than just create posts—it demonstrates intelligent content repurposing at scale. What the App Does: ✅ Takes a content URL, desired tone, and word count ✅ Generates a professional LinkedIn post using Snowflake Cortex COMPLETE (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) ✅ Automatically creates a concise summary using Cortex COMPLETE (Mistral-Large) ✅ Both outputs are cached with @st.cache\_data for instant retrieval Key Technical Insight: The real power here is the dual-LLM architecture. Different models excel at different tasks: Claude 3.5 Sonnet → Creative, engaging LinkedIn content (why it matters, calls to action) Mistral-Large → Concise, factual summarization (essence of the topic) The Challenge I Solved: Day 5's base tutorial generates posts. I added AI-powered summarization automatically, so users get: A polished LinkedIn post for immediate sharing A content summary for documentation/knowledge base This mirrors real-world content workflows where one source becomes multiple deliverables. Example in Action: From Snowflake's Apache Iceberg documentation, the app generated: A professional post about Iceberg's benefits for data engineers An executive summary for quick briefing Why This Matters: For data professionals managing multiple content channels (LinkedIn, documentation, presentations), this pattern—using different LLM models for specialized tasks—reduces manual effort while maintaining quality. Technical Stack: Streamlit for UI (@st.cache\_data for caching) Snowflake Cortex AI for both generation & summarization Snowpark functions API for seamless integration Thanks for the learning opportunity, [Chanin Nantasenamat](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chanin-nantasenamat?trk=public_post-text)! Sena Kwon/Arizent

The extent to which independent financial advisors are using artificial intelligence is only starting to catch up to the "great headlines" about wealth management firms tapping AI, according to Ritik Malhotra, founder and CEO of [Savvy Wealth](https://www.savvywealth.com/about).

For many advisors, the "actual utilization is low," beyond what has turned into "table stakes now" with tools designed to take notes, transcribe and summarize client meetings, said Malhotra, whose firm provides services such as AI-powered software to registered investment advisory firms. The necessary mindset shift in the industry revolves around understanding how the technology could dramatically reduce the amount of time advisors have to spend on the more menial tasks that take them away from clients, he said. And it's easier for advisors and clients to adopt AI than it may appear.

"We're not asking them to suddenly change and send clients this highly complex digital workflow," Malhotra said. "It still fits into how they're operating today."

As part of Financial Planning's [annual IBD Elite study](https://www.financial-planning.com/news/ibd-elite-2025-the-race-for-ai-at-independent-wealth-firms) of the [independent brokerage channel](https://www.financial-planning.com/data/ibd-elite-2025-deep-dive-into-independent-wealth-manager-data) of wealth management, FP spoke with LPL Financial, Cambridge Investment Research, Osaic, Independent Financial Group, Commonwealth Financial Network, Raymond James Financial Services, Ameriprise and Cetera Financial Group about the firms' AI tools and investments. The slideshow below highlights a sampling of the eight firms' responses.

The firms are racing to create AI tools and deploy them for advisors and their teams and for solutions at the corporate level. Six years after the launch of [CogniCor Technologies](https://www.cognicor.com/about), which developed an AI Copilot for advisors, investors and wealth management firms, the company has witnessed many more broker-dealers and RIA firms trying to leverage AI, according to CEO Sindhu Joseph. AI's scaling ability allows companies to work with more clients.

"We are seeing that increased adoption from the RIA world, that there's appetite for these kinds of tools," Joseph said. "That's been my personal mission as well, in terms of democratizing the access to wealth by reaching more households."

Enterprise agreements with firms such as LPL Financial, Cetera Financial Group, Osaic, Cambridge Investment Research, Sanctuary Wealth, Savant Wealth Management, Merit Financial Advisors and Integrated Partners highlight the reach of [Jump](https://jumpapp.com/company), which has developed meeting assistants and other AI tools.

The protection of advisor and client data has "been a really important aspect for all of these large firms," said Parker Ence, the company's CEO. That remains a concern, but it's "a pretty easy fix" for AI developers who can create tools that effectively provide the solution while forgetting the underlying personal client data for purposes of future outputs, he said.

"What we've seen is that AI has gone from, 'Does it work?' to a novelty, like 'Oh, there are some interesting parlor-trick things you could do.' Then it was scary," he said. "Then suddenly it became very practical, and now I think firms are looking at this like, 'We have to have this in our tech stack, or else we are falling behind.'"

With integrations across every possible customer relationship management software and enterprise agreements at firms like Osaic and Cambridge Investment Research, the AI assistants developed by Zocks enable advisors to "offer more services and just expand what they're doing with the clients," said Mark Gilbert, [the firm's](https://www.zocks.io/about-us) CEO and co-founder.

For clients at any tier of a firm's segmentation, advisors can follow up after a meeting or phone conversation with the key takeaways and tasks for the customers, at a cost of $800 per year for a basic account or $1,300 for teams of independent advisors, Gilbert noted.

"They're able to actually stack those up and frankly get back to that client often before they're in the car in the parking lot," he said. "They start to see value in the first day or week, as soon as they start meeting with clients."

Executives with independent wealth management firms are "thinking about how they can use it," because they "know its important to their advisors and to investors," said Andrew Altfest, president of New York-based RIA firm [Altfest Personal Wealth Management](https://www.altfest.com/about/) and co-founder of AI-powered estate, tax and insurance software firm [FP Alpha](https://fpalpha.com/about/).

However, more firms must prepare the tools to set up for "a future in which it's going to be an advisor who's working directly with clients, spending more time with clients" by guiding them on key planning strategies that go far beyond the starting point of AI with note-taking, Altfest said.

"We're at the infancy," Altfest said. "We're just scratching the surface at the entry level."

To read the main feature of this year's IBD Elite study of the largest independent brokerages in the industry, "How independent advisors win the AI adoption race,"* [*click here*](https://www.financial-planning.com/news/ibd-elite-2025-the-race-for-ai-at-independent-wealth-firms)*. ## Cetera Financial Group
