# Best AI Tool for Personal Finance: ChatGPT, Copilot, Gemini, and Claude Compared

[Mark Scribner](/advisor/mark-scribner)

12/26/2025

8 minutes

### Share:

[Opens in a new window](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.wealthenhancement.com/blog/best-ai-assistants-for-personal-finance&title=Best%20AI%20Tool%20for%20Personal%20Finance%3A%20ChatGPT%2C%20Copilot%2C%20Gemini%2C%20and%20Claude%20Compared "Share to Facebook")   [Opens in a new window](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Best%20AI%20Tool%20for%20Personal%20Finance%3A%20ChatGPT%2C%20Copilot%2C%20Gemini%2C%20and%20Claude%20Compared+https://www.wealthenhancement.com/blog/best-ai-assistants-for-personal-finance "Share to X")    [Opens in a new window](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https://www.wealthenhancement.com/blog/best-ai-assistants-for-personal-finance "Share to LinkedIn") 

Copied to clipboard

![](/sites/default/files/styles/2x1_half/public/2025-06/strategic-fin-planning-gi2122148349-blog.jpg.webp?itok=Yfk1EIVb)

*Updated: 2/19/2026*

AI (short for artificial intelligence) has become an everyday tool for managing money. It can do everything from explain basic financial concepts to offer personalized help with your budget and savings plan to help you prepare for meetings with your financial advisor.

Not all AI assistants are the same, and each platform has its own [strengths, weaknesses](https://www.wealthenhancement.com/blog/pros-and-cons-using-ai-manage-your-finances), and ideal use cases. If you’re comparing ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and Claude and trying to decide which is better for managing your personal finances, keep reading to see our thoughts.

## TL;DR

* ChatGPT is best for learning about personal finances, including breaking down complex financial concepts and adapting to many different types of prompts.
* Gemini is best for Google Workspace users thanks to its easy integration with Gmail, Google Drive, Docs, and Sheets.
* Copilot is best for Windows and Microsoft 365 users who want an AI assistant they can use in their Outlook inboxes, as well as Word and Excel.
* Claude is best for reading and summarizing long PDFs, which can be helpful when you’re reviewing documents from your financial advisor.
* Be mindful of the privacy settings for AI chats, especially when dealing with financial information
* Results will vary between AI tools. Test a couple of tasks to find one that works best for your situation.

AI assistants can help you learn about personal finances and organize your documents, but they aren’t a suitable replacement for [working with a fiduciary advisor](https://www.wealthenhancement.com/comprehensive-wealth-management/financial-planning). It’s best to bring in a professional when it comes to things like taxes, investing, retirement planning, and big financial decisions.

For more personalized help with your personal finances, [schedule a free consultation](https://www.wealthenhancement.com/request-a-meeting) with an advisor today.

## Quick Definitions

Before we delve into our conversation regarding AI for personal finance, let’s outline a few definitions:

**AI Assistant:** A chat-based tool that interprets your query (prompt) and generates a response. Example responses can include text, tables, images, or summaries.

**Hallucination:** An AI-generated response that sounds confident but is inaccurate or unsubstantiated.

**Fiduciary advisor**: An advisor who is legally obligated to put your interests first.

## What AI Assistants Can and Can’t Do for Your Money

ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and Claude are among the most popular AI assistants on the market. Each one brings different strengths to [managing your personal finances](https://www.wealthenhancement.com/blog/ai-prompts-help-you-manage-your-household-finances).

Each of these AI tools has some similarities. They rely on technologies like natural language processing, machine learning, and data analysis to understand and process your inputs, perform tasks, and learn from your interactions to improve their performance over time.

### Typical strengths for consumers

AI assistants are excellent tools to help with learning and analysis. First, they can be an effective way to help you learn the basics of personal finances, from how a 401(k) works to different budgeting methods available.

AI is also well-suited to analyzing and summarizing information. For example, you could use an AI assistant to analyze and explain your spending trends, your retirement plan options, your workplace’s vesting schedule, and more.

Another way to use AI is to turn PDFs into plain language summaries. Did you receive a lengthy financial document from your workplace’s HR or your financial advisor, and you’re having a hard time getting through it and understanding it? An AI assistant could be useful for that task.

Finally, AI assistants are best used in conjunction with a real financial planner. They can help you prepare for your meetings, draft questions you should ask, review information from your advisor, and create a schedule to tackle all of the tasks your advisor has recommended.

### Real limits you need to know

While AI assistants have some clear benefits for your personal finances, they also have some major limitations and risks.

First, as we mentioned, AI isn’t 100% accurate. Most people who regularly use AI have likely had the experience of being provided with blatantly false information. Even if you’re only using it for learning, it could provide inaccurate information, which could lead you to make mistakes with your personal finances.

Next, there are some privacy risks when it comes to using AI, especially if you’re plugging in sensitive information. Each AI assistant has different privacy policies, and there’s no way to know your data is completely safe and isn’t being used to train the AI system. You should never enter sensitive information like your bank account numbers or Social Security number into an AI tool.

Finally, AI isn’t really appropriate for personalized advice. No AI assistant has a [fiduciary duty](https://www.wealthenhancement.com/blog/what-is-a-fiduciary) to you in the same way many financial planners do. Not only that, but they aren’t capable of the same critical thinking and human touch that real advisors are. They also aren’t capable of nuance like an advisor is, meaning they may not be able to adapt their recommendations based on your unique situation or goals.

Using AI as your sole source of financial information and advice could put you in a poor financial position that is difficult to come back from.

## Best AI Assistants for Personal Finance – Quick Comparison

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assistant | Best for | Standout strengths | Common limits | Privacy controls | Works with |
| ChatGPT | Learning concepts and brainstorming | Plain-English answers, broad plugin ecosystem | Hallucinations on niche finance | Chat history controls; custom instructions | Web, iOS, Android |
| Gemini | Google Workspace users | Gmail/Drive/Docs/Sheets integration | Workspace dependence for best results | Data controls in account settings | Chrome, Android, Workspace |
| Copilot | Microsoft 365 and Windows users | Outlook/Word/Excel integration | Best inside Microsoft apps | Commercial data protections; user settings | Windows, Edge, M365 |
| Claude | Long PDFs and careful summaries for research heavy users | Long-context reading, concise summaries | Limited ecosystem integrations and can be confidently wrong with citations and figures | Privacy settings in account | Web |

## Deep Dives: Strengths, Gaps, Best Fit

### ChatGPT

[ChatGPT](https://www.chatgpt.com) is ideal for explaining and breaking down both basic and complex financial topics. It can also answer financial questions in clear, conversational language. ChatGPT can understand a wide range of different prompt types. It can also remember your conversations, which allows it to retain context and understand your unique needs and use cases. Many people use it as their primary AI assistant because of how easy it is to use, how it remembers things about you, and its versatility.

### Gemini

[Gemini](https://gemini.google/us/about), Google’s AI assistant, integrates well with the company’s other products. It’s good at summarizing emails, reading, analyzing, and interpreting files in your Google Drive, and assisting with budgeting and planning tasks in your Google Sheets. If you want a platform that can review and understand files, and you’re often working in the Google ecosystem, this is a great option for you.

### Microsoft Copilot

[Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/for-individuals/) is Microsoft’s AI assistant. Similar to Gemini’s integrations with other Google products, Copilot integrates well with other Microsoft products, including Outlook, Word, and Excel. It can help you summarize, analyze and draft emails, quickly process documents, and analyze or refine spreadsheets.

### Claude

[Claude](https://claude.com/product/overview) is best at reading, understanding, and summarizing long documents. Its long memory helps it approach long PDFs, including plan descriptions, disclosures, financial statements, and more. It’s also well-suited to writing, meaning it can help you draft correspondence with your financial planner. Finally, its careful reasoning makes it a good option for research-heavy tasks.

## Practical Money Tasks You Can Try Today

AI assistants can help you with a variety of both simple and complex financial tasks and concepts. While it’s not the best option for personalized financial advice, here are some tasks it is well-suited to.

### Budget Audit from a Bank CSV

You can upload your bank account activity from a spreadsheet into an AI assistant and have it review and analyze your recent spending. It could show you where you’re spending most of your money, recurring expenses, and where you may be able to cut back.

Just make sure that before you upload any documents or spreadsheets, you’ve removed your account numbers and other sensitive personal data.

### Explain Your 401(k) Match and Vesting

401(k) plan documents can be difficult to navigate, but an AI assistant can help. You can upload your plan documents into an AI assistant and ask it to analyze and summarize the information, including how employer contributions work, your vesting schedule, and other benefits information. Finally, it can break down your investment options. While you shouldn’t rely on AI to choose your investments, it could help you understand your options better.

### Debt Management

Consider using an AI assistant to help you pay off your debt. You can upload a spreadsheet of all of your debts, including each one’s balance, interest rate, monthly payment, and payment term. From there, AI can help you create a debt repayment schedule that helps you pay off your debt faster and pay the least amount of interest. You can ask it to show you your potential savings across different methods, such as the debt snowball versus the debt avalanche.

### Prep For An Advisor Meeting

While AI isn’t a suitable replacement for a financial advisor, it can make your time with your advisor more efficient and productive. You can use an AI assistant to organize your financial documents, draft questions to ask your planner, and summarize your goals and next steps after your meeting with your advisor.

## Personal Finance Prompt Examples

* “Summarize this 401(k) plan PDF and list 5 action items I can discuss with my advisor. Keep bullets under 12 words.”
* “From this cleaned bank CSV, group expenses, flag subscriptions, and show a simple monthly budget.”
* “Explain Roth vs Traditional contributions in plain English for a W-2 employee in a 24 percent tax bracket. Add a pros and cons list.”
* “Turn these meeting notes into 3 follow-up questions to ask my advisor about retirement timelines.”
* “Redraft this email to HR asking for plan fee disclosures, keep it polite and short.”

## Safety and Privacy Checklist

Before you start using an AI assistant to manage your personal finances, there are some basic safety precautions you should understand.

### Ground rules before you paste anything

Before sharing financial information with any AI tool, it’s important to follow best practices for privacy and security. Avoid sharing sensitive information, including account numbers, Social Security numbers, or full financial statements.

Before using any AI assistant, make sure to turn on account security and review their privacy policies and data controls so you know what information is and isn’t being stored. And here’s a pro tip, you can use AI to summarize the privacy policies and terms of service of the AI platforms.

### Safety First Rules

#### What not to share with any AI tool (and what’s usually okay)

**Never Share:**

* Social Security Number (SSN)
* Driver License or State ID Number
* Address
* Birthday
* Account numbers (Banks, Investments, Credit Cards, etc.)
* Passwords
* Full, unredacted account statements or other financial documents
* Images of IDs, Social Security Card, etc.

**Usually OK (after redaction):**

* Category totals
* Anonymized transactions
* Plan excerpts with names removed

[Investopedia notes](https://www.investopedia.com/financial-data-privacy-chatgpt-11717128) users risk exposing sensitive financial data in AI conversations, so it’s important to take precautions when using these tools. In addition, the U.S. Department of the Treasury weighed in on the [risks of AI in Financial Services](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/jy2760).

#### How to Reduce Training Use

##### ChatGPT

Data sharing is enabled by default on [ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8983130-what-if-i-want-to-keep-my-history-on-but-disable-model-training), however you can opt-out of using the data for training by following these steps:

* Navigate to You Profile > Settings > Data Controls > Improve the Model for Everyone
* Toggle off

##### CoPilot

[According to Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/microsoft-365/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy), “prompts, responses, and data accessed through Microsoft Graph aren’t used to train foundation LLMs.”

##### Claude

* Navigate to Settings > Privacy
* Toggle Off “Help Improve Claude”

##### Gemini

Google provides some documentation in their support community for [disabling Gemini](https://support.google.com/gemini/thread/342177585?hl=en&sjid=1067973766706675939-NC).

* Go to <https://myactivity.google.com/product/gemini>
* Login if prompted
* Toggle the “On” to “Turn Off” or “Turn Off and Delete Activity”

Here are some additional resources you can turn to for guidance:

* FTC AI Reports and Press: <https://www.ftc.gov/industry/technology/artificial-intelligence>
* NIST AI Risk Management Framework: <https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework>
* FBI Internet Crime Report 2024: <https://www.ic3.gov/AnnualReport/Reports/2024_IC3Report.pdf>
* SEC Conflicts of Interest and Predictive Data Fact Sheet: <https://www.sec.gov/files/34-97990-fact-sheet.pdf>

### Spotting AI-enabled scams

AI is increasingly being used across all industries, including fraud. It can be used to create deepfake videos, voice cloning, and phishing scams that are difficult to detect and easy to fall for. It’s important to understand how to recognize and [protect yourself from these cyber-attacks](https://www.wealthenhancement.com/blog/how-to-protect-yourself-from-cyberattacks) and to immediately report anything suspicious.

## How To Pair AI With A Fiduciary Advisor

As we mentioned, AI can do a lot to help you with your personal finances, but it’s no replacement for a financial advisor. Let’s talk about how to pair your AI assistant with an advisor.

### Where AI helps, where an advisor is essential

As we mentioned, Ai can be helpful for learning about personal finances, summarizing long documents, and analyzing data. However, it can’t look at your whole financial picture and offer personalized advice the same way a fiduciary advisor can.

When you’re making decisions about retirement contributions and withdrawals, tax strategy, long-term investing, and [estate planning](https://www.wealthenhancement.com/blog/your-complete-guide-to-estate-planning), it’s best to turn to a professional.

### Turn AI output into action with a pro

Once AI helps you learn the basics and frame your questions, turn to a fiduciary advisor to help turn that preparation into an actionable, [comprehensive financial plan](https://www.wealthenhancement.com/comprehensive-wealth-management/financial-planning). A real advisor can provide context that AI can’t, and help to weigh trade-offs and make the best decisions for your situation and goals.

## Turn AI help into a plan

AI assistants are great companions for your day-to-day money tasks, not stand-ins for a fiduciary. Pick the one that fits your world and the job at hand: ChatGPT for learning and plain-English explanations, Gemini for heavy Google Workspace use, Copilot for Microsoft 365, and Claude for long documents. Keep privacy in mind, strip sensitive details before you paste, and treat any output as a starting point.

Quick next steps you can take today:

1. Choose one assistant and turn on account security in its settings.
2. Test two tasks: summarize a 401(k) plan PDF and run a simple budget review from a cleaned bank CSV.
3. Capture your questions and bring them to a planning conversation.

When you want real guidance that accounts for taxes, investments, retirement, and trade-offs, talk with a fiduciary advisor. We can turn your AI prep into a clear plan that matches your goals. [Schedule a free consultation](https://www.wealthenhancement.com/request-a-meeting) to get started.

## FAQs

### Can I rely on AI for financial advice?

While AI can be helpful for enhancing your financial literacy and performing basic analysis and automation tasks, you shouldn’t turn to it for personalized financial advice. Instead, combine the power of AI with the critical thinking, empathy, and years of training of a financial advisor.

### Which assistant fits Microsoft vs Google users better?

Microsoft Copilot is best for regular Microsoft users, as it integrates easily with other Microsoft products, including Outlook, Word, and Excel. Gemini, on the other hand, is best for Google users who want an AI assistant to seamlessly integrate with their other products.

### Is my chat data used for training?

AI assistants are constantly learning, partially through past conversations with users. When you use AI, your chats could be used for training the assistant to get better. Depending on your AI assistant, you may be able to turn off this feature so that your chats are more private.

### How do I keep chats private?

First, make sure your account is secure with a strong password and multifactor authentication. Most AI assistants also allow you to turn on enhanced privacy, but you’ll have to go into your settings to do this.

### What about summarizing long PDFs like plan documents?

AI assistants are particularly well-suited to summarizing long PDFs, including plan documents. Claude is especially good at handling large documents and can provide clear, concise summaries.

### Are there other AI tools that can help manage my personal finances?

There are thousands of AI tools available, some more specialized than others. You can discover these tools through simple online searches, online groups, or by asking AI.

This article from Wealth Enhancement Group compares four major AI assistants for personal finance management: ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, and Claude. It was written by Mark Scribner, Senior Vice President and Financial Advisor, and updated on 2/19/2026.

**Key Findings:**

- **ChatGPT** is best for learning financial concepts, breaking down complex topics, and plain-English explanations with broad plugin ecosystem support.
- **Gemini** is best for Google Workspace users due to integration with Gmail, Drive, Docs, and Sheets.
- **Copilot** is best for Microsoft 365 and Windows users, integrating with Outlook, Word, and Excel.
- **Claude** is best for reading and summarizing long PDFs, making it useful for reviewing financial documents.

**What AI Can and Cannot Do:**
- Strengths: Learning personal finance basics, analyzing spending trends, summarizing documents, preparing for advisor meetings
- Limitations: Not 100% accurate (hallucinations), privacy risks, no fiduciary duty, cannot provide personalized advice

**Practical Tasks for AI:**
- Budget audit from bank CSV files
- Explain 401(k) match and vesting schedules
- Create debt management plans (e.g., debt snowball vs. avalanche)
- Prepare for advisor meetings

**Privacy & Safety Rules:**
- Never share: SSN, driver's license, address, birthday, account numbers, passwords, full financial statements
- Usually OK (after redaction): category totals, anonymized transactions, plan excerpts with names removed
- Instructions provided to disable data training for each AI assistant

The article emphasizes that AI assistants should complement, not replace, a fiduciary financial advisor, especially for taxes, investing, retirement planning, and major financial decisions.

![Image 22: chevron icon](https://www.fidelity.com/plpResources/assets/svgs/icons/faq-accordion-chevron-icon.svg)How does Fidelity Go® work?

With Fidelity Go® you'll start by telling us about yourself and your individual financial goals so we can suggest an investment strategy for your account. Once your account is open, you can add money through either one-time or recurring transfers. Once your account balance reaches $10, we'll start investing for you in accordance with your goal, helping you track your progress along the way. Each year, we'll check in with you to ask if anything major in your life has changed, and if necessary, we'll adjust your investment strategy to fit with your new situation. And remember that this is a relationship. So if your needs change at any time, you can let us know and we can help by making changes consistent with your new goal.

 Additional features:

*   All customers have access to our online planning tools, and once your account balance reaches $25,000, you'll also have access to unlimited 1-on-1 financial coaching sessions with a team of advisors. Whether you need help creating a budget, paying down debt, planning for retirement, or investing for your future, you'll have the comfort of knowing that 1-on-1 advice from Fidelity is just a call away.
*   For taxable accounts with a balance of at least $25,000, we'll look for tax-loss harvesting opportunities in your Flex Funds that hold stocks, which can help you lower your tax bill.

![Image 23: chevron icon](https://www.fidelity.com/plpResources/assets/svgs/icons/faq-accordion-chevron-icon.svg)How much does Fidelity Go® cost?

Fidelity Go® charges no advisory fees while your account balance is under $25,000. Once your balance reaches $25,000, you'll be charged a 0.35% advisory fee per year, which will give you access to financial coaching sessions and, for taxable accounts, tax-loss harvesting. Either way, there are no trading fees, transaction fees, or rebalancing fees.

![Image 24: chevron icon](https://www.fidelity.com/plpResources/assets/svgs/icons/faq-accordion-chevron-icon.svg)What does Fidelity Go® do for me?

Once you provide some information about yourself and your financial goals, we'll handle all day-to-day investing decisions for your Fidelity Go® account, and we'll do the following:

*   Suggest an initial investment strategy, or mix of stocks and bonds in your account, according to information you provide, such as your goal, your time horizon, and your comfort with risk
*   Invest your money according to the investment strategy you've chosen after you fund your account with at least $10
*   Buy and sell investments in your account to maintain the investment strategy you've chosen, often referred to as "rebalancing"
*   Keep you informed about how your investments are doing
*   Remind you each year to review and update the information you've provided
*   Offer financial coaching sessions to you with our trained advisors once your account balance reaches $25,000
*   Look for tax-loss harvesting opportunities in your Flex Funds that hold stocks, once your balance reaches $25,000 (for taxable accounts only)

![Image 25: chevron icon](https://www.fidelity.com/plpResources/assets/svgs/icons/faq-accordion-chevron-icon.svg)What types of Fidelity Go® accounts are available?

The following types of accounts are available through Fidelity Go®:

*   Taxable (individual/joint)
*   Traditional IRA
*   Roth IRA
*   Rollover IRA
*   Simplified Employee Pension Plan (SEP IRA)
*   Health savings account (HSA)

![Image 26: chevron icon](https://www.fidelity.com/plpResources/assets/svgs/icons/faq-accordion-chevron-icon.svg)What's a robo advisor?

A robo advisor is an affordable digital financial service that uses technology to help automate investing based on information investors provide about themselves and their financial situation. "Robo" refers to these services being almost completely digital, and that computers, smartphones, or tablets are used to access and interact with your accounts. "Advisor" speaks to the investment advisors that offer digital advice and account management services, often for a lower fee than traditional investment advisory services.

args.summary:
## Fidelity Go® - Robo Advisor Service

Fidelity Go is a robo-advisor service from Fidelity Investments that provides automated, discretionary investment management. Key features include:

**Pricing:**
- $0 advisory fees for accounts under $25,000
- 0.35% annual advisory fee for accounts $25,000 and above
- No trading, transaction, or rebalancing fees

**How It Works:**
1. Users answer questions about their financial goals, time horizon, and risk tolerance
2. Fidelity proposes a strategy using a mix of mutual funds
3. Once funded with at least $10, Fidelity invests and manages the account
4. The service automatically rebalances and offers "Smart Shift" to adjust strategy over time

**Account Types Available:** Taxable (individual/joint), Traditional IRA, Roth IRA, Rollover IRA, SEP IRA, and Health Savings Account (HSA).

**Premium Features (at $25,000+):**
- Unlimited 1-on-1 financial coaching calls with advisors
- Tax-loss harvesting for taxable accounts

**Recognition:** Fidelity Go was awarded Best Robo Advisor of 2025 by Kiplinger's (survey conducted June-July 2025, awarded August 2025).

**Minimum:** No minimum to open; $10 minimum to start investing.

**Conversion:** Existing Fidelity accounts can be converted to Fidelity Go for free (though selling securities may incur fees or tax consequences).

Advisory services are provided by Strategic Advisers LLC (a registered investment adviser), with brokerage services by Fidelity Brokerage Services LLC.

# Integrity Collaborates with Microsoft to Offer AI-Driven Innovation Across Entire Organization

,PR Newswire- 11:12 AM ET 3/3/2026 default

*   [![Image 2: Facebook.](https://www.fidelity.com/bin-public/060_www_fidelity_com/images/facebook-26.png)](javascript:void(0);)
*   [![Image 3: Twitter.](https://www.fidelity.com/bin-public/060_www_fidelity_com/images/twitter-26.png)](javascript:void(0);)
*   [![Image 4: LinkedIn.](https://www.fidelity.com/bin-public/060_www_fidelity_com/images/linkedin-26.png)](javascript:void(0);)
*   [![Image 5: Print](https://www.fidelity.com/bin-public/060_www_fidelity_com/images/print-26.png)](https://www.fidelity.com/news/article/default/202603031012PR_NEWS_USPR_____LA98644#print)

_Integrity's full workforce receives personal AI Digital Assistant through Microsoft 365 Copilot, adding robust AI-powered capabilities that will enhance productivity, services and speed of work_

DALLAS, March 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Integrity, LLC ("Integrity"), a leading distributor of life and health insurance, and provider of wealth management and retirement planning solutions, today announced a strategic collaboration with Microsoft to empower Integrity's workforce by integrating AI capabilities across core business operations. All Integrity employees will now have access to its intuitive AI Digital Assistant through Microsoft 365 Copilot — designed to help employees be more productive, creative and efficient. The collaboration will streamline processes and automate tasks to unlock an enhanced quality of work, enabling the Integrity team to create and execute stronger solutioning for agents and consumers.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=50XurczWfZM)

"Embedding AI into our workflows is much more than just a technology investment — it's a crucial part of Integrity's commitment to Putting People First," said Bryan W. Adams, Co-Founder and CEO of Integrity. "We were already at the forefront of the industry with our AI-powered digital assistant that helps agents and advisors better serve their clients. Now, we're excited to bring transformative AI technology to our entire workforce. It's a solution that creates a fundamental shift away from routine processes and toward higher, more strategic levels of work with greater focus on decision making and long-term impact. This integration with Microsoft builds on our foundation of ongoing innovation and ignites our next phase of industry transformation."

Integrity has been an industry leader for years with significant investments in AI technology, including the creation of Ask Integrity®,which delivers efficiency gains across Integrity's entire value chain, from strengthening agent support to further developing the proprietary Integrity platform that is transforming the way agents and advisors serve today's consumers. Through this collaboration, all 5,000 Integrity employees will now have a personalized AI Digital Assistant that is fully integrated into the tools they use every day. Adding Copilot's powerful and compliant technology will help employees research, create and learn more efficiently. It offers them assistance with tasks such as creating first drafts of documents and communications, providing meeting and task summaries, and building presentation content. It can also add clarity and precision to specific Integrity projects, streamline tasks and processes, while expanding instant access to relevant information and knowledge.

"Our AI team is setting a new industry standard for innovation, combining deep technical expertise with a relentless focus on real-world impact," said Harsh Singla, Chief Product and Technology Officer of Integrity. "By giving our employees access to their own AI Digital Assistant, we're empowering them to work smarter, move faster and deliver more meaningful results for the people we serve. Providing our team members across the country with this cutting-edge technology unlocks creativity, accelerates problem-solving and transforms how we innovate, collaborate and scale."

This deployment complements Integrity's many other groundbreaking innovations — including Ask Integrity for agents and advisors. As one of the industry's first-of-its kind, AI-powered digital assistants, this technology utilizes personalized insights and key coverage recommendations to help agents and advisors more proactively serve clients. Providing the powerful capabilities of Copilot across its enterprise will become a vital part of Integrity's proprietary all-in-one technology platform that will continue to transform business growth through more holistic solutions. Every advancement at Integrity is thoughtfully designed to optimize workflows so more Americans can access the life, health and wealth protection and planning they need.

"Through Ask Integrity, we've already seen the real value that generative AI brings to agents and advisors by increasing productivity and deepening customer relationships," said Said Taiym, COO of Integrity. "Bringing the AI capabilities of Microsoft 365 Copilot to our team will enable employees across all levels of our organization to experience similar strides in efficiency and impact. We are committed to being a category-defining leader that actively shapes the future of AI in our industry. By taking a deliberate approach to responsibly embed AI into our workflows, our teams can do the best work they're capable of — with expanded bandwidth to create more innovative solutions that will benefit millions of Americans."

"Integrity is a trusted partner to its agents and advisors and a champion of consumer wellbeing," said Jim DeMarco, Head of Insurance Industry Advisory, Microsoft. "Integrating Microsoft 365 Copilot into Integrity's highly advanced technology platform of products and services means employees can work more strategically, creatively and decisively to create outcomes that are stronger and simpler. We're excited to enable Integrity with real–time insight, data and intelligence that enriches the meaningful, human interactions their teams deliver to customers and clients every day."

To learn more about Integrity's transformative technology platform, please visit www.integrity.com.

**About Integrity**Integrity, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, is a leading distributor of life and health insurance, and provider of innovative solutions for wealth management and retirement planning. Through its broad partner network of agents and advisors, Integrity helps millions of Americans protect their life, health and wealth with a commitment to meet them wherever they are — in person, over the phone and online. Integrity's proprietary, cutting-edge technology helps expand the insurance and financial planning experience for all stakeholders using an omnichannel approach. In addition, Integrity develops products with carrier partners and markets them compliantly through its nationwide distribution network. Providing best-in-class service to their clients and consumers is at the center of Integrity's holistic approach to life, health and wealth protection. The company and its partners focus on helping families and individuals prepare for the good days ahead, so they can make the most of what life brings. The recipient of nationally ranked business awards, including Newsweek's America's Greatest Workplaces, Inc.'s Power Partner, and Business Intelligence Group's AI Excellence Award, Integrity has also earned impressive employee sentiment awards such as Best Company for Career Growth, Best Company Leadership, Best Company Culture, and Best Company Happiness. For more information, visit www.integrity.com.

# AI Financial Advisor Comparison: PortfolioPilot vs Vanguard Digital Advisor (2025)

By

Alexander Harmsen

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/639a2cc97bf1c270bf6d6d95/66d20af5d5a014a7a4d4a7d8_alex-profile-img.png)

Alexander Harmsen is the Co-founder and CEO of PortfolioPilot. With a track record of building AI-driven products that have scaled globally, he brings deep expertise in finance, technology, and strategy to create content that is both data-driven and actionable.

Reviewed by

PortfolioPilot Compliance Team

The PortfolioPilot Compliance Team reviews all content for factual accuracy and adherence to SEC marketing rules, ensuring every piece meets the highest standards of transparency and compliance.

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/6486a80c48d5ac597d110aff/69c5c804a12ffdd8bc0d843e_6914d0bfe3ca195d1f6e6f46_ChatGPT%2520Image%2520Nov%252012%252C%25202025%252C%252003_23_46%2520PM.webp)

Many people still conflate “[AI financial advisor](https://portfoliopilot.com/ai-financial-advisor)” with “[robo-advisor](https://portfoliopilot.com/ai-financial-advisor/resources/portfoliopilot-vs-robo-advisors-understanding-automated-investment-approaches).” The reality is that PortfolioPilot and Vanguard Digital Advisor represent two distinct models: one offers fully managed automation inside a single custodian, the other provides cross-platform recommendations without taking control. This article compares the two approaches, showing how differences in execution, custody, and tax handling can significantly shape the investor experience.

## Key Takeaways

* **Vanguard Digital Advisor**: a discretionary robo that automatically trades and rebalances portfolios at Vanguard.
* **PortfolioPilot**: a non-discretionary AI platform that analyzes all accounts and provides ongoing recommendations while leaving execution to the user.
* Fees are structured differently: Vanguard charges an annual percentage of assets (~0.20% for index-based portfolios), while PortfolioPilot uses a flat monthly subscription with no AUM fee ($29/month or $20/month billed annually).
* Vanguard emphasizes **automation within Vanguard funds**; PortfolioPilot emphasizes **breadth and flexibility across custodians and asset types**.
* The core trade-off is between **hands-off automation** and **cross-platform analysis with investor control**. Descriptions are based on publicly available disclosures and are provided for general informational purposes only.

## Vanguard Digital Advisor: Automated Robo Inside a Single Custodian

[Vanguard Digital Advisor](https://investor.vanguard.com/advice/robo-advisor) is built around automation. Once a client enrolls in a Vanguard account, the platform:

* Allocates investments into Vanguard ETFs or mutual funds.
* Monitors accounts daily and rebalances automatically.
* Provides optional tax-loss harvesting for taxable accounts.
* Restricts client-initiated trades to maintain consistency with the plan.

The fee is approximately **0.20% annually for index portfolios** (0.25% for a mix with active funds), plus underlying fund expenses. With a minimum now set at **$100**, Vanguard Digital Advisor opens the door to smaller accounts that previously might not have met robo minimums.

The clear appeal is convenience: for investors who want to “set it and forget it,” the robo handles transactions without requiring ongoing input. The trade-off is less flexibility and a portfolio tied to one custodian and fund family.

## PortfolioPilot: Cross-Platform AI Guidance Without Execution

[PortfolioPilot](https://portfoliopilot.com/), developed by Global Predictions Inc., takes another stance. It is [**hybrid-AI**](https://portfoliopilot.com/ai-financial-advisor/resources/what-hybrid-AI-investing-looks-like-with-portfoliopilot) **advice software** rather than a robo-manager. Users connect multiple accounts - [brokerage](https://portfoliopilot.com/faqs/how-can-i-sync-my-portfolio-in-my-brokerage-with-portfoliopilot), [retirement](https://portfoliopilot.com/retirement-planning), [real estate](https://portfoliopilot.com/faqs/can-i-integrate-real-estate-investments-into-my-portfoliopilot-assessment), [crypto](https://portfoliopilot.com/faqs/is-portfoliopilot-a-crypto-portfolio-tracker), and more - and the system provides:

* [Personalized monthly recommendations](https://portfoliopilot.com/tutorials/tutorial-personalized-recommendations).
* [Tax](https://portfoliopilot.com/tax-optimization) impact and fee analysis across all accounts.
* Scenario modeling for [retirement](https://portfoliopilot.com/tutorials/tutorial-retirement-planning) and [estate planning](https://portfoliopilot.com/estate-planning).
* Diversification scoring across more than 30 asset classes.

[Pricing](https://portfoliopilot.com/pricing) is a **flat subscription** ($29/month or $20/month billed annually), with no asset-based fees. Core tracking and analysis features are available at no cost, while premium tiers unlock tax optimization and personalized planning tools.

PortfolioPilot’s core value lies in **personalization, breadth, and control**. It doesn’t take custody or execute trades, meaning the investor remains fully in charge of implementation. This can be appealing to self-directed investors who want advanced analysis without ceding authority.

Insights generated by the platform are informational and require the investor to determine whether and how to act.

> [**Get recommendations across fees, taxes, risk, returns, and downside factors.**](https://portfoliopilot.com/ai-financial-advisor)

## Why the Difference Matters

***Hypothetical:*** *Imagine a 40-year-old investor with a 401(k) at Vanguard, a taxable brokerage at Fidelity, and some real estate. Enrolling only the Vanguard account in Digital Advisor means the robo will manage that slice - but not touch the other holdings. PortfolioPilot, by contrast, can show how the Fidelity account, the 401(k), and the real estate interact, highlighting tax or diversification gaps, though the investor must execute changes manually.*

**So what?** The choice isn’t only about cost - it’s about **scope and control**. Vanguard Digital Advisor may appeal to those who want a single account managed automatically. PortfolioPilot may resonate with investors who want **a holistic view** and are comfortable making the final call on trades.

## Vanguard Digital Advisor vs PortfolioPilot — Fees, Access & Features

  What is the minimum investment required for Vanguard Digital Advisor in 2025? ▼ 

Vanguard Digital Advisor requires at least $100 to enroll, a threshold that enables access for smaller accounts compared with past robo minimums.

   How does Vanguard Digital Advisor calculate its annual fee for index-based portfolios? ▼ 

Vanguard charges roughly 0.20% of assets annually for index-focused portfolios, in addition to underlying fund expenses.

   Does Vanguard Digital Advisor allow investors to trade freely once enrolled? ▼ 

No. Client-initiated trades are restricted to keep portfolios consistent with the automated plan.

   What extra cost applies if an investor chooses active funds inside Vanguard Digital Advisor? ▼ 

Fees increase to about 0.25% annually for portfolios blending active funds with index strategies, plus underlying fund expenses.

   How does PortfolioPilot charge compared to Vanguard’s asset-based fees? ▼ 

PortfolioPilot uses flat pricing of $29 per month or $20 per month when billed annually, with no percentage-of-assets charge.

   Does PortfolioPilot take custody of client assets or execute trades? ▼ 

No. PortfolioPilot provides analysis and recommendations but leaves all execution and custody with the investor.

   What types of accounts and assets can PortfolioPilot analyze in one dashboard? ▼ 

PortfolioPilot can connect brokerage, retirement, crypto, and real estate holdings, assessing diversification and tax impacts across more than 30 asset classes.

   How frequently does PortfolioPilot deliver personalized recommendations? ▼ 

Subscribers receive monthly recommendations, along with tax impact and fee analysis across all connected accounts.

   Does Vanguard Digital Advisor offer tax-loss harvesting for taxable accounts? ▼ 

Yes. Vanguard includes optional tax-loss harvesting for taxable portfolios as part of its automated service.

   What’s the main trade-off between Vanguard Digital Advisor and PortfolioPilot? ▼ 

Vanguard emphasizes automated execution within its custodian, while PortfolioPilot emphasizes cross-platform analysis and investor control over trades.

args.summary: This article compares PortfolioPilot and Vanguard Digital Advisor as two distinct models of AI-driven investment advice. Vanguard Digital Advisor is a discretionary robo-advisor that automatically trades and rebalances portfolios within Vanguard, charging ~0.20% annually for index portfolios (minimum $100). PortfolioPilot is a non-discretionary AI platform that analyzes all connected accounts (brokerage, retirement, real estate, crypto) across custodians and provides ongoing recommendations, charging a flat subscription ($29/month or $20/month billed annually) with no AUM fee. The core trade-off: Vanguard offers hands-off automation within a single custodian, while PortfolioPilot offers cross-platform analysis and breadth with investor control over execution. PortfolioPilot provides personalized monthly recommendations, tax impact analysis, fee analysis, scenario modeling, and diversification scoring across 30+ asset classes. Vanguard Digital Advisor offers optional tax-loss harvesting but restricts client-initiated trades. The article uses a hypothetical scenario of a 40-year-old investor with accounts at Vanguard, Fidelity, and real estate to illustrate how PortfolioPilot can provide a holistic view while Vanguard only manages its slice.

You are tasked with summarizing the raw content of a webpage retrieved from a web search. Your goal is to create a summary that preserves the most important information from the original web page. This summary will be used by a downstream research agent, so it's crucial to maintain the key details without losing essential information.

Here is the raw content of the webpage:

<webpage_content>
![Morningstar](/assets/img/morningstar.d826858.svg)

## Table of Contents

# The Best Robo-Advisors of 2025

Understand the ins and outs of digital advice and see our top picks.

![](https://media.morningstar.com/resizer/v2/https%3A%2F%2Fauthor-service-images-prod-us-east-1.publishing.aws.arc.pub%2Fmorningstar%2Fb41a1177-9e6e-486c-bb45-434ac569d47e.jpg?auth=519266dde5ce2cbabd670c7c303dc0bb462b5634197d30b794b2364de15f629a&quality=80&height=2000&width=2000&smart=true)
![Collage illustration featuring a deconstructed pie chart, with images of an investor viewing a computer, a portfolio, and an avatar.](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/S6VE2P5YFVH3JIUZJ6FCZQDSV4.png)

The robo-advisor revolution never really arrived.

Instead of supplanting traditional planners as some people predicted, independent digital advice providers have struggled to meet those early, heady expectations. Meanwhile, some established firms they had sought to upend have co-opted robo-advisors’ methods and seized the market.

Although robo-advisors have grown in the two decades they’ve existed, they still compose a sliver of the asset-management industry. In 2024, robo-advisor assets were between $634 billion and $754 billion, according to [Cerulli Associates](https://www.condorcapital.com/the-robo-report/data/aum-statistics/) and other sources. That’s a fraction of the $36.8 trillion US retail market, which Cerulli defines as investors with assets of $100,000 to $5 million.

That’s not to say these would-be disrupters have not had any disruptive influence, however. Digital advice has become another way for established firms to reach digital-savvy investors and an additional tool for human advisors to use in serving clients. Digital advisors’ chief benefits include cheap, diversified portfolios and simple interfaces; a few have added valuable features, such as nonretirement goal planning and [tax-loss harvesting](https://www.morningstar.com/funds/its-not-too-late-tax-loss-harvesting). There are several differences among platforms’ fees and offerings, though.

To help investors sort through the options, Morningstar recently assessed 16 major robo-advisors as part of its [2025 Robo-Advisor Report](https://www.morningstar.com/lp/robo-advisor-landscape). We took a closer look at what the top robo-advisors can—and can’t—do for investors. A couple stood out for low costs and service breadth. Higher costs and poor transparency held others back.

If robo-advisors sound like a good fit, consider our list of top providers to better understand the options that could work for you.

## What Is a Robo-Advisor?

Robo-advisors occupy a middle ground between a wealth manager and a do-it-yourself trading platform. For example, robo-advisors use computer algorithms to provide low-cost [asset allocation](https://www.morningstar.com/investing-definitions/asset-allocation) and build automated investor [portfolios](https://www.morningstar.com/portfolios/model-vanguard-portfolios-short-intermediate-term-goals). They offer more specificity than the straightforward trade execution of a brokerage platform but not as much as the personalization you would get from a living, breathing wealth manager.

Morningstar defines “robo-advisors” as platforms that offer automated, semitailored strategic asset-allocation investment portfolios directly to retail customers. They commonly provide additional services and financial planning tools, as well as access to human advisors.

## More about Robo-Advisors

### Are Robo-Advisors Still Worth It?

Dive into what differentiates robo-advisor programs and which investors could benefit from robo-advice.

### Should You Be Using a Robo-Advisor?

These six questions can help you decide if robo-advice is right for you.

### Are Robo-Advisors Worth Your Investment?

Digital investment advice offers automated portfolios and cheaper fees, but talking with a person might appeal to some investors.

### 5 Questions to Ask a Financial Advisor

Ask about areas of expertise, compensation arrangements, and credentials before signing on for financial help.

## Who Are the Best Robo-Advisors?

Our assessment focused on the factors that most directly help investors reach their financial goals: fees, quality of portfolio construction and investment advice, and financial planning tools.

## Robo-Advisor Rankings

### Vanguard Digital Advisor/Vanguard Personal Advisor Services

![Vanguard Digital Advisor/Vanguard Personal Advisor Services  

Overall Evaluation: High 
Minimum Investment: $100 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.15% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? No](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/KZVNNKY6KJDRTI5PGJ6NTW2COM.png)

Vanguard Digital Advisor again took the top position among robo-advisors.

As of September 2024, the firm has lowered its minimum to $100, a move that put a wide variety of robust services within reach of almost everyone.

The services use Vanguard’s Life-Cycle Investing Model to create customized portfolios of passive exchange-traded funds with [glide paths](https://www.morningstar.com/investing-definitions/glide-path) based on investors’ ages, goals, and risk profiles.

Vanguard Digital Advisor charges as little as 0.20% per year, including underlying funds. Clients with $50,000 qualify for Vanguard Personal Advisor Services, which charges 0.30% annually, and get CFP access. Those with more than $500,000 get dedicated CFPs, while those with more than $5 million can invest in [private equity](https://www.morningstar.com/funds/its-getting-easier-invest-private-assets-what-does-that-mean-investors-2) and get [estate](https://www.morningstar.com/personal-finance/how-tackle-estate-planning-basics) and trust services.

### Fidelity Go

![Fidelity Go (logo)

Overall Evaluation: Above Average 
Minimum Investment: $10 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.00% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? No](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/QO7VGDSAFBHD3G3NQTCQOJZYAI.png)

Fidelity Go’s approach is cheap, simple, and based on robust research. It’s free for accounts up to $25,000, then charges 0.35% annually. For accounts of $25,000 or more, it includes access to a Fidelity advisor.

A risk-tolerance questionnaire covering the investor’s investment goals, time horizon, risk tolerance, investment experience, and financial situation helps steer investors into portfolios across eight risk levels that focus on core asset classes and shun esoteric ones.

The plan invests in a list of zero-expense-ratio Fidelity Flex funds to control total costs. Text alerts and other communications inform customers about their progress. However, Fidelity Go does not offer [tax-loss harvesting](https://www.morningstar.com/personal-finance/how-you-could-benefit-tax-loss-selling-this-year).

### Betterment/Betterment Premium

![Betterment/Betterment Premium   

Overall Evaluation: Above Average 
Minimum Investment: None 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.32% 
Drawdown/ Retirement Income Tools? Yes](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/C4KXP6AXEZD2FLA3ZHZPP5AS6U.png)

Betterment’s transparency, value, and sleek technology set it apart.

It’s one of the few robo-advisors that offers a glide path, which gradually makes its well-thought-out portfolios more conservative over time.

Betterment’s Core portfolios offer a mix of low-cost ETFs in all major asset classes. It once offered direct [crypto investing](https://www.morningstar.com/portfolios/how-use-bitcoin-your-portfolio) for 1% but switched to [crypto ETFs](https://www.morningstar.com/funds/memecoin-etfs-other-crypto-news-what-investors-should-know) charging 0.12% each.

It offers a wide range of services for reasonable fees. Betterment charges 0.25% annually, including for investors with balances under $20,000 who make monthly $250 deposits. Betterment Premium for clients with $100,000 charges 0.65% and includes access to certified financial planners.

### Schwab Intelligent Portfolios

![Schwab Intelligent Portfolios/Schwab Intelligent Portfolios Premium (logo)

Overall Evaluation: Above Average 
Minimum Investment: $5,000 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.00% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? Yes](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/J7WJVLCLCNFTRAKH7IWFX26PV4.png)

Low fees, solid investments, and extensive services make Schwab’s robo-advisor compelling.

Schwab Intelligent Portfolios uses an intuitive risk-tolerance questionnaire to match investors with portfolios fitting one of 12 risk profiles. Plus, the firm uses solid underlying investments, rebalances thoughtfully, and offers tax-loss harvesting.

Cash stakes, however, range from 6% to 30%, which curbs volatility but hampers returns. In 2022, Schwab paid $187 million to settle SEC charges that it put Intelligent Portfolio clients’ cash in deposit accounts of affiliated banks, which earned money for Schwab while hindering clients’ results.

The digital-only service levies no fee, while its premium version charges $30 per month and includes CFP access.

### Wealthfront

![Wealthfront   

Overall Evaluation: Above Average 
Minimum Investment: $500 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.25% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? Yes](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/JD57BQTAJNFKPN7K2XOFZ65MXY.png)

Wealthfront offers a strong combination of cost efficacy, service breadth, and investment quality.

It charges a 0.25% annual advisory fee, and expense ratios for most of its underlying funds are reasonable. The quality of these funds is strong: Most of them hold [Morningstar Medalist Ratings](https://www.morningstar.com/funds/why-were-enhancing-morningstar-medalist-rating) of Gold or Silver.

The program’s risk questionnaire also incorporates behavioral economics to evaluate investors’ willingness to take risk and ability to take it given their financial situation.

Wealthfront slots investors into a portfolio matching one of 20 risk levels and spanning taxable, retirement, and socially responsible accounts. It also offers tools for spending, savings, income, inflation, Social Security, taxes, college planning, and home equity, though it doesn’t offer access to human advisors.

### SigFig

![SoFi Wealth   

Overall Evaluation: Below Average 
Minimum Investment: $1 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.00% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? No](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/PDYCHVP2L5HIXKC5PYKVOXDWRM.png)

SigFig checks some, but not all, the right boxes.

Although fees are appealing (free for accounts up to $10,000), we have concerns with the transparency of its holdings.

SigFig uses low-cost ETFs but does not waive or return their fees, nor disclose the ETFs it uses, making it difficult to judge their quality. Allocations are strategic and reasonable, with equity weightings for taxable portfolios ranging from 26% to 90% of assets, depending on risk level, and 13% to 85% for tax-advantaged portfolios. All the tax-deferred portfolios allocate at least 7% of assets to emerging-markets debt, which is aggressive, and 5% to REITs.

### E-Trade Core Portfolios

![E-Trade Core Portfolios (logo)

Overall Evaluation: Average 
Minimum Investment: $500 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.30% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? No](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/JRSO4BTNWFCO7EAGKAJZG3HJHQ.png)

E-Trade Core Portfolios’ 0.3% annual fee is average, and its services meet investors’ basic needs—but rarely exceed them.

The low-cost ETFs it uses are its bright spot; they earn Gold or Silver Morningstar Medalist Ratings. E-Trade’s investment team builds [diversified portfolios](https://www.morningstar.com/portfolios/top-10-things-know-about-building-diversified-portfolio) that are not meant to shift much over time. A short risk questionnaire buckets investors into one of six target risk portfolios ranging from aggressive to conservative. E-Trade’s approach does not account for risk capacity, or how much risk an investor can handle based on their total wealth, goals, or investment horizon, something that many rivals do.

### Acorns

![Acorns  logo

Overall Evaluation: Average 
Minimum Investment: None 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.24% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? No](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/TZZCTVVIHZBY7E4I2A5YMDDALQ.png)

Acorns allows investors to round up everyday spending to build investment portfolios, which can appeal to investors who struggle to meet other programs’ minimum investment requirements.

However, its subscription pricing model is exorbitant for its audience. Its $3 monthly charge amounts to 0.24% for a $15,000 account but a steep 2.53% for Acorn’s estimated average account size of $1,425.

For that price point, Acorns clients get a limited number of risk-based portfolios—albeit with solid underlying investments from iShares, Vanguard, J.P. Morgan, and Goldman Sachs.

However, Acorns does allow some clients to wager some money on bitcoin and individual stocks.

### Merrill Guided Investing

![Merrill Guided Investing (logo)

Overall Evaluation: Average 
Minimum Investment: $1,000 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.45% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? Yes](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/Y33BBHM4RNFCJM3KGHFBVJG4QE.png)

Excessive fees hurt Merrill Guided Investing and Merrill Guided Investing with Advisor.

The services have added in-retirement income portfolios and tax-efficient rebalancing and tax-loss harvesting tools, but MGI’s and MGIA’s respective 0.45% and 0.85% fees are hefty.

They drop to 0.30% and 0.70% if members of the bank’s Preferred Rewards program accrue at least $100,000 in assets, but clients with $20,000 or less pay the full fee.

Merrill uses low-cost ETFs in its core and retirement-income portfolios, but its sustainability-focused and active/passive hybrid portfolios cost more. Investors who want access to CFPs must have Merrill-managed accounts or advisory relationships.

### SoFi Wealth

![SoFi Wealth logo

Overall Evaluation: Below Average 
Minimum Investment: $1 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.00% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? No](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/GWRKNGSZ6JFYTJ3OHRZ6A4I6GA.png)

SoFi clients can still get access to a certified financial planner, but its recently revamped portfolios now charge an annual fee and include questionable investments.

SoFi announced its BlackRock partnership in November 2024 as it overhauled its robo-advisor, which led to it offering more asset classes.

While no longer free, SoFi’s new 0.25% annual fee is cheap for services that include CFP access. There are other costs, though.

The robo-advisor’s portfolios have gotten more sophisticated since it partnered with BlackRock, albeit with some questionable choices. This includes some newer, niche ETFs that cost double or triple typical core holdings.

### Wells Fargo Intuitive Investor

![Wells Fargo Intuitive Investor   

Overall Evaluation: Below Average 
Minimum Investment: $500 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.35% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? No](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/QZ66QC3V3ZFNVPYZ7WQJPDOCRM.png)

Wells Fargo Intuitive Investor is a fine choice for existing bank clients. Although it’s a bit pricey at 0.35%, clients can qualify for rates as low as 0.25% depending on account types.

Its investment minimum of $500 is low, and underlying fund expense ratios are reasonable. But because it doesn’t disclose specific portfolio building blocks to nonclients, it’s hard to gauge their quality.

Wells Fargo uses SigFig’s algorithm to monitor, rebalance, and harvest tax losses. Its risk questionnaire is standard and suggested asset allocations seem prudent, with adequate exposure to core asset classes. It also offers phone access to financial advisors and tax-loss harvesting.

### Ally Invest

![Ally Invest logo

Overall Evaluation: Below Average 
Minimum Investment: $100 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.30% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? No](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/6IYBT35BQRCFBGHKK6QR5O66FE.png)

Ally Invest is good for Ally Bank customers, but it has fallen behind rivals.

Its 32 portfolios come in two flavors: Market-Focused, which keeps 2% in cash and charges 0.30% annually, and Cash-Enhanced, which has 30% in cash and no fee. The latter version has steep opportunity cost, though, as the cash allocation hinders returns when markets rise.

Ally Invest includes access to a human advisor for a tiered fee. However, those fees are high compared with premium services from Betterment, Fidelity, and Vanguard. Ally also lacks common features like outside account aggregation, multiple goal planning, and tax-loss harvesting.

### Empower Personal Wealth

![Empower Personal Wealth (logo)  

Overall Evaluation: Below Average 
Minimum Investment: $100,000 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.89% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? Yes](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/7R7EDKABKNH7HHZ6A2OPKHJPLM.png)

Empower Personal Wealth is comprehensive but expensive.

Fees start at 0.89% on the first $1 million and decline to 0.49% on anything above $11 million.

All clients have access to the impressive Empower Personal Dashboard that tracks spending, savings, checking, and investment accounts.

Accounts from $100,000 to $200,000 get basic ETF portfolios based on clients’ goals and risk tolerance. Those with $200,000 to $1 million get CFP access and customized portfolios that include individual securities. At higher levels, the firm also offers private banking and estate planning. Accounts with more than $5 million can invest in private equity.

### Citi Wealth Builder

![Citi Wealth Builder (logo)  

Overall Evaluation: Below Average 
Minimum Investment: $5000 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.25% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? No](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/KGDCWBLOURA6RJJEO7TFC2MODI.png)

Citi Wealth Builder is a viable, but limited, offering for Citi clients.

The program’s flat 0.25% advisory fee is competitive. That’s a large reduction from the 0.55% in 2022, but this is offset by the elimination of fund fee waivers, making the true reduction hard to determine, as Citi does not disclose the third-party funds it uses in its portfolios.

The firm also recently rolled out a more expensive, 0.60% premium offering, Citi Wealth Builder Plus. This tier requires an account minimum of $25,000 but comes with more planning resources and tax-efficient portfolio options. Its approach to portfolio construction, however, remains fairly basic.

### UBS Advice Advantage

![UBS Advice Advantage   

Overall Evaluation: Below Average 
Minimum Investment: $5,000 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 0.75% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? Yes](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/MWMWGIX7AFFA5ICMFE3RXG5XJA.png)

Hefty costs and poor transparency diminish the appeal of UBS Advice Advantage’s otherwise relatively robust offering.

With an annual fee of 0.75%, the program is among the priciest robo-advisors. And those fees are on top of underlying fund expense ratios, which are difficult to determine because UBS does not disclose the funds it uses.

The firm doesn’t disclose basic asset-allocation information about its five digital advice portfolios, which it recommends based on a standard risk questionnaire. The platform, powered by SigFig’s algorithm, has basic capabilities such as investment advice, trading/execution, and performance reporting. It also offers access to financial advisors.

### Titan

![Titan logo

Overall Evaluation: Low
Minimum Investment: $500 
Advisory Fees (Annual): 1.87% 
Drawdown/Retirement Income Tools? No](https://cloudfront-us-east-1.images.arcpublishing.com/morningstar/YSENSTHPVBDXZMEPOS2OHPF57M.png)

Titan has made sweeping changes to its pricing model and benefits but remains the least attractive robo-advisor we evaluated.

The firm has changed its fee structure before, flipping from a flat fee to an asset-based one. On Jan. 1, 2025, it began charging a $25 monthly fee or $250 annual “membership” fee. This is on top of a 0.20% annual advisory fee and the costs of the third-party funds it uses.

At 1.87% for a $15,000 account, this program is still the most expensive robo-advisor we’ve assessed. Portfolios remain a mixed bag of proprietary strategies, cryptocurrency accounts, and closed-end funds.

## How We Analyzed Robo-Advisors

[The Robo-Advisor Landscape report](https://www.morningstar.com/lp/robo-advisor-landscape) was designed to provide useful information to consumers before they sign up for a robo-advisor.

In the assessments, Morningstar’s analysts prioritized low, transparent fees; a robust risk-tolerance questionnaire; logical mapping to portfolios; sound portfolio diversification that steers clear of questionable asset classes and investment tactics; and a broad range of planning-related features.

Morningstar scored robo-advisors on a five-point scale (High, Above Average, Average, Below Average, and Low) along with four dimensions: total price (30% weighting); the process used to select investments, construct portfolios, and match portfolios with investors (30%); the organization behind the digital platform (20%); and the breadth of services (20%). Morningstar weighted each category score and then summed it to arrive at an overall score, which was then used to rank the robo-advisors.

In our evaluation of each provider, we assumed a $15,000 account balance for ease of comparison and have noted providers whose fees decrease for higher investment amounts.

*The following Morningstar analysts also contributed to this report: Lan Anh Tran; Drew Carter; David Kathman, CFA, Ph.D.; Vedran Beogradlija; Michael Dobson; Max Curtin; and Connor Gallagher.*

The author or authors do not own shares in any securities mentioned in this article.

## Popular

### Your 7-Figure Retirement Fund Might Not Stretch As Far As You Think. Here’s How to Change That

### This Wide-Moat Stock Is Still a Buy After Its Rally

Instead of supplanting traditional planners as some people predicted, independent digital advice providers have struggled to meet those early, heady expectations., In 2024, robo-advisor assets were between $634 billion and $754 billion, according to Cerulli Associates and other sources. That's a fraction of the $36.8 trillion US retail market., Vanguard Digital Advisor again took the top position among robo-advisors. As of September 2024, the firm has lowered its minimum to $100, a move that put a wide variety of robust services within reach of almost everyone., Fidelity Go's approach is cheap, simple, and based on robust research. args.summary:
Morningstar's 2025 Robo-Advisor Report evaluates 16 major digital advice platforms, noting that while robo-advisors have grown to between $634 billion and $754 billion in assets (2024), they remain a small fraction of the $36.8 trillion US retail market. The report ranks Vanguard Digital Advisor as the top pick, followed by Fidelity Go, Betterment, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios, and Wealthfront. Key evaluation criteria include fees, portfolio construction quality, financial planning tools, and transparency. The assessment scored providers on a five-point scale across four dimensions: total price (30% weighting), investment process (30%), organization (20%), and service breadth (20%), assuming a $15,000 account balance for comparison.

**Top Robo-Advisors:**
- **Vanguard Digital Advisor** (Overall: High) — Minimum $100, fees from 0.15%-0.20% annually, uses Life-Cycle Investing Model with glide paths. Clients with $50K+ get CFP access.
- **Fidelity Go** (Overall: Above Average) — Minimum $10, free for accounts under $25K, then 0.35% annually. Uses zero-expense-ratio Fidelity Flex funds.
- **Betterment/Betterment Premium** (Overall: Above Average) — No minimum, 0.25% annual fee (0.65% for Premium with CFP access). Offers glide paths and crypto ETF investing.
- **Schwab Intelligent Portfolios** (Overall: Above Average) — Minimum $5,000, no advisory fee (Premium $30/month). Uses 12 risk profiles but cash holdings of 6%-30% can hamper returns.
- **Wealthfront** (Overall: Above Average) — Minimum $500, 0.25% annual fee. Uses behavioral economics in risk assessment, offers 20 risk levels, and provides tools for spending, savings, retirement, and tax planning.

**Lower-Rated Providers:** SigFig, SoFi Wealth, Wells Fargo Intuitive Investor, Ally Invest, Empower Personal Wealth, Citi Wealth Builder, UBS Advice Advantage (0.75% fee), and Titan (1.87% for $15K account) were rated Below Average or Low due to high costs, poor transparency, or limited features.

[Pressroom home](/content/corporatesite/us/en/corp/who-we-are/pressroom/index.html)

# Vanguard Launches “Expert Insights,” Equipping Advisors with AI-Powered Portfolio Analysis Expertise

April 09, 2026

*Expert Insights delivers instant, personalized portfolio insights, combining Vanguard’s portfolio expertise with generative AI to help advisors scale high‑quality counsel*

VALLEY FORGE, PA (April 9, 2026)—Vanguard today announced the launch of Expert Insights, an AI-enabled portfolio analysis tool designed to help financial advisors deliver clear, confident investment guidance at scale. Expert Insights empowers advisors with instant, intuitive, deeply personalized portfolio insights, transforming complex data into actionable, client-ready guidance aligned with Vanguard’s trusted methodology.

Vanguard’s annual portfolio analysis engagements with advisors have approximately quadrupled over the past six years. Expert Insights puts the expertise of Vanguard’s portfolio analysis specialists directly in advisors’ hands.

“When advisors share their portfolios with us, we can work together on a powerful goal: helping create better outcomes for investors,” said Amma Boateng, Managing Director, Financial Advisor Services, Vanguard. “Vanguard is continually innovating on behalf of advisors and their clients, and we are excited to see Expert Insights help advisors in their effort to give more investors the best chance for investment success.”

Currently in pilot with select advisors, Expert Insights will be embedded within Vanguard’s open-access [Portfolio Analytics Tool](https://advisors.vanguard.com/strategies/portfolio-strategies/portfolio-analytics) later in 2026, giving advisors on-demand access to insights designed to help them pressure test and improve client portfolios

“I am constantly energized by seeing how advisors use AI to streamline their roles, and Vanguard is in a great position to be an important partner in that process,” said Sid Ratna, Head of Digital and Analytics, Financial Advisor Services, Vanguard. “With Expert Insights, we’re providing advisors with a clear, straightforward way of communicating the advantages of their clients’ portfolios, opening more time for advisors to spend coaching and building trust with their clients.”

**Providing New Enhancements for Advisors**

Expert Insights is the latest in a growing list of recent enhancements from Vanguard to help advisors streamline and scale client support. Others include:

* Launched in 2025, Vanguard’s [Client-Ready Article Summaries](/content/corporatesite/us/en/corp/who-we-are/pressroom/press-release-vanguard-unveils-generative-ai-client-summaries-for-financial-advisors-050525.html) use GenAI to produce customizable synopses of its top-read market perspectives tailored by financial acumen, investing life stage, and tone.
* Available within Vanguard’s Portfolio Analytics Tool, the [Stress Testing](https://advisors.vanguard.com/strategies/portfolio-strategies/portfolio-analytics/stress-testing) feature helps advisors evaluate their clients’ portfolios in extreme markets to uncover vulnerability, test performance during historical and future scenarios, and demonstrate preparedness for a range of market conditions.
* The [Health Care Cost Estimator](https://advisors.vanguard.com/wealth-management/healthcare-costs-in-retirement/calculator) helps advisors forecast their clients’ annual and long-term health care costs, giving advisors a clearer picture of what their client may pay to help them plan for retirement with more accuracy.
* The [Social Security Calculator](https://advisors.vanguard.com/wealth-management/social-security-calculator/client-information) forecasts an investor’s future primary, spousal, and survivorship Social Security benefit amounts; recommends the optimal age and month to claim Social Security benefits; and estimates mortality-weighted lifetime values based on primary, spousal, and survivor benefits as they apply.

Together, these enhancements reinforce Vanguard’s commitment to equipping advisors with technology that combines scale, rigor, and simplicity.

For more information on Expert Insights and the other advisor enhancements mentioned above, visit [advisors.vanguard.com](https://advisors.vanguard.com/).

###

**About Vanguard**  
 Founded in 1975, Vanguard is one of the world's leading investment management companies. The firm offers investments, advice, and retirement services to tens of millions of individual investors around the globe—directly, through workplace plans, and through financial intermediaries. Vanguard operates under a unique, investor-owned structure where Vanguard fund shareholders own the funds, which in turn own Vanguard. As such, Vanguard adheres to a simple purpose: To take a stand for all investors, to treat them fairly, and to give them the best chance for investment success. For more information, visit [vanguard.com](https://investor.vanguard.com/corporate-portal).
