### What are the benefits of Vanguard Digital Advisor versus investing in a target-based fund?

A target retirement fund (or target-date fund) is a specific type of fund that automatically adjusts its asset mix over time. Target retirement fund names typically refer to the approximate year (the target date) when an investor would retire.

[Vanguard's target retirement funds](/investment-products/mutual-funds/target-retirement-funds) start aggressively and are mostly made up of stock funds. As years pass, the funds become more conservative and hold more bond funds along a singular glide path. All Vanguard target retirement funds charge an expense ratio and make the assumption that investors are retiring at 65 and have the same risk tolerance.10

Since Digital Advisor is a [paid advisory service](/advice/robo-advisor#DaFeeCalculator), investors enrolled in Digital Advisor can take advantage of more benefits. Your asset mix will come from one of over 300 personalized glide paths that help you find an appropriate asset mix based on a wide range of factors including your current age, risk attitude and loss aversion, and marital status.

Digital Advisor clients can also take advantage of tools and services like a debt calculator,4 a goal optimizer, an emergency fund tool, and tax-loss harvesting5 at no additional cost.

### What's the minimum amount I need to enroll in Vanguard Digital Advisor?

Enrollments in Vanguard Digital Advisor require at least $100 in each Vanguard Brokerage Account.2 For each taxable, traditional, Roth, or rollover IRA you wish to enroll, the entire balance must be in certain investment types (based on eligibility screening by Digital Advisor at the time of enrollment, see next question for more details) and/or the brokerage account's settlement fund.

For eligible 401(k) retirement accounts, the minimum enrollment balance is $5.9

### What else do I need to know about my Vanguard Brokerage Account/settlement fund before I enroll?

Your eligibility screening will determine whether you have the types of investments that Digital Advisor can manage. In some cases, you'll need to sell all or a portion of certain investments as part of the enrollment process so we can manage them for you.

For each brokerage account you wish to enroll, the entire balance must be in certain investment types (based on eligibility screening by Digital Advisor at the time of enrollment) and/or the brokerage account's settlement fund. If your brokerage accounts include Vanguard index funds or Vanguard ETFs®, you may be able to keep those investments in your Digital Advisor account. However, we may recommend you sell down those or other investments before enrolling. Since there may be costs and tax consequences associated with selling your existing investments, we use a breakeven cost analysis to weigh the costs of transitioning the investments you hold before enrolling in Digital Advisor (see our [Digital Advisor brochure](https://personal1.vanguard.com/ngf-next-gen-form-webapp/forms) for more details). We estimate the capital gains tax impacts compared to the expense ratio benefits from selling investments that aren't our lead recommendation (the investment we would typically recommend for you), but that still align with your recommended asset allocation. So depending on the outcome of the breakeven analysis, we may recommend that you continue to hold certain investments subject to our portfolio construction guidelines—or we may determine it's in your interest to sell down a particular investment during enrollment.

The following types of investments cannot be in your brokerage account before enrolling in Digital Advisor: certain non-Vanguard mutual funds, individual bonds, securities traded on international exchanges, preferred stocks, penny stocks, illiquid stocks, and options.

In this case, you'd need to sell the ineligible investments and invest the proceeds in your brokerage account settlement fund before enrolling. If you're in this situation, you might also consider opening a new Vanguard Brokerage Account to enroll in Digital Advisor.

Important: Digital Advisor doesn't assess the suitability of the sale of existing holdings given a particular client's financial circumstances, recommend selling a client's existing holdings to enroll, or provide tax advice. The sale of existing holdings could cause you to incur capital gains—costs associated with incurring capital gains vary based on the time you hold a position and your individual tax situation. The cost of incurring capital gains can be substantial. We recommend you consult a qualified tax advisor to discuss your individual situation and any potential tax consequences.

For eligible 401(k) retirement accounts, Digital Advisor doesn't require a money market or stable value fund minimum balance.9

### Should I know about any other expenses?

You'll incur expenses to invest in the underlying funds, collective investment trusts, and ETFs in your portfolio (i.e., expense ratios). If you're invested in ETFs, collective investment trusts, or mutual funds today, you're already paying these expenses. We credit the revenue received from your investment portfolio toward the gross advisory fee and deduct only the additional net advisory fee from your managed accounts.

In general, if you incur a fee that results in revenue for Vanguard or a Vanguard affiliate, it will be included in this credit amount. Certain regulatory required trading fees aren't considered revenue and are still incurred for trades within Vanguard Brokerage Accounts, but not credited. For more information about Digital Advisor's fee structure, refer to [Form CRS Conversation Starter questions](https://personal1.vanguard.com/usa/ngf-next-gen-form-webapp/public/forms) and the [Vanguard Digital Advisor Brochure](https://personal1.vanguard.com/usa/ngf-next-gen-form-webapp/public/forms).

### Frequently asked questions about Robo-Advisors

#### What's an advantage of using a robo-advisor to invest?

One key advantage is that a robo-advisor helps to take the day-to-day complexity out of investing. It builds and manages a diversified portfolio for you based on your goals, time horizon, and tolerance for risk. A robo-advisor will then keep that strategy on track automatically over time. That means ongoing portfolio monitoring, rebalancing, and adjustments happen in the background without requiring constant decisions from you.

#### Are robo-advisors worth it?

A robo-advisor can be worth it if you want a low-cost, low-maintenance way to invest with a long-term strategy—and prefer to spend less time worrying about the details and more time focusing on what matters to you.

#### What sets Vanguard Digital Advisor apart from other robo-advisors?

We're glad you asked! Our money-management service:

Digital Advisor can manage your personal investment accounts and certain employer-sponsored 401(k) retirement accounts for which Vanguard is the recordkeeper.9

#### What types of accounts can Vanguard Digital Advisor manage?

Digital Advisor can manage eligible 401(k) retirement accounts9 and the following types of retail Vanguard Brokerage Accounts:

However, we recommend that you connect other Vanguard and non-Vanguard accounts as you plan your goals so we can incorporate them into your goal growth projections, and help you forecast your likelihood of meeting your long-term goals.

#### What types of accounts qualify for the 90-day fee waiver offer?

Your first eligible Vanguard Brokerage Account (IRA or taxable) or employer-sponsored retirement plan account (such as a 401(k)) qualify for the advisory fee waiver. (If your employer-sponsored plan account qualifies for the advisory fee waiver, you’ll see that during the enrollment process.)

If your account has been enrolled in Digital Advisor for more than 90 days, any new accounts you subsequently enroll are not eligible for the advisory fee waiver.

Employer-sponsored retirement accounts enrolled by the plan fiduciary are not eligible for the advisory fee waiver.

For more information on Digital Advisor’s fee structure, [see the VAI Form CRS and the Vanguard Digital Advisor Brochure](https://personal1.vanguard.com/ngf-next-gen-form-webapp/forms).

#### How will Vanguard Digital Advisor handle market volatility?

Market volatility is when the price of stocks swings up or down because there's too much trading in one direction (substantially more buys than sells or vice versa). Many investors might see the stock dip and want to sell or wait to "time the market." The market, however, is unpredictable. But that doesn't mean your money is completely up to the whims of the headlines. Even with daily ups and downs, the overall market has historically grown over the decades.

With Digital Advisor, you can benefit from the market's long-term growth with a time-tested strategy: owning a balanced portfolio. The foundations of a balanced portfolio are asset allocation and diversification. Digital Advisor will maintain your investments so you'll always have a portfolio that aligns to your retirement goal. If you choose to add other goals, it can adjust your holdings to keep you on target. We'll rebalance your portfolio if we detect it's drifted more than 5% from our recommended allocation.

What can you do during market swings? You can look at your accounts and update your information if anything has changed. You can also check out Vanguard's resources on market swings. Rest assured that your goal projections take all kinds of market volatility into account—while short-term "blips" might feel jarring, we have your long-term focus in mind.

args.summary: Vanguard Digital Advisor is a robo-advisor service that provides automated, personalized investment management. Key features include: no advisory fees for the first 90 days, a minimum of $100 in assets to enroll, and annual fees of approximately $15-$16 per $10,000 for all-index portfolios. The service offers three investment options: All-Index (0.20% gross advisory fee, up to $20/year per $10,000), Active/Index (0.25% gross advisory fee, up to $25/year per $10,000), and ESG (0.20% gross advisory fee, up to $20/year per $10,000). The enrollment process involves creating a profile, completing a financial profile, taking a risk attitude quiz, setting retirement goals, and funding accounts. Digital Advisor provides tools like goal optimizer, debt payoff calculator, emergency fund tool, and tax-loss harvesting. It was the first robo-advisor to receive a 5.0 rating in Morningstar's Robo-Advisor report (January 2025). The service can manage eligible 401(k) accounts and various Vanguard Brokerage Accounts. It uses over 300 personalized glide paths and automatically rebalances portfolios when they drift more than 5% from the recommended allocation. Vanguard Digital Advisor is designed for investors seeking a low-cost, hands-off approach to long-term investing. For those with $50,000 or more, Vanguard Personal Advisor offers additional guidance with access to a human advisor.

Scenario

## Using Copilot for AI-assisted broker portfolio management

Client advisors can use AI for assistance with recommending investment opportunities by analyzing market data, aggregating news, and understanding client priorities.

### 1. Analyze market overview

Day to day management of investment portfolios requires staying current on quickly changing market data and analyzing existing portfolios.

![Microsoft Copilot icon](/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/icon-copilot.svg)

Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat1

Benefit: **Use Copilot to compile** the latest figures for identified markets along with a sentiment analysis.

### 2. Analyze VIP client portfolios

Identify the top client portfolios that require immediate attention due to significant changes in asset value or risk exposure due to market shifts.

![Microsoft Copilot Studio icon](/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/icon-microsoft-copilot-studio.png)

AI Agent

Benefit: **Use Copilot to provide summary of portfolios that need attention** and click to open specific portfolios in a modal for teams for a detailed view of the portfolio.

### 3. Check for recent news and info

Find and analyze news articles affecting specific segments that may impact stock holdings within a specific portfolio.

![Microsoft Copilot Studio icon](/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/icon-microsoft-copilot-studio.png)

AI Agent

Benefit: **Copilot integrates with news aggregators** and identifies the most impactful recent news articles along with summary of key points impacting portfolio holdings.

### 4. Identify investment opportunities

Based on current market conditions and news, identify a list of potential investment opportunities from the portfolio optimization system with reasons for recommending.

![Microsoft Copilot Studio icon](/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/icon-microsoft-copilot-studio.png)

AI Agent

Benefit: **Ask Copilot to assemble top 5 investment opportunities** based on the information gathered from the portfolio management agent.

### 5. Draft customer recommendation

Draft email to client regarding rebalancing their portfolio due to the market shifts.

![Outlook icon](/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/icon-outlook.svg)

Copilot in Outlook

Benefit: **Use Copilot to draft a personalized email** to client outlining the need for a portfolio review and suggesting a meeting.

### 6. Assist with compliance

Help propose portfolio adjustments that comply with SEC regulations and company standards and policies.

![Microsoft Copilot Studio icon](/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/icon-microsoft-copilot-studio.png)

AI Agent

Benefit: **Copilot scans proposed changes** and reviews against regulatory and compliance documentation for SEC and the company. Copilot highlights any compliance concerns it recognizes to give the broker a head start on their review.

# The College for Financial Planning®—a Kaplan Company Launches AI-Driven Wealth Management Professional Assistant for Financial Advisors

Kaplan

Centennial, CO (September 30, 2025) ⁠— The [College for Financial Planning](https://www.cffp.edu/)—a [Kaplan](https://kaplan.com/) Company has launched the Wealth Management Professional Assistant, leveraging artificial intelligence, designed to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of financial advisors when serving clients. Built on the College’s trusted educational content, the CFFP Wealth Management Professional Assistant provides financial professionals with on-demand access to up-to-date information and scenario-based guidance. The tool is intended to complement advisors’ expertise, offering quick fact checks, conceptual refreshers, and support in navigating complex client questions.

The launch of the Professional Assistant comes on the heels of a [recent Advisor360° survey](https://www.advisor360.com/2025-connected-wealth-report) highlighting a dramatic shift in financial advisors’ views on artificial intelligence. A strong 85 percent of advisors now say AI is helpful to their practice, up from 65 percent just a year ago, and 76 percent report experiencing immediate benefits from generative AI–enabled tools.

In response to the changing sentiment among financial advisors, the CFFP Wealth Management Professional Assistant functions as an interactive resource: Advisors enter their questions and receive clear, reliable answers in real time. For straightforward inquiries, such as retirement distribution rules or the impact of recent legislation, the tool delivers quick responses. In more complex cases, it further prompts advisors with clarifying questions, ensuring that the guidance is tailored to the situation at hand.

Dirk Pantone, president of the College, said:

“The CFFP Wealth Management Professional Assistant represents a significant step forward in integrating AI responsibly into the financial services profession, enhancing advisor capabilities and client outcomes. By leveraging the College for Financial Planning’s trusted and continually updated content, the Professional Assistant enables financial advisors to save time, deliver superior client services, and remain knowledgeable in an ever-evolving industry.”

Financial advisory and wealth management firms, as well as independent advisors, can visit the [Professional Assistant website](https://www.kaplanfinancial.com/wealth-management/advisor-ai-tools) to learn more and purchase a monthly subscription.

Reporters interested in covering this launch can contact Russell Schaffer at [russell.schaffer@kaplan.com](mailto:russell.schaffer@kaplan.com)

### About the College for Financial Planning®—a Kaplan Company

Founded in 1972, the College for Financial Planning®—A Kaplan Company provides accessible and flexible degree, non-degree, and continuing professional education programs to students nationwide. Shortly after its founding, the College introduced the CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ certification, which is now the world's most recognized and respected financial planning credential with more than 100,000 certified professionals. The College for Financial Planning is accredited by the [Higher Learning Commission](https://www.hlcommission.org/institution/1590/) and is a member of the North Central Association. More than 200,000 students have graduated from the College’s programs.  The College is part of global education company Kaplan. For more information, visit [www.cffp.edu](https://www.cffp.edu/).

# Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank Launch AI-Powered Meeting Journey

AI solution modernizes the full lifecycle of client engagement

New capability can save financial advisors up to four hours per meeting across millions of meetings annually

## Key points

* **Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank introduce an AI-powered meeting solution** to transform the advisor-client experience.
* **The solution’s intelligent workflow tools** help deliver meeting prep materials, summaries, and actionable next steps.
* **This capability expands the firm’s growing suite of tech‑enabled workflows** as Bank of America accelerates its enterprise‑wide deployment of purpose‑built AI.

## Key points

* **Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank introduce an AI-powered meeting solution** to transform the advisor-client experience.
* **The solution’s intelligent workflow tools** help deliver meeting prep materials, summaries, and actionable next steps.
* **This capability expands the firm’s growing suite of tech‑enabled workflows** as Bank of America accelerates its enterprise‑wide deployment of purpose‑built AI.

NEW YORK, N.Y. – Bank of America’s Wealth Management businesses, Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank, today announced the full-scale rollout of AI‑Powered Meeting Journey, an integrated solution that helps optimize how advisors and their teams prepare for, conduct, and follow up on client meetings. The streamlined meeting experience enables advisors to redirect meaningful time toward strategic planning and deeper client engagement.

*“AI‑Powered Meeting Journey represents a meaningful advancement in how the wealth management industry uses AI,”* said **Patricio Diaz, Chief Operating Officer at Merrill**. *“This latest solution empowers advisors to shift capacity toward activities that drive business growth and strengthen how we serve clients.”*

## AI-Powered Meeting Journey Core Capabilities

* **Meeting Prep:** Quickly searches and consolidates client relationship insights and recent activity into ready‑to‑use prep materials to enable more personalized and productive client conversations.
* **Meeting Summarization:** With client consent, acts as an AI notetaker during virtual meetings, capturing discussion highlights and creating a shareable meeting summary.
* **Meeting Follow‑Up:** Summarizes meeting decisions and next steps based on meeting notes, generating tasks and documentation.

*“Early users of the Meeting Prep and Meeting Summarization capabilities are already seeing significant improvements in their workflows*,” said **Shimna Sameer, Head of Products, Solutions & Platforms at Bank of America Private Bank**. “*This is time our teams are reinvesting into client engagement, with even more proactive guidance and meaningful support.*”

## Frequently asked questions: Bank of America’s Approach to AI in Wealth Management

### Question: How is AI used at Bank of America today?

**Answer:** Bank of America invests thirteen point five billion dollars$13.5 billion annually on technology. Of this, four billion dollars$4 billion is dedicated to new initiatives, such as AI. AI is helping transform employee productivity and strengthen operational excellence. By leveraging AI at scale across our global operations, we are expanding capabilities, optimizing process efficiency, and driving exceptional client service.

### Question: Why is AI a strategic priority for Bank of America’s wealth management businesses?

**Answer:** AI enables us to deliver more personalized, efficient, and intuitive experiences for clients. AI increases advisors’ capacity to focus on deeper client conversations, strategic planning, and long‑term relationship building.

### Question: What’s next for AI in Merrill and Private Bank?

**Answer:** We will continue expanding AI capabilities that strengthen advisor‑client relationships. Future advancements will focus on accelerating advisor efficiency, enhancing personalization and supporting more proactive guidance delivered through our high‑tech, high‑touch approach.

### Question: What role will advisors continue to play as AI becomes more widely used in wealth management?

**Answer:** The role of the advisor will always remain central to the client relationship. While AI can enhance efficiency, it cannot replace the valuable judgment, empathy, understanding and personal connection advisors bring to clients.

### Question: Has Bank of America been an early adopter of AI?

**Answer:** Bank of America has been investing in AI for more than a decade, taking a disciplined approach to developing and deploying AI solutions effectively and responsibly at scale. We work to ensure our AI solutions and investments are reusable across different areas of the business. For example, in 2018, we launched Erica®, the first widely adopted AI‑driven virtual financial assistant. Since then, clients have interacted with Erica more than three point two billion times3.2 billion times. We leveraged the same underlying technology to launch ask MERRILL® and ask Private Banking®, helping advisors and employees quickly find information, connect with colleagues, and better serve clients.

Bank of America is one of the world’s leading financial institutions, serving individual consumers, small and middle-market businesses and large corporations with a full range of banking, investing, asset management and other financial and risk management products and services. The company provides unmatched convenience in the United States, serving nearly 70 million clients with approximately 3,600 retail financial centers, approximately 15,000 ATMs (automated teller machines) and award-winning digital banking with approximately 59 million verified digital users. **Overview:** Bank of America's Wealth Management businesses (Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank) announced the full-scale rollout of the AI-Powered Meeting Journey, an integrated solution designed to optimize how advisors prepare for, conduct, and follow up on client meetings. The capability can save financial advisors up to four hours per meeting across millions of meetings annually.

**Core Capabilities:**
- **Meeting Prep:** Searches and consolidates client relationship insights and recent activity into ready-to-use prep materials.
- **Meeting Summarization:** With client consent, acts as an AI notetaker during virtual meetings, capturing discussion highlights and creating shareable summaries.
- **Meeting Follow-Up:** Summarizes meeting decisions and next steps based on meeting notes, generating tasks and documentation.

**Key Quotes:**
- Patricio Diaz, COO at Merrill: "AI-Powered Meeting Journey represents a meaningful advancement in how the wealth management industry uses AI."
- Shimna Sameer, Head of Products, Solutions & Platforms at Bank of America Private Bank: "Early users of the Meeting Prep and Meeting Summarization capabilities are already seeing significant improvements in their workflows."

**Broader AI Context at Bank of America:**
- Bank of America invests $13.5 billion annually on technology, with $4 billion dedicated to new initiatives such as AI.
- The company has been investing in AI for over a decade, launching Erica® in 2018 (the first widely adopted AI-driven virtual financial assistant, with over 3.2 billion client interactions since then).
- The same underlying technology powers ask MERRILL® and ask Private Banking® for advisors and employees.
- The role of the advisor remains central to the client relationship; AI enhances efficiency but cannot replace judgment, empathy, and personal connection.

**About Bank of America:** One of the world's leading financial institutions, serving nearly 70 million clients with approximately 3,600 retail financial centers, 15,000 ATMs, and 59 million verified digital users. The company serves clients across the U.S. and more than 35 countries.

# Building an AI-Powered Financial Assistant App: Features and Use Cases

Explore how AI-powered personal finance apps drive customer engagement and business growth.

Personal finance has become increasingly complex in recent years. With the growing trend towards a subscription economy, people now have to manage numerous bills across the physical and digital realms. The average US consumer now has [4.5 video streaming subscriptions](https://www.forbes.com/sites/bradadgate/2024/02/20/survey-on-average-subscribers-pay-924-a-year-with-streaming-video/) alone.

This shift has led to budgeting issues for the average consumer. In America, [84% of people exceed their monthly budget](https://www.nerdwallet.com/article/finance/data-2023-budgeting-report), with 44% of those people using credit cards to cover their overspending. One thing is clear: the need for effective personal finance tools has never been greater.

To meet this growing demand, banks and FinTechs are building AI-driven financial applications that provide automation and real-time finance analytics. In addition to basic budgeting tools, AI-powered personal finance assistants now provide hands-on guidance that actively improves users’ financial literacy.

If you’re interested in taking advantage of the opportunity that AI in personal finance offers, you’ve come to the right place. Read on to explore everything you need to know about AI personal financial assistant app development. We’ll cover:

* The benefits and use cases of AI for personal finance
* Key technologies and features of AI personal finance apps
* How Intellias can help you develop an AI personal financial assistant that users will love

[With deep industry knowledge and technology expertise, we help banks, FinTechs, and other financial businesses harness the power of technology.

Explore our services](https://intellias.com/financial-services/)

## Global trends in AI for personal finance

Personal finance is evolving rapidly in response to technological advancements. With the rise of AI, regular people now have access to financial tools that offer:

* Real-time and predictive analytics
* Tailored financial advice and financial planning
* Automated budgeting and investment tracking

These tools enable users to understand their finances with a level of granularity that was once impossible. Users can see how much they spend on different consumer categories. They can track spending habits and understand future trends. And they can budget for upcoming holidays and other life events.

But that’s not all. AI-based financial assistants provide real-time guidance. Just like a human financial advisor, they learn about the individual’s needs, goals, and financial situation. They then offer personalized advice designed to help the user achieve long-term financial stability. And unlike a human financial advisor, AI-powered robo-advisors are affordable for all.

For financial institutions, shifting towards AI for personal finance management provides an opportunity for growth, improved customer satisfaction, and differentiation. Put simply, banks that offer AI financial assistants will have a competitive advantage over those that don’t.

As a result, the market for AI in personal finance is booming.

### Global AI in personal finance market

*Source: [Market.us](https://market.us/)*

In 2025, it was valued at $1 billion and is [forecast to grow to $3.7 billion](https://market.us/report/ai-in-personal-finance-market/) by 2033 at a CAGR of 18.1%.

*Source: [Market.us](https://market.us/)*

## Why do banks need artificial intelligence?

Banking is nothing like it used to be. Where traditional, in-branch processes were once the norm, customers now expect slick, digital interactions with their banks.

Challenger banks like Monzo and Revolut have been quick to jump on this trend, disrupting the sector with a digital-only approach. These banks have captured market share thanks to their strong focus on mobile apps, outstanding UX, and frictionless processes.

With mobile banking now standard, AI represents the next frontier of digital transformation for banks. It provides the foundation for a whole host of transformative features and services that revolutionize the banking experience for customers.

From a business perspective, AI offers powerful benefits. Banks that build AI-based personal finance assistants can:

* Differentiate themselves in an increasingly crowded market
* Meet customer expectations for automated, hyper-personalized services
* Enhance the user experience, leading to improved customer satisfaction and loyalty
* Reduce manual workloads and improve cost optimization

The chart below shows which AI benefits are the most significant for the financial services sector across different regions.

*Source: [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/louiscolumbus/2020/10/31/the-state-of-ai-adoption-in-financial-services/)*

## Key components of AI-powered personal finance apps

Building an AI-driven financial application requires integrating core technologies to address user challenges and deliver value. Here are some of the key components that combine to create outstanding personal finance apps:

### Financial data management

Users often struggle to consolidate their financial data across accounts, making budgeting and cost-tracking difficult. At the same time, traditional online banking portals offer little in the way of financial insights.

AI-powered personal finance assistants can solve these issues through seamless integration with a range of data sources. Modern financial apps use APIs and secure integrations to enable real-time data flows. The result is an accurate, unified, up-to-date view of finances.

### Predictive analytics

Data is the driving force behind AI assistants. In addition to consolidating financial data, it enables apps to deliver personalized advice, track spending, and provide budgeting forecasts.

AI-powered apps take data from multiple sources, analyze it using machine learning algorithms and predictive models, and then deliver financial insights tailored to the individual. These insights help users budget, save, and invest more effectively.

### Natural language processing (NLP)

The user experience of legacy banking portals often leaves a lot to be desired. The more complex a financial interface is, the more customs will be deterred from using it. NLP solves this problem by allowing users to interact with modern banking apps using natural language.

NLP combines deep learning, computer learning, and computational linguistics to analyze language and understand the meaning and context of text or speech. It then generates human-like answers that are highly relevant and personalized.

### Generative AI

While similar to NLP in some ways, [generative AI](https://intellias.com/generative-ai-services/) offers broader options for content creation that spans text, images, videos, and even code. Gen AI typically uses large language models (LLMs), like those behind popular tools such as ChatGPT. This opens the door for powerful use cases, including:

* Personalized finance advice
* Dynamic reports based on real-time financial data
* Accurate forecasts based on different scenarios

Gen AI has the potential to reshape the way customers and banks interact, potentially [adding $340 billion](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/financial-services/our-insights/capturing-the-full-value-of-generative-ai-in-banking) to the banking sector in the coming years.

### Robust data security

When it comes to digital banking, data security is one of the biggest concerns among users. Data breaches can be catastrophic, leading to lost funds and shattered user trust. This is why robust data security is of central importance when creating an AI financial assistant. We recommend following security best practices such as:

* Data encryption
* Two-factor authentication
* AI-driven fraud detection

[Transform your financial services business with custom AI-powered apps your customers will love.

## Must-have features of an AI-powered personal finance app

While no two personal finance apps are the same, some features are non-negotiable. Below, we’ll look at some key features of a personal finance assistant app that customers increasingly expect.

### Financial coaching

One of the most powerful features for your AI personal financial assistant is financial coaching. Powered by [predictive analytics](https://www.predictiveanalyticstoday.com/what-is-predictive-analytics/), machine learning, and behavioral analysis, so-called robo-advisors provide tailored financial advice that aligns with users’ unique situations and goals.

By analyzing transaction history and behavior patterns, this powerful feature recognises the user’s habits and makes predictions about their future actions. Moreover, it democratizes the kind of bespoke advice that was once only available to high-net-worth individuals. Offering this type of feature is a game-changer for customer satisfaction and retention rates.

With demand for robo-advisors booming, the US market is forecast to grow at a CAGR of 28.3% through the end of the decade, [reaching $41 billion by 2030](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/robo-advisory-market-report).

U.S. robo advisory market

*Source: [Grand View Research](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/robo-advisory-market-report)*

### Goal setting and progress tracking

This handy feature enables users to set savings goals for major purchases, holidays, weddings, or other key events. It provides real-time updates, with visualizations that show progress towards goals. The same goes for debt repayments.

Visualizing progress towards financial goals is inherently motivating. It provides users with the transparency and insights they need to see their commitments through, resulting in improved customer satisfaction.

### Expense tracking and categorization

Where traditional banking apps typically only allow users to sort transactions by incoming/outgoing, modern personal finance apps automatically sort transactions into specific categories using AI algorithms.

Expense tracking and categorization enable users to see where their money is being spent, which helps with budgeting. It also improves the UX by reducing manual effort, resulting in higher retention rates.

### Expense forecasting

The best AI-based personal finance assistants leverage predictive analytics to analyze a user’s spending behavior, transaction history, and recurring patterns. By identifying trends and patterns in this data, apps can anticipate future expenses. Users receive alerts such as “your outgoings are likely to be higher next month,” enabling them to budget more proactively.

### Investment tracking

The best financial apps combine day-to-day financials with investment accounts for a complete view of a user’s financial position. With APIs providing real-time price updates, users can see how their investments are performing and the total value of their portfolios at any given time.

For your business, providing investment tracking opens the door to investors as well as regular consumers. It creates a one-stop shop for users to manage the entirety of their financial affairs, resulting in greater adoption and a broader user base.

### Chatbots and digital assistants

NLP, coupled with AI, enables users to interact with advanced [AI chatbots](https://intellias.com/introduce-ai-and-chatbots-to-your-business/) and engage in human-like conversations, transforming the user experience. NLP-powered chatbots can:

* Answer queries about investing and budgeting
* Provide personalized financial guidance
* Troubleshoot technical issues

By providing users with 24/7 assistance, you can reduce operational costs associated with customer support. And with [72% of banking customers](https://www.zendesk.co.uk/blog/customer-experience-in-banking/) expecting immediate service, integrating a chatbot into your financial assistant is now non-negotiable.

A comparison table contrasts governed AI (data stays in tenant, retrievable records) vs. public chatbots (data leaves firm, no firm-side copy).

--- SOURCE 1: Artificial Intelligence at Edward Jones - Two Use Cases - Emerj Artificial Intelligence Research ---
URL: https://emerj.com/artificial-intelligence-at-edward-jones-two-use-cases

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from Emerj Artificial Intelligence Research explores two business use cases of AI at Edward Jones, a U.S.-based financial services firm with $16 billion in revenue (2024), 20,000+ financial advisors, and $2.2 trillion in client assets. The firm's strategic investment arm, Edward Jones Ventures (launched 2025), funded Grantd, an AI-powered equity compensation planning platform, in September 2025.

**Use Case 1: Scaling Modernization Efforts with GenAI**
Edward Jones partnered with EPAM Systems to integrate GenAI into software engineering workflows. CIO Kevin Adams (quoted via The Wall Street Journal) described challenges with legacy mainframe systems and cloud migration. GenAI was used to automate code migration, refactoring, unit test generation, documentation, and to analyze legacy codebases. A notable example involved using GenAI to examine a legacy fee-billing system for retirement invoicing, extract business rules, and generate technical documentation. AI-generated unit tests validated that new systems behaved consistently with original applications. The company reported measurable productivity gains, faster modernization cycles, and cost savings.

**Use Case 2: Delivering Real-Time Advisor Intelligence**
Edward Jones faced data silos across hundreds of systems that prevented advisors from accessing real-time insights during client conversations. Key challenges included fragmented data, inability to deliver real-time insights, complex infrastructure, and scalability issues. The firm invested in an "advisor intelligence" strategy using AI-powered systems to surface relevant insights within advisor workflows, with key elements including real-time data integration, AI-powered recommendations, contextual insights, and scalable infrastructure. MuleSoft's Director of Financial Services noted that Edward Jones connected data across 900+ applications using MuleSoft. The article references MIT Sloan Management Review research indicating wealth management firms using AI for advisors have seen measurable improvements in efficiency, client engagement, and decision-making.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"Kevin Adams, Edward Jones's chief information officer and head of digital, described the complex environment in which the company's engineering teams operate. He attributed this complexity to the firm's long-standing reliance on legacy mainframe systems and its ongoing cloud migration efforts.", "The company reported that the use of GenAI translated directly into measurable productivity gains, faster modernization cycles, and meaningful cost savings.", "Lindsey Turner, Principal in Data Science, Analytics, and BI at Edward Jones, took to her LinkedIn to share some insights from the panel. Details from that discussion were later reported by RTInsights.", "Peter Hegyi, Director of Financial Services at Mulesoft, highlighted how Edward Jones' advisor intelligence strategy was enabled by MuleSoft's ability to connect data across more than 900 applications.", "Research from MIT Sloan Management Review highlights that wealth management firms using AI to support advisors have seen measurable improvements in efficiency, client engagement, and decision-making."

[J.P. Morgan Chase](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/) reportedly unveiled an artificial intelligence-powered tool designed to facilitate thematic investing.

The tool, called [IndexGPT](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-05-03/jpmorgan-unveils-indexgpt-in-next-wall-street-bid-to-tap-ai-boom?sref=zNmRQ0gk), delivers thematic investment baskets created with the assistance of [OpenAI](https://openai.com/)’s [GPT-4](https://openai.com/index/gpt-4) model, Bloomberg reported Friday (May 3).

The tool allows for the selection of a broader range of stocks, going beyond the obvious choices that are already well-known, [Rui Fernandes](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rui-fernandes-a3364a2/), J.P. Morgan’s head of markets trading structuring, told Bloomberg.

Thematic investing, which focuses on emerging trends rather than traditional industry sectors or company fundamentals, has gained popularity in recent years, the report said.

Thematic funds experienced a surge in popularity in 2020 and 2021, with retail investors spending billions of dollars on products based on various themes. However, interest in these strategies waned amid poor performance and higher interest rates, per the report.

J.P. Morgan Chase’s IndexGPT aims to reignite interest in thematic investing by providing a more accurate and efficient approach, according to the report.

While AI has been widely used in the financial industry for functions such as trading, risk management and investment research, the rise of generative AI tools has opened new possibilities for banks and financial institutions, the report said.

args.summary: JPMorgan Chase has unveiled IndexGPT, an AI-powered tool for thematic investing that uses OpenAI's GPT-4 model. The tool, reported by Bloomberg on May 3, 2024, creates thematic investment baskets by generating keywords associated with a theme and using natural language processing to scan news articles and identify relevant companies. According to Rui Fernandes, J.P. Morgan's head of markets trading structuring, the tool allows for selecting a broader range of stocks beyond obvious well-known choices. Thematic investing gained popularity in 2020-2021 but waned due to poor performance and higher interest rates. IndexGPT aims to reignite interest by providing a more accurate approach. Fernandes sees it as a first step in integrating AI across the bank's index offerings. The article also mentions similar AI deployments at Morgan Stanley (AI-powered assistant for financial advisors) and in venture capital for investment decisions.

By   [Madeline Garfinkle](https://www.entrepreneur.com/author/madeline-garfinkle)    |   May 26, 2023

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

The widespread popularity of ChatGPT has prompted other big companies like Google to launch [their own AI services](https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/7-big-announcements-from-googles-developer-conference/451987) to compete. However, it’s not just tech companies entering the AI race.

JP Morgan Chase is developing a “ChatGPT-like” service that will use artificial intelligence to help customers select investments, CNBC [reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2023/05/25/jpmorgan-develops-ai-investment-advisor.html).

According to a filing in New York, JP Morgan applied to trademark the product “IndexGPT.” The service will use artificial intelligence and cloud computing software to analyze and select securities “tailored to customer needs,” the filing states.

**Related: [Microsoft Revealed Major AI Updates at Its Developer Conference — Here’s What You Need to Know](https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/microsoft-revealed-ai-updates-at-its-developer-conference/452796)**

While it’s unclear when the product will launch, the trademark could signal that it might be in the near future.

“Companies like JP Morgan don’t just file trademarks for the fun of it,” Josh Gerben, a trademark attorney in Washington D.C. told CNBC. “The filing includes a sworn statement from a corporate officer essentially saying, ‘Yes, we plan on using this trademark.'”

IndexGPT may also only be one of several AI products in development at JP Morgan. During the company’s annual investor conference on Monday, Lori Beer, global technology chief at the company, [said](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/content/dam/jpmc/jpmorgan-chase-and-co/investor-relations/documents/events/2023/jpmc-investor-day-2023/JPM-Investor-Day-2023-Final-Full-Transcript.pdf) that the bank is testing “a number of use cases” for AI technology.

“We are actively evaluating opportunities with large language models and see great potential in that space,” she added.

# Meet ‘IndexGPT,’ the A.I. stock picker JPMorgan is developing that may put your ‘financial advisor out of business’

![Will Daniel](https://fortune.com/img-assets/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/id-2.png?format=webp&w=1440&q=100)

By 

[Will Daniel](/author/will-daniel/)

Will Daniel

![Will Daniel](https://fortune.com/img-assets/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/id-2.png?format=webp&w=1440&q=100)

By 

[Will Daniel](/author/will-daniel/)

Will Daniel

May 26, 2023, 1:05 PM ET

![JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon](https://fortune.com/img-assets/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/GettyImages-1255488782-e1685107586533.jpg?format=webp&w=1440&q=100)

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie DimonSarah Silbiger—Bloomberg/Getty Images

Add Fortune on Google for similar content.

[JPMorgan Chase](https://fortune.com/company/jpmorgan-chase/) is leaning into the artificial intelligence [boom](https://fortune.com/2023/05/25/nvidia-guidance-4-billion-jaw-dropping-ai-artificial-intelligence-gold-rush/) in a way that could make some financial advisors uneasy. The firm, which topped the [first-ever ranking](https://fortune.com/2023/01/26/jpmorgan-chase-tops-first-of-its-kind-ranking-of-a-i-progress-in-banking/) of A.I. progress among banks this year, is creating an A.I. tool to help investors pick stocks.

Recommended Video

---

On May 11, JPMorgan filed a [trademark application](https://tsdr.uspto.gov/#caseNumber=97931538&caseType=SERIAL_NO&searchType=statusSearch) with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office for “IndexGPT,” an A.I. software service that can be used for the “selection of financial securities and financial assets.” The filing was [first cited in a CNBCreport](https://www.cnbc.com/2023/05/25/jpmorgan-develops-ai-investment-advisor.html).

Trademark attorney [Josh Gerben](https://www.gerbenlaw.com/about/josh-gerben/) told CNBC’s Hugh Son that the move is a “real indication” that JPMorgan might soon launch an A.I. product for investors. “Companies like JPMorgan don’t just file trademarks for the fun of it,” he said. “This sounds to me like they’re trying to put my financial advisor out of business.”

IndexGPT is likely to do more than just advise investors, too. JPMorgan’s trademark application also includes a reference to the technology being used in “financial investment in the field of securities” as well as “funds investment.” And it could potentially be used in everything from “advertising” and “marketing services” to clerical and administrative tasks.

That’s because JPMorgan filed its IndexGPT application for three separate international classes of trademark. The first is for “advertising and business” services, the second is for “insurance and financial” services, and the third is “computer and scientific” services, according to the [United States Trademark and Patent Office](https://tmep.uspto.gov/RDMS/TMEP/current#/current/TMEP-1400d1e1.html).

A JPMorgan Chase representative declined to comment on the company’s trademark application and its recent push into artificial intelligence in an email to *Fortune.* It’s unclear if or when the company will make its A.I. technology available to either its own employees or customers.

IndexGPT isn’t JPMorgan’s first move into A.I., however. In April, the investment bank’s economists began using an [A.I. model](https://fortune.com/2023/04/28/jpmorgan-artificial-intelligence-chatgpt-llm-hawk-dove-federal-reserve-speak/) that analyzes Federal Reserve communications to help predict the central bank’s next moves. And CEO Jamie Dimon has lauded recent developments in A.I. repeatedly over the past few years. In March, he said the technology was “staggering” in an interview with [Bloomberg](https://fortune.com/2023/03/06/jamie-dimon-ukraine-war-china-relations-soft-landing-ai-artificial-intelligence-extraordinary/) and briefly discussed how the bank plans to use it in a variety of ways.

“We’re already using it to do risk, fraud, marketing, prospecting—and it’s the tip of the iceberg. To me this is extraordinary,” he said.

Other big investment banks have also begun testing A.I. products recently. In March, [Morgan Stanley](https://fortune.com/company/morgan-stanley/) [announced](https://fortune.com/2023/03/14/morgan-stanley-testing-openai-chatgpt-gpt4-to-help-financial-advisors/) that it is developing tools to help its wealth managers sift through and better understand the investment bank’s mountain of research on the economy and markets. In a similar move, *Fortune*’s Jeremy Kahn [reported](https://fortune.com/2023/04/14/goldman-sachs-create-chatgs-ai-chatbot-cio-internal-message/) in April, [Goldman Sachs](https://fortune.com/company/goldman-sachs-group/) is considering creating its own “ChatGS” A.I. technology to help financial advisors sort through data and better serve clients.

# Unveiling IndexGPT: JPMorgan’s latest AI innovation in thematic investing

![Unveiling IndexGPT: JPMorgan's latest AI innovation in thematic investing](https://fintech.global/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/joshua-mayo-HASoyURgPMY-unsplash-3-696x464.jpg "Unveiling IndexGPT: JPMorgan's latest AI innovation in thematic investing")

**[JPMorgan Chase & Co.](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/) recently announced the launch of IndexGPT, marking a significant step in the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and finance, according to a report from [Bloomberg](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/jpmorgan-unveils-indexgpt-in-next-wall-street-bid-to-tap-ai-boom-1.2068519).**

IndexGPT introduces a novel approach to thematic investing, leveraging OpenAI’s GPT-4 model to construct thematic investment baskets. Unlike traditional indexes that rely on industry sectors or company fundamentals, IndexGPT identifies investments based on emerging trends, powered by AI-generated keywords extracted from news articles.

The Wall Street enthusiasm for AI-driven innovations continues to grow, with IndexGPT poised to capitalize on the investor frenzy.

Rui Fernandes, JPMorgan’s head of markets trading structuring, emphasizes that IndexGPT represents the bank’s commitment to integrating AI across its offerings gradually and thoughtfully.

# Bank of America’s AI Agent Ecosystem

## Bank of America Uses AI Agents Executive Summary

Bank of America’s prominent position in the application of artificial intelligence within the financial services sector is not the result of a recent surge in technological adoption but the deliberate culmination of a patient, decade-long strategy. This report provides an exhaustive analysis of the bank’s AI agent ecosystem, deconstructing ten primary use cases that serve as exemplars of a deeply ingrained, infrastructure-first philosophy. The bank’s approach is defined by a doctrine of treating AI not as a series of discrete projects but as a foundational layer of its operational and technological infrastructure. This has been supported by consistent, substantial investment, totaling approximately $13 billion annually in technology, with about $4 billion of that directed toward new initiatives in 2025.1

The cornerstone of this strategy is a principle of “invest once, reuse everywhere”.3 This is most clearly demonstrated by the proprietary natural language processing engine developed for the consumer-facing virtual assistant, Erica®, which now powers a suite of specialized AI agents across wealth management and corporate banking. This platform-based model creates a powerful flywheel effect, where each new application enhances the core intelligence of the system while benefiting from the initial foundational investment, a strategy protected by a formidable portfolio of nearly 1,400 AI and machine learning patents.1

The tangible return on this investment is evident across the enterprise. Internally, AI agents have driven profound operational efficiencies, including a 20% productivity increase for 17,000 software developers and a 50% reduction in IT service calls.1 Externally, client-facing agents like Erica have managed over 2.7 billion interactions, achieving a 98% query containment rate and fundamentally shifting the customer relationship from reactive service to proactive guidance.3 In specialized domains, AI is transforming core banking functions, from providing corporate treasurers with near-instant cash flow forecasting to automating invoice reconciliation and enhancing fraud detection with sophisticated behavioral modeling.4

This analysis will detail these ten core use cases, not as a simple list, but as interconnected components of a cohesive and remarkably successful AI strategy. It will demonstrate how Bank of America’s disciplined, risk-managed, and long-term approach to building AI agents has created a durable competitive advantage, driving shareholder value through significant cost savings, enhanced productivity, and deeply integrated client relationships.

> [FAQ: Bank of America Uses AI Agents – 10 Ways to Use AI [FAQ] [2025]](https://www.klover.ai/faq-bank-of-america-uses-ai-agents-10-ways-to-use-ai-faq-2025/)

# The BofA Blueprint: A Strategy of Patient, Foundational AI

To comprehend the success and scale of Bank of America’s individual AI applications, it is essential to first understand the strategic blueprint that governs them. The bank’s approach is not a reaction to the recent hype surrounding generative AI but a continuation of a long-term vision characterized by patience, foundational investment, and disciplined execution. This philosophy explains why the bank has succeeded where others have struggled, creating a resilient and compounding technological advantage.

## AI as Infrastructure: The “Basement, Not Just the Branch” Doctrine

Bank of America’s leadership articulates a clear and defining principle: “AI isn’t a project at the bank; it’s the infrastructure layer that powers everything”.3 This mindset, described as “patient, data-first, and deeply operational,” fundamentally distinguishes its strategy from competitors who may pursue isolated, high-profile AI projects.3 Instead of focusing on the “razzle-dazzle” of a single application, the bank has concentrated its efforts on building the “basement”—the robust, underlying data and technology architecture required to power AI at an enterprise scale.

This strategic commitment required immense preparation long before the launch of its flagship AI products. Years before the consumer-facing virtual assistant Erica debuted in 2018, the bank undertook the massive and complex task of aggregating the “lion’s share of its customer interaction and transactional data”.3 This proactive unification of data from disparate systems created a “clean runway for insight discovery and model training,” providing its analytics and AI experts with the high-quality, structured data necessary to build effective models.3 This foundational work, while resource-intensive, was a critical prerequisite for every subsequent AI success.

This long-term vision is underpinned by consistent and substantial capital allocation. The bank dedicates roughly $13 billion annually to its IT infrastructure and operations.1 Of this amount, nearly a quarter, or approximately $4 billion in 2025, is specifically directed toward new technology initiatives, including the continued development of its AI capabilities.2 This level of sustained investment signals that AI is not a discretionary expense but a core component of the bank’s long-term growth and efficiency plans.

By treating AI as core infrastructure, Bank of America has strategically avoided the common pitfall of chasing short-term, siloed AI experiments that often fail to scale or deliver lasting value. The significant upfront investment in unifying data and building enterprise-grade pipelines, though costly, established a durable competitive advantage. This foundation ensures that every new AI application can be developed and deployed more rapidly and at a lower marginal cost, creating an environment where innovation can flourish responsibly and sustainably.3 This approach is a direct technological manifestation of the bank’s overarching corporate strategy of “Responsible Growth,” which prioritizes building a simple, stable, and resilient enterprise capable of delivering consistent performance over the long term.8 The focus on building the “basement” before showcasing the “branch” mirrors the bank’s post-financial crisis philosophy, demonstrating a rare and powerful alignment between technology strategy and corporate identity.

## The Flywheel of Reuse and Investment: Compounding Returns on IP

A central tenet of Bank of America’s AI strategy is the mantra to “Invest once; reuse everywhere”.3 This principle transforms the high initial cost of building foundational AI capabilities from a one-time expense into a compounding asset. According to this model, the first project in any given portfolio “pays the freight charge”—it bears the cost of developing the heavy-lifting infrastructure, such as enterprise-grade data pipelines, a governed feature store for machine learning models, and reusable Application Programming Interfaces (APIs).3 Consequently, every subsequent project built upon this foundation can be developed and deployed with greater speed and at a significantly lower cost.

The most potent example of this platform strategy is the natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning engine originally developed for Erica. This core technology, representing a massive investment in development and training, is not a standalone product. Instead, it serves as the intelligent chassis for a growing fleet of specialized AI agents. The same engine that helps a retail customer check their balance now powers “Ask Merrill” and “Ask Private Bank” for high-net-worth clients and the “CashPro Chat” tool for corporate treasurers.3 This strategic reuse allows the bank to deliver sophisticated, personalized AI experiences to diverse client segments without having to rebuild the core intelligence from scratch for each one.

This strategy is not merely about saving costs; it creates a powerful flywheel effect that accelerates innovation. Each new application built on the central platform feeds new data and user interactions back into the system, continuously refining the underlying models and making the entire platform more intelligent and effective. This virtuous cycle enhances the value of the core asset with every deployment.

To protect this compounding investment, Bank of America has built a formidable intellectual property (IP) portfolio that serves as a competitive moat. The bank holds nearly 1,400 granted patents and pending applications focused on AI and machine learning, the most of any financial services company.1 This represents a 94% increase in its AI-related patent portfolio since 2022 alone, signaling an acceleration of its innovation efforts.4 This vast IP library codifies the bank’s unique processes and technologies, making it difficult for competitors to replicate its capabilities. Beyond its defensive value, this patent leadership serves as an offensive tool in the fierce competition for talent. For a bank competing with technology giants, being the recognized IP leader in financial AI creates a highly attractive environment for top engineers and data scientists. The bank fosters a culture where innovation is “decentralized by design,” with nearly 8,000 employees contributing to patents, and acknowledges that such achievements serve as a “moral booster”.5 This creates another virtuous cycle: top talent is attracted to an innovative environment, leading to more groundbreaking work, which results in more patents, further solidifying the bank’s reputation as a technology leader and attracting even more talent.

## Governed Innovation: A Bifurcated Approach to AI Risk

Bank of America navigates the complex risk landscape of artificial intelligence with a sophisticated and deliberate strategy of governed innovation. The institution consistently emphasizes that its use of AI is grounded in principles of “human oversight, transparency, and accountability for all outcomes”.2 This commitment is not merely a public statement but is embedded in the architecture of its AI systems, revealing a bifurcated approach that separates high-risk, client-facing applications from lower-risk, internal use cases.

This caution is most evident in the design of its flagship virtual assistant, Erica. While the industry rushes to integrate large language models (LLMs), BofA executives have expressed clear reservations about their unpredictability for critical financial tasks, noting that with generative AI, “you’ve got to worry about hallucinations”.5 Consequently, Erica was explicitly designed

*not* to use generative AI or LLMs. Instead, it relies on proprietary, “supervised machine learning” that draws responses from a “pre-defined set of answers” curated and controlled by a team of human experts.12 This deterministic approach sacrifices the boundless creativity of generative AI for the absolute certainty and accuracy required when providing financial information to millions of customers.

Simultaneously, the bank is aggressively deploying cutting-edge generative AI in controlled, internal environments where the risk profile is dramatically different. It has rolled out generative AI-powered coding assistants to its 17,000 software developers to boost productivity.1 It has also developed an internal generative AI platform for its Global Markets division, enabling sales and trading teams to rapidly search, summarize, and synthesize vast quantities of proprietary research reports.2

This dual strategy is a masterful example of risk stratification. For high-stakes, externally-facing functions that are subject to intense regulatory scrutiny and have a direct impact on client finances, the bank deploys highly controlled, proprietary AI to eliminate unpredictability and ensure compliance. For lower-risk, internal productivity applications, it embraces the latest generative AI tools to capture significant efficiency gains and accelerate its own development cycles. This bifurcated model allows Bank of America to innovate at the cutting edge where it is safe to do so, while maintaining the fortress-like controls necessary for a systemically important financial institution. It is a pragmatic and responsible approach that maximizes the benefits of AI while rigorously managing its inherent risks.
