# Client-Facing AI Agents: Redefining the Customer Relationship

Bank of America has placed AI agents at the forefront of its digital client experience, transforming how millions of customers interact with the institution. These agents are not merely add-on features but are central to the bank’s strategy of delivering personalized, efficient, and proactive service at an unprecedented scale. The following use cases, summarized in Table 1, demonstrate how BofA is leveraging AI to redefine the modern banking relationship.

## Use Case 1: Erica® – The Cornerstone Virtual Financial Assistant

Launched in 2018, Erica® stands as Bank of America’s flagship AI agent and is described as the “first widely adopted AI-driven virtual financial assistant” in the industry.2 Integrated directly into the bank’s mobile app, Erica serves as the primary digital interaction point for millions of customers. Its functionality is extensive, enabling users to perform a wide array of banking tasks with ease. These include fundamental actions like checking account balances, searching for specific transactions, transferring funds between accounts, and sending money via Zelle.18 It also handles more advanced needs, such as locking and unlocking debit cards, accessing FICO® Score updates and alerts, and redeeming cash-back rewards.13 Clients can interact with Erica through multiple modalities, including voice commands, text messages, or by tapping suggested options on their screen, providing a flexible and intuitive user experience.18

The scale and impact of Erica are immense. The assistant has successfully managed over 2.7 billion client interactions since its inception, serving a base of 20 million active users.2 Critically, it achieves a 98% containment rate, meaning the vast majority of customer queries are fully resolved by the AI without needing to escalate to a human agent.3 This level of automation has freed up human call center staff to focus on more complex, high-value client issues.3

The success of Erica is rooted less in technological novelty and more in a disciplined focus on flawless execution of core user needs. The most frequently used features are fundamentally simple, such as searching for transactions with specific merchants or viewing account balances.18 By perfecting this limited but critical set of high-volume tasks, BofA built a tool that is exceptionally reliable and trustworthy. This disciplined approach, prioritizing dependability over a wider but less reliable feature set, has been the key to its massive adoption and high client satisfaction.

Perhaps the most significant evolution in Erica’s function has been its shift from a reactive tool to a proactive guide. Initially designed to answer client questions, the platform now initiates the majority of its engagements. Proactive insights now account for 60% of all Erica interactions.14 These unsolicited alerts include notifications about potential duplicate charges, warnings of subscription price increases, confirmations of merchant refunds, and weekly spending snapshots.13 This transformation represents a fundamental change in the bank-customer relationship. The AI agent has elevated the bank from a passive keeper of records that a customer must query into a vigilant, proactive financial partner that constantly monitors for risks and opportunities on the client’s behalf. This provides immense perceived value, deeply embedding the bank in the client’s financial life and creating a powerful “stickiness” that drives loyalty and retention.

## Use Case 2: “Ask Merrill” & “Ask Private Bank” – Tailored Wealth Management Guidance

Building directly on the success and technological foundation of Erica, Bank of America has deployed specialized AI assistants, “Ask Merrill” and “Ask Private Bank,” for its wealth management clients.3 These agents are a prime demonstration of the bank’s “reuse” strategy, leveraging the core natural language processing engine and infrastructure developed for the mass-market Erica platform and tailoring it to the specific needs of high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individuals.

While they share the same technological backbone as Erica, the functionality of these wealth-focused assistants is highly specialized. They are trained on a distinct corpus of knowledge related to investments, market analysis, and portfolio management. Clients can use these tools to ask questions about their portfolio’s performance, get real-time quotes for securities, inquire about investment balances and holdings, and understand trading activity.15 This provides affluent clients with immediate, on-demand access to critical information about their wealth.

Crucially, these AI agents are designed not to replace human advisors but to augment them. They serve as an efficient “off-ramp,” providing clients with a seamless pathway to connect with their dedicated human Merrill advisor or Private Bank relationship manager for more complex conversations and strategic advice.15 This hybrid model enhances the client experience by providing the instant gratification of AI for informational queries while preserving the high-touch, trust-based relationship with a human expert for strategic guidance. The impact of this use case extends beyond client service. By leveraging the foundational investment in Erica, the bank was able to develop and deploy these sophisticated assistants for its highest-margin business segments far more quickly and at a lower cost than would have been possible if building them from scratch.3 This allows the bank to efficiently scale its personalization capabilities and deliver a cutting-edge digital experience to its most valuable clients, reinforcing its position as a leader in wealth management technology.

## Use Case 3: AI-Enhanced Digital Mortgage Experience

Bank of America is strategically applying artificial intelligence to its digital mortgage platform, creating a competitive offering in a market increasingly dominated by digital-native lenders like Rocket Mortgage.16 The bank’s approach to this complex product demonstrates a nuanced understanding of where AI can add the most value, blending back-end automation with essential human interaction.

The platform utilizes AI to significantly accelerate key parts of the mortgage process. Former executives have noted that AI is crucial for processing vast amounts of information and for developing the underlying software, stating, “Without AI, we would not be able to write code fast enough”.16 This suggests that AI is used to streamline document analysis, data extraction, and other repetitive tasks that are common in loan origination, similar to industry trends where AI is used to move applications more efficiently from preapproval to underwriting.22

However, the most distinctive feature of Bank of America’s approach is its deliberate integration of a human touch. Rather than pursuing complete automation, the bank’s research revealed a critical customer insight: applicants “wanted to speak with an expert at certain points of the mortgage application process”.16 Recognizing that a mortgage is a high-anxiety, emotionally charged transaction, the bank strategically built human interaction points directly into the digital workflow. This hybrid model allows customers to benefit from the speed and convenience of a digital application while having access to the reassurance and expert guidance of a loan officer at critical decision points.

This use case highlights a sophisticated strategic choice. Bank of America has prioritized customer trust and experience over a purely technological solution. By recognizing the limitations of AI in managing the complex emotional needs of a mortgage applicant, the bank has created a product that balances the efficiency of automation with the irreplaceable value of human expertise. This nuanced approach aims to capture the best of both worlds, using AI to drive back-end productivity while deploying human capital where it has the greatest impact on client satisfaction and conversion.16

# Internal & Operational AI Agents: Driving Enterprise Efficiency

While its client-facing AI agents garner the most public attention, Bank of America’s internal deployment of artificial intelligence is arguably just as impactful. The bank has systematically turned its AI capabilities inward, creating a suite of agents designed to optimize operational processes, reduce internal friction, and empower its global workforce of over 213,000 employees.2 These internal applications are a primary driver of the bank’s significant efficiency gains and cost savings.

## Use Case 4: Erica for Employees – The Internal Productivity Engine

Mirroring the success of its client-facing counterpart, “Erica for Employees” is an internal, generative AI-powered virtual assistant that has been rolled out across Bank of America’s entire global workforce.1 This powerful tool functions as a centralized, intelligent resource for automating a wide range of common administrative, HR, and IT support tasks that were previously handled by human support teams.

The functionality of Erica for Employees is broad and practical. Associates use the assistant to execute routine but essential tasks such as resetting passwords, managing equipment refreshes, locating payroll and tax forms, and finding information about their health benefits and other company policies.1 By providing instant, self-service resolution for these high-volume queries, the tool dramatically reduces the burden on internal support desks.

The scale of adoption and its resulting impact are profound. The assistant is now utilized by nearly all of the bank’s more than 210,000 associates.1 This widespread deployment is directly credited with achieving a more than 50% reduction in calls to the IT service desk, a clear and measurable return on investment.5 This use case is a powerful example of applying AI to streamline internal operations, reduce administrative overhead, and free up specialized support staff to focus on more complex, strategic issues.

Beyond the direct cost savings, the deployment of Erica for Employees represents a brilliant change management strategy. By making a helpful and reliable AI agent a part of the daily workflow for every single employee—from branch tellers to senior executives—the bank has systematically built familiarity and trust in its AI capabilities from the ground up. This has normalized the use of AI across the organization, creating a workforce that is culturally more prepared and receptive to further AI-driven transformations. This widespread, positive, low-stakes interaction effectively lowers the internal barriers to adoption for future, more critical AI initiatives.

## Use Case 5: Generative AI for Software Development

Bank of America has made a strategic investment in deploying automated, generative AI-powered coding tools across its vast technology division, directly targeting the heart of its innovation engine.1 These tools are designed to augment the capabilities of the bank’s software developers, accelerating the entire software development lifecycle from conception to deployment.

The functionality of these AI assistants is multifaceted. They help developers write new code more quickly, generate comprehensive test cases to ensure software quality, and improve the overall stability and performance of applications.6 By automating some of the more repetitive and time-consuming aspects of programming, these tools allow developers to focus on higher-level problem-solving and architectural design.

This initiative has been implemented at a significant scale, with the tools being used by the bank’s 17,000 programmers.1 The impact on productivity has been immediate and quantifiable. Bank of America has already measured a 20% efficiency improvement among its coders who are using these generative AI tools.5 This translates into a substantial increase in development velocity, enabling the bank to build, test, and release new applications and updates to its digital platforms much more rapidly.

This use case creates a powerful, self-reinforcing loop of technological acceleration. The efficiency gains realized by the developers using these AI tools directly impact their ability to build and refine all of the bank’s other technology systems, including its other AI platforms like Erica and the CashPro suite. In essence, the investment in developer-focused AI is an investment in the “factory” that produces all of the bank’s digital “products.” This creates a compounding effect, where the bank’s overall capacity for innovation grows at an accelerated rate, providing a significant and sustainable competitive advantage in the fast-moving world of financial technology.

## Use Case 6: The Academy’s AI Conversation Simulators

In a novel application of artificial intelligence, Bank of America utilizes AI-based conversation simulators within “The Academy,” its globally recognized onboarding, education, and professional development organization.2 This initiative demonstrates the bank’s commitment to using technology not just for technical tasks but also for developing the crucial “soft skills” of its client-facing employees.

The AI simulators provide a safe and interactive environment where employees can practice a wide variety of client conversations. These simulations can range from routine service inquiries to more complex and sensitive discussions about financial products or client needs. The core of the technology is its ability to provide interactive coaching and real-time feedback. As an employee navigates a simulated conversation, the AI analyzes their responses, language, and tone, offering immediate guidance and suggestions for improvement.2 This allows staff to build proficiency, refine their communication techniques, and ensure they are delivering a consistent, high-quality service experience in line with the bank’s standards.

The adoption of this training tool has been extensive. In a single year, Bank of America employees completed over one million of these AI-powered simulations.2 Many employees have noted that the opportunity to practice client conversations in this risk-free setting helps them feel more confident and prepared when they engage with real clients, ultimately leading to better and more consistent service delivery.2 This use case is a compelling example of how AI can be applied to enhance human-to-human interaction, directly investing in the quality of the bank’s most valuable asset: its people. It shows a forward-thinking approach to talent development, leveraging technology to scale high-quality coaching and training across a massive workforce.

# Specialized Financial AI Agents: Core Banking and Market Operations

Beyond its broad consumer and internal applications, Bank of America deploys a range of highly specialized AI agents designed to operate within the complex, high-value domains of corporate banking, risk management, and global markets. These agents tackle some of the most intricate challenges in finance, leveraging AI to drive efficiency, mitigate risk, and provide deep analytical insights for the bank and its most sophisticated clients.

## Use Case 7: CashPro® AI Suite for Corporate Treasurers

CashPro® is Bank of America’s global treasury management platform, a critical tool for its corporate and commercial clients worldwide. In recent years, the bank has systematically infused the platform with a powerful suite of AI and machine learning tools, transforming it from a simple transactional portal into an intelligent, predictive financial command center.6

The AI suite within CashPro includes several key functionalities:

### **CashPro Forecasting:**

This tool uses machine learning to analyze a client’s historical cash flows, automatically selecting the most accurate models to predict future cash positions. It replaces traditional, manual spreadsheet processes that could take a week with sophisticated modeling that is completed in minutes. The models are retrained daily with new data, allowing them to continuously adapt to a company’s specific seasonality and operational patterns.6

### **CashPro Chat:**

Built on the same Erica platform, this virtual assistant is tailored for corporate treasurers. It helps financial professionals quickly navigate the platform, view transactions, and find information about their accounts, with approximately 40% of queries being self-serviced through the tool.6

### **CashPro Insights:**

This proactive AI capability analyzes a client’s transactional data to deliver tailored recommendations. It might encourage a shift from paper checks to more efficient digital payments or highlight opportunities to enhance account security. The goal is to help clients understand “what they should be doing, not just what they are doing today”.6

The impact of these tools is transformative. They are fundamentally changing the role of corporate treasurers, moving them away from manual data aggregation and toward strategic, data-driven decision-making. Clients have described the amount of data and insight now available as “jaw-dropping,” providing valuable data points that previously took many internal steps to obtain.6 This deep integration of intelligence into a client’s core workflow creates a powerful “data ecosystem” lock-in. The AI learns the specific patterns of a client’s business, with one client noting, “CashPro knows more about my business than some of my team does”.6 This accumulated, proprietary intelligence makes the platform indispensable, creating extremely high switching costs and cementing Bank of America’s relationship with its corporate clients.

## Use Case 8: AI-Powered Fraud Detection and Risk Management

Bank of America employs a multi-layered, AI-driven approach to fraud detection and risk management, which is essential for protecting the bank and its 69 million consumer and small business clients.7 This system leverages advanced machine learning algorithms to monitor financial activities in real-time, moving beyond simple rule-based alerts to a more dynamic and predictive security posture.

The functionality of the bank’s fraud prevention system is built on several key AI techniques:

### **Behavioral Profiling:**

The system first establishes a baseline of normal activity for each customer by analyzing their typical transaction patterns, locations, and frequencies. AI algorithms then monitor for significant deviations from this established behavior, which can be an early indicator of account takeover or fraud.7

### **Real-Time Transaction Scoring:**

As transactions occur, machine learning models instantly analyze dozens of variables to assign a risk score. This allows the system to flag potentially fraudulent activities in real-time, enabling immediate intervention, such as blocking a transaction or alerting the customer.7

### **Network Analysis:**

AI is used to identify subtle, coordinated patterns of activity across multiple, seemingly unrelated accounts. This is particularly effective in detecting and dismantling sophisticated, organized fraud rings that would be invisible to systems looking at accounts in isolation.7

Beyond fraud, AI plays a pivotal role in credit risk assessment. Instead of relying solely on traditional credit scores, the bank’s AI models can analyze a much broader range of data, including a customer’s detailed transaction history and spending behavior, to create a more comprehensive and accurate risk profile.17 This enhanced assessment leads to better-informed lending decisions, reducing the likelihood of defaults and improving the overall quality of the bank’s loan portfolio. It can also help facilitate access to credit for individuals who may have been unfairly overlooked by conventional scoring methods.17 The impact of this comprehensive AI risk framework is a significant reduction in fraud incidents, faster and more accurate detection of threats, and a more resilient and profitable lending business.17

## Use Case 9: Intelligent Receivables® – Automating B2B Payments

Bank of America’s Intelligent Receivables® solution is a highly sophisticated AI-powered service designed to solve a critical and often inefficient aspect of business-to-business commerce: cash application and invoice reconciliation.4 This tool leverages artificial intelligence and advanced optical character recognition (OCR) data capture technology to streamline and automate the complex process for its corporate clients.

The core function of Intelligent Receivables is to automatically match incoming payments, which may arrive through various channels like ACH, wire, or check, with a company’s corresponding outstanding invoices. This task, traditionally performed manually by accounts receivable staff, is often time-consuming and prone to error, especially when remittance information is missing or separate from the payment itself. The system uses AI to bring together the payment information and the associated remittance detail, intelligently matching them to close out open invoices.4

A key feature of the platform is its ability to learn over time. The AI models analyze customer payment patterns and behaviors, continuously improving the accuracy of remittance data and the system’s matching capabilities. For example, if a particular customer consistently bundles payments for multiple invoices, the system learns to recognize and correctly apply these complex payments in the future.4

The impact for corporate clients is substantial. By automating this labor-intensive process, Intelligent Receivables dramatically reduces the time, cost, and human error associated with manual cash application. This accelerates the entire reconciliation cycle, which in turn improves a company’s cash flow, provides a clearer view of its financial position, and frees up accounts receivable staff to focus on more value-added activities like collections and customer service.4 This is another example of BofA embedding intelligent automation deep into its clients’ core financial workflows, making its services stickier and more valuable.

## Use Case 10: Global Markets Research & Trading Assistance

Within its high-stakes Global Markets division, Bank of America has deployed specialized AI agents to provide its sales and trading teams with a critical information advantage.2 These internal tools are designed to help professionals navigate the immense volume of data and proprietary research that is essential for making timely and informed decisions in fast-moving markets.

The bank has developed an internal generative AI platform specifically for this purpose. This platform allows sales and trading teams to instantly search, summarize, and synthesize information from the bank’s vast library of industry-leading research reports and market commentary.2 Instead of manually sifting through hundreds of documents, a trader or salesperson can simply ask the platform a question in natural language and receive a concise, synthesized answer, complete with sources. This dramatically reduces the friction of data retrieval and analysis.

In addition to the research platform, the division uses a separate, internally-facing chatbot. This conversational agent is connected to the bank’s proprietary trading systems and databases. It can answer real-time, trading-related questions that arise throughout the day, such as queries about current market depth for a security, trending indicators, historical trading volumes on a specific instrument, or a client’s current risk exposure.4 It can also provide status updates on trades, such as identifying those that are unmatched or have been cancelled.

The impact of these AI agents is to provide traders and salespeople with faster, more intuitive access to the critical information they need to perform their jobs effectively. By eliminating the time spent on manual data hunting, the tools enable these professionals to respond more quickly to market shifts and client requests. This increased speed and clarity in decision-making is a significant competitive advantage in the global markets, where seconds can make a substantial difference in outcomes.11

# Synthesis and Strategic Outlook

Bank of America’s journey with artificial intelligence offers a compelling case study in how a large, incumbent financial institution can successfully operationalize technology to create durable, enterprise-wide value. The ten use cases analyzed in this report are not isolated successes but interconnected outcomes of a coherent, long-term strategy rooted in foundational investment, disciplined execution, and a clear-eyed view of risk and reward. The result is an AI ecosystem that is not only driving significant returns today but is also positioned to be a primary engine of the bank’s growth and competitive differentiation for years to come.

## The ROI of a Decade of AI Investment: A Story in Numbers

The cumulative impact of Bank of America’s sustained, decade-long investment in technology and AI is not theoretical; it is clearly visible in the company’s key performance metrics. By synthesizing the quantitative outcomes discussed throughout this analysis, a holistic picture emerges of a strategy that is delivering substantial and measurable returns for shareholders.

### **Operational Efficiency and Cost Savings:**

The most dramatic impact has been on the bank’s operational leverage. Over the past 15 years, a period marked by intense technological investment, the company’s headcount has been reduced from 300,000 to approximately 212,000.1 This significant reduction in personnel occurred concurrently with massive business growth; for example, deposits in the consumer bank more than doubled from $400 billion to over $900 billion during a similar period.1 This demonstrates a profound increase in productivity, allowing the bank to operate a much larger and more profitable enterprise with a smaller workforce. Process improvements, many of which are driven by AI and automation, have resulted in $6 billion in expense savings and freed up 14.4 million hours of employee capacity through 2024.8

### **Targeted Productivity Gains:**

The impact is also clear at the functional level. The deployment of generative AI coding assistants to 17,000 developers has yielded a 20% efficiency gain, accelerating the bank’s ability to innovate.1 The “Erica for Employees” tool has cut calls to the IT help desk by more than 50%, a direct reduction in internal support costs.5

### **Enhanced Client Engagement and Digital Adoption:**

AI has been central to the bank’s successful digital transformation. The Erica virtual assistant has become a primary channel for customer interaction, handling over 2.7 billion engagements since its launch.3 This has driven deeper digital adoption, with a record 55% of all new sales in 2024 originating through digital channels, up from 49% the previous year.21

These metrics collectively prove that Bank of America’s AI strategy is a core driver of its financial performance. The investments are directly contributing to a more efficient operating model with a lower expense base, a more productive workforce, and deeper, more profitable client relationships that are increasingly digital-first.

## The Next Frontier: The Deliberate Path to Agentic AI

As the industry looks toward the next wave of AI—truly autonomous, agentic systems—Bank of America’s strategic outlook appears to be one of continued, deliberate caution. Executives have confirmed that the bank is “deep into evaluating” more advanced agentic AI but are emphatic that they want to “make sure we have the right controls around its use”.10 This statement is highly consistent with the bank’s established pattern of governed innovation and risk stratification.

While competitors may rush to announce pilots of autonomous agents, BofA’s history strongly suggests it will follow a more measured and internally focused path. The most likely trajectory is that the bank will first introduce more advanced agentic capabilities in highly controlled, internal environments where the potential for error can be contained and managed. Logical starting points would be to further automate the software development lifecycle, using agents to manage code deployment and testing, or to enhance internal operational workflows in areas like compliance monitoring or back-office processing.

This cautious stance is a strategic asset, not a liability. In a risk-averse and highly regulated industry, a reputation for responsible and reliable innovation is paramount. By thoroughly testing and validating agentic AI in lower-risk internal settings first, the bank can build the necessary expertise and safety protocols before ever considering its use in direct, unsupervised client-facing applications. This approach allows BofA to remain at the forefront of technological exploration without jeopardizing the trust it has painstakingly built with its clients and regulators.

## Lessons for the Industry: The BofA Playbook

Bank of America’s successful implementation of AI at scale offers a clear and actionable playbook for other large enterprises seeking to navigate their own technological transformations. The strategy’s success can be distilled into four key lessons:

### **Win the “Boring” Game First:**

The most critical lesson is the importance of prioritizing foundational infrastructure over flashy applications. Bank of America’s success was predicated on the difficult, upfront work of building a clean, unified data layer years before its major AI products were launched.3 This “basement-first” approach is the single greatest accelerator for all future AI development, providing the high-quality fuel that all models require.

### **Build Platforms, Not Projects:**

A project-based approach to AI leads to siloed, non-scalable solutions. By contrast, BofA designed its core AI capabilities, such as the Erica NLP engine, as reusable enterprise platforms.3 This creates compounding value, allowing new, sophisticated applications to be built and deployed across different business lines with increasing speed and efficiency.

### **Stratify Your Risk:**

A one-size-fits-all approach to AI governance is suboptimal. The bank’s bifurcated strategy demonstrates the wisdom of separating AI applications by risk profile. Highly controlled, proprietary, and deterministic AI should be used for high-stakes, regulated functions, while cutting-edge generative AI can be safely embraced for internal productivity gains where the risks are lower and more manageable.1

### **AI’s Biggest Impact is on People:**

The ultimate goal of enterprise AI should not be to simply replace humans, but to augment and empower them. Bank of America has successfully redeployed talent freed by automation into higher-value roles focused on building AI, managing complex client relationships, and providing strategic oversight.3 Furthermore, it uses AI as a tool to train and develop its workforce, investing in the skills of its people to deliver better human-to-human service.2 This human-centric approach ensures that technology serves the broader goals of the enterprise and its most valuable asset—its employees.

# Bank of America's AI Agent Ecosystem: Summary

This in-depth analysis by Dany Kitishian of Klover.AI examines how Bank of America has strategically deployed AI agents across its enterprise. The bank's approach is defined by a decade-long, infrastructure-first philosophy rather than chasing short-term AI trends.

## Strategic Foundation
- BofA spends approximately **$13 billion annually** on technology, with ~$4 billion directed toward new initiatives in 2025.
- Core principle: "Invest once, reuse everywhere" — the proprietary NLP engine developed for Erica® now powers specialized agents across wealth management and corporate banking.
- The bank holds **nearly 1,400 AI and machine learning patents**, the most of any financial services company (a 94% increase since 2022).
- AI is treated as foundational infrastructure ("the basement, not just the branch").

## Key Results
- 20% productivity increase for **17,000 software developers** using generative AI coding tools.
- 50% reduction in IT service calls via "Erica for Employees."
- Erica has managed **2.7 billion+ interactions** with a **98% containment rate** (queries resolved without human escalation).
- 60% of Erica interactions are now proactive insights (not reactive responses).
- $6 billion in expense savings through process improvements; 14.4 million hours of employee capacity freed up.

## The 10 AI Agent Use Cases

### Client-Facing Agents
1. **Erica® Virtual Assistant** — Consumer banking flagship; 20 million active users; handles balance checks, transfers, card management, and proactive alerts.
2. **"Ask Merrill" & "Ask Private Bank"** — Wealth management assistants for high-net-worth clients, built on Erica's engine.
3. **AI-Enhanced Digital Mortgage** — Blends AI-driven back-end automation with strategically placed human expert touchpoints.

### Internal & Operational Agents
4. **Erica for Employees** — Internal gen AI assistant for HR, IT, and administrative tasks across 210,000+ employees.
5. **GenAI for Software Development** — Coding assistants for 17,000 programmers yielding 20% efficiency gains.
6. **AI Conversation Simulators** — Training tool for client-facing staff; over 1 million simulations completed annually.

### Specialized Financial Agents
7. **CashPro® AI Suite** — Corporate treasury tools including CashPro Forecasting (reduces cash forecasting from a week to minutes), CashPro Chat, and CashPro Insights.
8. **AI Fraud & Risk Management** — Behavioral profiling, real-time transaction scoring, and network analysis to detect fraud and assess credit risk.
9. **Intelligent Receivables®** — Automates B2B invoice matching and reconciliation using AI and OCR.
10. **Global Markets AI Assistant** — Internal gen AI platform for sales and trading teams to search, summarize, and synthesize proprietary research.

## Risk Management Approach
BofA employs a **bifurcated strategy**: Erica explicitly avoids generative AI/LLMs, using proprietary supervised machine learning with pre-defined answers for reliability. Meanwhile, cutting-edge generative AI is deployed aggressively in controlled internal environments (coding, research synthesis).

## Strategic Outlook
The bank is "deep into evaluating" more advanced agentic AI but emphasizes the need for proper controls. Future deployment is expected to follow the established pattern — starting in controlled internal environments before any client-facing use.

## Key Lessons for Industry
1. Prioritize foundational infrastructure (data unification) over flashy applications.
2. Build reusable platforms, not isolated projects.
3. Stratify AI risk by use case.
4. Use AI to augment and empower humans, not replace them.

*AI solution modernizes the full lifecycle of client engagement*

*New capability can save financial advisors up to four hours per meeting across millions of meetings annually*

**Key Points**

* **Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank introduce an AI-powered meeting solution** to transform the advisor-client experience.
* **The solution's intelligent workflow tools** help deliver meeting prep materials, summaries, and actionable next steps.

NEW YORK, March 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bank of America's Wealth Management businesses, Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank, today announced the full-scale rollout of AI‑Powered Meeting Journey, an integrated solution that helps optimize how advisors and their teams prepare for, conduct, and follow up on client meetings. The streamlined meeting experience enables advisors to redirect meaningful time toward strategic planning and deeper client engagement.

*"AI**‑**Powered Meeting Journey represents a meaningful advancement in how the wealth management industry uses AI,"* said **Patricio Diaz, Chief Operating Officer at Merrill**. *"This latest solution empowers advisors to shift capacity toward activities that drive business growth and strengthen how we serve clients."*

**AI-Powered Meeting Journey Core Capabilities**

* **Meeting Prep:** Quickly searches and consolidates client relationship insights and recent activity into ready‑to‑use prep materials to enable more personalized and productive client conversations.
* **Meeting Summarization:** With client consent, acts as an AI notetaker during virtual meetings, capturing discussion highlights and creating a shareable meeting summary.
* **Meeting Follow****‑****Up:** Summarizes meeting decisions and next steps based on meeting notes, generating tasks and documentation.

*"Early users of the Meeting Prep and Meeting Summarization capabilities are already seeing significant improvements in their workflows*," said **Shimna Sameer, Head of Products, Solutions & Platforms at Bank of America Private Bank**. **Q: Why is AI a strategic priority for Bank of America's wealth management businesses?**  
A: AI enables us to deliver more personalized, efficient, and intuitive experiences for clients. AI increases advisors' capacity to focus on deeper client conversations, strategic planning, and long‑term relationship building.

**Q:** **What's next for AI in Merrill and Private Bank?**  
A: We will continue expanding AI capabilities that strengthen advisor‑client relationships. Future advancements will focus on accelerating advisor efficiency, enhancing personalization and supporting more proactive guidance delivered through our high‑tech, high‑touch approach.

**Q: What role will advisors continue to play as AI becomes more widely used in wealth management?**A: The role of the advisor will always remain central to the client relationship. While AI can enhance efficiency, it cannot replace the valuable judgment, empathy, understanding and personal connection advisors bring to clients.

**Q: Has Bank of America been an early adopter of AI?**A: Bank of America has been investing in AI for more than a decade, taking a disciplined approach to developing and deploying AI solutions effectively and responsibly at scale. We work to ensure our AI solutions and investments are reusable across different areas of the business. For example, in 2018, we launched Erica®, the first widely adopted AI‑driven virtual financial assistant. Since then, clients have interacted with Erica more than 3.2 billion times. We leveraged the same underlying technology to launch ask MERRILL® and ask Private Banking®, helping advisors and employees quickly find information, connect with colleagues, and better serve clients.

Bank of America is one of the world's leading financial institutions, serving individual consumers, small and middle-market businesses and large corporations with a full range of banking, investing, asset management and other financial and risk management products and services. args.summary:
On March 26, 2026, Bank of America's wealth management businesses—Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank—announced the full-scale rollout of AI-Powered Meeting Journey, an integrated AI solution designed to optimize the full lifecycle of client meetings. The solution helps advisors prepare for, conduct, and follow up on client meetings, potentially saving financial advisors up to four hours per meeting across millions of meetings annually.

**Core Capabilities:**
- **Meeting Prep:** Searches and consolidates client relationship insights and recent activity into ready-to-use prep materials.
- **Meeting Summarization:** With client consent, acts as an AI notetaker during virtual meetings, capturing discussion highlights and creating shareable summaries.
- **Meeting Follow-Up:** Summarizes decisions and next steps, generating tasks and documentation.

**Key Context:**
- Bank of America invests $13.5 billion annually on technology, with $4 billion dedicated to new initiatives like AI.
- The company has been investing in AI for over a decade, launching Erica in 2018 (3.2 billion+ client interactions), and leveraging similar technology for ask MERRILL and ask Private Banking.
- The firm emphasizes that AI enhances efficiency but cannot replace the judgment, empathy, and personal connection of advisors.
- Future AI advancements will focus on accelerating advisor efficiency, enhancing personalization, and supporting more proactive guidance.

Quotes from executives Patricio Diaz (COO at Merrill) and Shimna Sameer (Head of Products at Bank of America Private Bank) highlight the solution's potential to shift advisor capacity toward strategic planning and deeper client engagement.

# AI Adoption by BofA’s Global Workforce Improves Productivity, Client Service

More than ninety percent90% of employees use AI-driven virtual assistant for increased efficiency

[Leer en español](/content/newsroom/press-releases/2025/04/la-implementacion-de-ia-por-parte-de-la-fuerza-laboral-global-de.html)

CHARLOTTE,North Carolina N.C., LONDON, HONG KONG – Bank of America uses innovative technology to meet and anticipate the needs of its clients and 213,000 employees. For many years, this commitment has carried through in its approach to AI and machine learning. The technology is embedded today across the company’s business lines and areas including global technology, operations, and training.

*“AI is having a transformative effect on employee efficiency and operational excellence,”* said **Aditya Bhasin, Chief Technology & Information Officer at Bank of America**. *“Our use of AI at scale and around the world enables us to further enhance our capabilities, improve employee productivity and client service, and drive business growth.”*

Seven years ago, in 2018, Bank of America launched Erica®, the first widely adopted AI-driven virtual financial assistant, within its mobile app. Since then, clients have interacted with Erica more than [2.5 billion times](https://newsroom.bankofamerica.com/content/newsroom/press-releases/2025/02/digital-interactions-by-bofa-clients-surge-to-over-26-billion--u.html), with 20 million clients now actively using the virtual assistant.

Bank of America’s approach to AI includes human oversight, transparency, and accountability for all outcomes. In addition to recently shared [examples](https://newsroom.bankofamerica.com/content/newsroom/press-releases/2024/10/ai-patents-at-bofa-increase-94--since-2022.html) of how AI benefits clients and employees, our employees’ use of AI continues to expand in areas such as:

* **Erica for Employees** – Building upon Erica’s success, in 2020, Bank of America launched Erica for Employees, an AI-driven internal virtual assistant which was rapidly adopted during the pandemic by employees seeking technology support in areas such as mobile device password reset, device activation, and many others. In 2023, the functionality was expanded to assist with additional topics such as where to review health benefits, locate payroll and tax forms, and more.  
     
   Today, over 90% of employees use Erica for Employees, with the virtual assistant having reduced calls into the I TIT service desk by more than 50%. The capabilities will expand this year to offer enhanced search and assistance across a broader set of topics – including answers to employee questions about Bank of America products and services – with plans to leverage both AI and generative AI (GenAI).
* ***ask* MERRILL® and *ask* PRIVATE BANK®** – Leveraging the technology behind Erica, these tools help Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank teams efficiently curate information to deliver superior client experiences. When needed, the chat functionality can also connect teams with experts at the bank for help with more complex requests. In 2024, there were more than 23 million interactions with *ask* MERRILL and *ask* PRIVATE BANK, an increase of 1 million over 2023, helping employees more proactively connect with clients about timely and relevant opportunities.
* **The Academy** – Bank of America’s onboarding, education, and professional development organization uses AI to provide interactive coaching through conversation simulators that enable teammates to practice different types of client interactions and increase proficiency through real-time feedback. Employees completed over 1 million simulations last year, with many noting that practicing client conversations helps them deliver better and more consistent service.

Additional AI deployments underway helping to increase employee productivity and improve client service include:

* **Coding assistance** – Bank of America software developers are using a GenAI-based tool to assist with code writing and optimization, through which they have experienced efficiency gains of over twenty percent20%.
* **Preparing for client meetings** – Developing materials in preparation for meetings with current and prospective business clients can take several hours per meeting. AI helps automate and standardize the creation of drafts of materials for meetings with Bank of America Business Banking and Global Commercial Banking clients, with the opportunity for employees to reallocate tens of thousands of hours per year to client engagement and growth.
* **Contact center optimization** – A modernized desktop tool leveraging AI proactively provides guided assistance to customer service specialists in Bank of America contact centers, enabling them to deliver a more personalized client experience, increase client satisfaction, and reduce call handling times.
* **Research summaries** – An internally-developed GenAI platform enables the Global Markets sales and trading team to search, summarize, and synthesize our industry-leading research and market commentary more quickly and efficiently.
* **Capturing client feedback** – A Gen AI capability to summarize call recordings designed to increase call center efficiency and ensure the company remains in tune with clients' needs and improves their experiences.

## AI Patent Portfolio

Bank of America holds nearly 7,400 granted patents and pending patent applications, the most United StatesU.S. granted patents of any financial services company. More than 1,200 of these patents are AI and machine learning focused – representing seventeen percent17% of the patent portfolio – and more than half have already been granted.

Other technology categories in which new patents were granted last year include information security, online and mobile banking, payments, data analytics, and augmented and virtual reality. This is thanks to the company’s more than 7,800 talented inventors in 14 countries and 42 United StatesU.S. states, and a culture that empowers teammates to explore and develop innovative solutions for individuals and businesses globally.

Bank of America spends thirteen billion dollars$13 billion annually on technology, of which approximately four billion dollars$4 billion will be directed to new technology initiatives in 2025.

## Bank of America

Bank of America is one of the world’s leading financial institutions, serving individual consumers, small and middle-market businesses and large corporations with a full range of banking, investing, asset management and other financial and risk management products and services. The company provides unmatched convenience in the United StatesU.S., serving approximately 69 million consumer and small business clients with 3,700 retail financial centers, approximately 15,000 ATMs (automated teller machines) and award-winning digital banking with approximately 58 million verified digital users. Bank of America is a global leader in wealth management, corporate and investment banking and trading across a broad range of asset classes, serving corporations, governments, institutions and individuals around the world. Bank of America offers industry-leading support to approximately 4 million small business households through a suite of innovative, easy-to-use online products and services. The company serves clients through operations across the United StatesU.S., its territories and more than 35 countries. Bank of America Corporation stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (New York Stock ExchangeNYSE: B A CBAC).

[New] Bank of America gives Merrill Lynch an AI makeover Hello LinkedIn financial services/fintech/venture community. I was quoted in an article this week entitled "Bank of America gives Merrill Lynch an AI makeover" by [American Banker](https://www.linkedin.com/company/american-banker?trk=public_post-text)'s Executive Editor [Penny Crosman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pennycrosman?trk=public_post-text). Here's the full link [https://lnkd.in/g-ndgMF2](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Flnkd%2Ein%2Fg-ndgMF2&urlhash=4Nc1&trk=public_post-text) and highlights: ✏️ BofA is rolling out new AI tools across Merrill Lynch and Private Bank that work inside Salesforce and Zoom to help advisors prepare for meetings, summarize conversations, manage follow-ups, and organize next steps. ✏️ The rollout is happening at major scale: 25,000 Merrill advisors across 500+ offices are getting the tools now, while the Private Bank’s 4,800 bankers in 100 offices across 42 U.S. markets began receiving key features this month, with more coming in Q2. ✏️ The strategic goal is to help advisors scale amid rising client expectations, an expected $124 trillion wealth transfer, and a projected advisor shortage over the next decade, while reducing administrative burden and improving responsiveness. ✏️ The new “meeting journey” includes daily planning tools, AI-generated meeting prep based on CRM data, Zoom-powered meeting summaries, post-meeting task and opportunity capture, and a conversational assistant that can search and summarize client or book-of-business information. ✏️ Bank of America is positioning AI as a workflow enhancer rather than a replacement for enterprise software or human advisors, with early users saying tasks that once took 45 minutes to four hours can now be compressed into just a few minutes, freeing advisors to focus more on strategy and client relationships. Thank you [Penny Crosman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pennycrosman?trk=public_post-text) for including my thoughts on BofA's AI launch of these new advisor tools. They demonstrate how AI has quickly become critical relationship infrastructure. AI-infused workflows will continue to take on a larger role in sectors of our business model like wealth management because they make relationship management much more efficient (and in the end, surprisingly more personal because they retain knowledge of every context and conversation). See the comments for more of my thoughts on this, and please, take a minute to add your own. Have a great weekend!

A recent prospect told me: "I'm spending 70% of my time on operations instead of client relationships, but I can't afford to hire a team." It's the classic solo advisor bottleneck. Your clients expect the comprehensive service of a 10-person firm while you're running every workflow yourself. This isn't just inefficient. It's a structural vulnerability. Without a back-office team, market updates are included in quarterly reviews at best. Your client's portfolio drifting toward over-concentration doesn't care that your next review is six weeks away. But here's what's changing: AI orchestration is bridging this gap. Not by replacing you but by running the background workflows that eat late night hours. The key is human-AI orchestration, not automation for its own sake. Three specific workflows where one-person RIAs are finding leverage: 1. Data aggregation automation: AI pulls and normalizes client financial data automatically, eliminating the manual compile time that eats your mornings. Expect 15% reduction in data analysis time and 25% improvement in validation efficiency. 2. Real-time monitoring workflows: This is the critical bridge most competitors miss. AI watches the markets continuously for anomalies, risks, and breaches — flagging issues at 9am instead of at quarter-end. 3. On-demand scenario modeling: Run plan scenarios when needed, not just at annual reviews. AI handles the computation; you provide the wisdom and client conversation. One case study worth noting: WealthPlus Advisors implemented AI-driven client analysis and saw a 35% increase in client satisfaction, 20% improvement in retention, and a 25% boost in new client acquisitions within six months. This isn't technology for technology's sake. It's about giving the solo advisor the operational capacity of a team — specifically the monitoring, data, and scenario workflows that a back-office would otherwise run. If automated, which workflow would make the biggest difference in your practice tomorrow? [Bank of America](https://www.linkedin.com/company/bank-of-america?trk=public_post_reshare-text) has started deploying AI agents to around 1,000 financial advisers, putting the technology directly into client-facing advisory roles rather than keeping it in back-office or productivity functions. This is a meaningful step and worth understanding clearly, because it represents something different from what most large institutions have been doing with AI so far. The platform, built on [Salesforce](https://www.linkedin.com/company/salesforce?trk=public_post_reshare-text)'s Agentforce, helps advisers handle client queries, prepare recommendations, and manage daily workflows. It sits alongside, not instead of, the human adviser. But the positioning matters. Financial advisers in wealth management sit at the centre of client relationships. Embedding AI into that role is a different governance and accountability decision than deploying it in coding or internal operations. To understand the scale of what Bank of America has already built, their virtual assistant Erica now handles work equivalent to around 11,000 employees. All 18,000 of their software developers use AI coding tools that have improved productivity by roughly 20%. This is not a bank experimenting cautiously with a pilot. It is one of the most AI-embedded institutions in financial services, moving the technology progressively closer to its most consequential client interactions. [J.P. Morgan](https://www.linkedin.com/company/jpmorgan?trk=public_post_reshare-text), [Wells Fargo](https://www.linkedin.com/company/wellsfargo?trk=public_post_reshare-text), and [Goldman Sachs](https://www.linkedin.com/company/goldman-sachs?trk=public_post_reshare-text) are all moving in similar directions, though at different paces and with different approaches. The common thread is the same: increase output without expanding headcount at the same rate, and do it in a way that keeps human oversight in place while the technology proves itself in production. For risk and compliance teams in financial services, two questions now sit at the centre of this transition. First, when an AI agent contributes to a financial recommendation that later proves wrong or harmful, how is accountability established and who carries it? Second, are the oversight mechanisms being built alongside these deployments designed for the scale and speed at which agents actually operate, or are they legacy frameworks applied to a new category of tool? The technology is clearly capable. The governance infrastructure around it is the part that most institutions are still figuring out in real time.

Last Friday we launched [RDC.AI](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=http%3A%2F%2FRDC%2EAI&urlhash=TJDN&trk=public_post-text) Platform v10.0, the same day the US banking agencies (OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC) jointly issued revised Model Risk Management guidance (SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13a). The timing wasn't planned. It was fitting. For non-US readers: this is the revised US MRM standard, the successor to SR 11-7. What's striking is what the new guidance deliberately leaves outside its scope. Generative and agentic AI are expressly out, but banks are still expected to apply their own governance practices to them, using the guidance's principles as the starting point. The responsibility for governing agentic AI sits squarely with the bank. That's the arc we've been on from day one. RDC's Glass Box already brings predictive AI inside a governed, explainable decisioning loop: audit-ready, bankers in the loop. v10 extends that discipline into the agentic layer. Three moves in v10: Tighter control on how data is shared and accessed across the platform, so banks can apply fine-grained entitlements by portfolio, team, and role. A harder boundary around sensitive data, no sensitive data ever leaves for a foundation model, by design. A smoother flow from data to model to decision. New decision-strategy building and reporting capabilities let analysts build, iterate, and evidence a strategy in the same view, making evidence-based, data-driven decisioning the default. Taken together, these set the stage for the next leg of the journey: a governed agentic AI workbench for regulated industries. All of it in service of one goal: giving bankers AI they can trust, so they can know more, do more, and grow more! args.summary: Bank of America (BofA) is rolling out new AI tools across its Merrill Lynch and Private Bank divisions, as highlighted in a LinkedIn post by Bradley Leimer (who was quoted in an American Banker article by Penny Crosman). The AI tools work inside Salesforce and Zoom to help advisors prepare for meetings, summarize conversations, manage follow-ups, and organize next steps. The rollout is at major scale: 25,000 Merrill advisors across 500+ offices are receiving the tools, while the Private Bank's 4,800 bankers in 100 offices across 42 U.S. markets began receiving features this month, with more coming in Q2. Strategic goals include helping advisors scale amid rising client expectations, an expected $124 trillion wealth transfer, and a projected advisor shortage over the next decade. The "meeting journey" includes daily planning tools, AI-generated meeting prep from CRM data, Zoom-powered summaries, post-meeting task capture, and a conversational assistant for client information. Bank of America positions AI as a workflow enhancer, not a replacement for human advisors, with early users reporting tasks that took 45 minutes to 4 hours now compressed into minutes. The post includes community discussion praising AI as "relationship infrastructure" that makes wealth management more personal by retaining context, while noting this is part of a broader industry trend with competitors like J.P. Morgan, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and Jump also deploying AI tools for financial advisors. Governance and accountability questions around AI in client-facing roles are also raised.

NEW YORK – Citi Wealth’s Data, Analytics & Innovation team has launched two new exciting innovations, Advisor Insights and AskWealth, both designed to enhance the way in which Citi Wealth communicates with its clients.

Through Advisor Insights, Citi Wealth bankers and advisors will have access to a tailored dashboard featuring timely messages about market turns, portfolios and current events. With the application, more clients will experience faster and deeper connections around useful content and alerts, including insights from Citi Wealth’s award-winning Chief Investment Office.

AskWealth is Citi’s GenAI-powered conversational assistant that gives service teams, advisors and managers instant answers across the Wealth ecosystem. With the help of AskWealth, service teams can resolve client inquiries with ease and speed, and advisors can access timely market insights and research to answer questions related to their clients and portfolios.

“Advisor Insights and AskWealth are pivotal steps forward in the expansion of Citi Wealth’s AI, data and technological capabilities,” said Joe Bonanno, Head of Data, Analytics & Innovation. “These platforms will save hours of time for our advisors, bankers and service teams while reinforcing for clients the personal and high-touch experience that is a tradition at our firm.”

Advisor Insights is currently in pilot with advisors in the Citigold and Citi Private Client North America business. Usage will be expanded to North America Citi Private Bankers and international colleagues in Q4 2025 and Q1 2026. AskWealth is now available to Citi Wealth colleagues around the globe following a successful launch in Asia.

“These new AI-powered tools are gamechangers for Citi Wealth. They give our advisors sharper insights, streamline how we work, and open new possibilities for serving clients with speed and precision,” said Andy Sieg, Head of Wealth, crediting the division’s Data, Analytics & Innovation, Wealth Technology and Platform & Experience teams. “We’re excited about the impact AI will have on our clients and colleagues alike as we continue to lead the industry into the future.”

If you are interested in a live demo of Advisor Insights and/or AskWealth, or would like to speak with Joe Bonanno, Head of Data, Analytics & Innovation at Citi Wealth, please reach out to the media contact below.

[Citi Wealth](https://www.citigroup.com/global/businesses/wealth) unveiled several new technology capabilities aimed at empowering advisors to deliver a more proactive, data-driven and personalized client experience. The new tools move Citi Wealth closer to its goal of building a unified, AI-driven layer of intelligence to support a client’s entire financial lifecycle.

The launch includes Portfolio Intelligence – a client-facing tool designed to provide Citi Wealth clients with swift and personalized portfolio insights at the click of a button. The rollout also features several advisor-first resources, including AskWealth CIO, Client 360 and CitiScribe, innovations aimed at streamlining advisor workflows and enriching client interactions.

“Citi Wealth aims to set the industry standard for client advice and service,” said Andy Sieg, Head of Wealth. “Our objective is to create an ecosystem of AI-powered tools that scale the identification of investment opportunities, spot risks and provide guidance for next steps.”

Other initiatives are in the works, according to Joe Bonanno, Head of Citi Wealth’s Data, Analytics and Innovation team. One priority is simplifying and modernizing the account opening process. Bonanno said his team is working with the firm’s major technology partners, including Google Cloud and Palantir, on this and other projects.

**Here are the tools currently in implementation:**

**Portfolio Intelligence: A Unified, Insight Driven Client View**

Portfolio Intelligence offers clients a holistic view of their portfolios in an easy-to-use interface. The platform integrates positions, performance metrics and market insights from Citi Wealth’s Chief Investment Office into a single digital experience. Through an app, it will also enable advisors to deliver personalized messages, thus strengthening relationships and informed decision-making through continuous engagement. Portfolio Intelligence is already available to Citi Private Bank clients in North America and will expand to Citi Private Bank clients globally in Q2 and all Wealth clients by year-end.

**AskWealth CIO: Chief Investment Office Insights for Advisors**

AskWealth CIO, an expansion of the firm’s successful AskWealth platform, provides advisors with access to the latest insights from Citi Wealth’s Chief Investment Office. Through a conversational chat interface, advisors can retrieve CIO perspectives sourced directly from the firm’s most recent reports. This platform is currently in pilot within the Citigold, Wealth at Work and Citi Private Bank businesses in North America, with an expansion planned to the remaining regions in the coming weeks.

**Client 360: A Comprehensive View of Client Portfolios**

Client 360 is a unified internal platform that consolidates disparate client data into a single, seamless view. Advisors can access holdings, positions, call logs, opportunities, interests and a host of related data points on one screen – allowing for faster and more personalized engagement. It is in pilot with a select group of advisors in Citi Private Bank and Wealth at Work in North America – with full rollouts to these segments planned for this month. All Citi Wealth colleagues will gain access in Q2 2026.

**CitiScribe: An AI Note-Taking Tool for Advisors**

CitiScribe is an AI powered note taking tool that summarizes client discussions and key points to eliminate manual documentation by advisors and their teams, thus improving accuracy, timeliness and follow up. CitiScribe rolled out to all Wealth advisors in North America in Q1 2026.

# Transforming Wealth Management Using AI At Citi

By[Randy Bean](https://www.forbes.com/sites/randybean/ "https://www.forbes.com/sites/randybean/"),

 Randy Bean is a noted Senior Advisor, Author, Speaker, Founder, & CEO.

Citi is revolutionizing its wealth management business by deeply integrating AI to enhance client advice and advisor productivity. The firm, led by CEO Jane Fraser, champions "Wealth Intelligence" through a unified data foundation, enabling personalized advice and real-time insights. Key innovations include "Citi Sky," developed with Google Cloud and DeepMind, which offers interactive video insights to clients, alongside tools like "Advisor Insights." Citi fosters an AI-driven culture by embedding these tools directly into advisor workflows, built collaboratively with advisors, and partners with leading tech firms. The company prioritizes responsible AI, transparency, and human oversight to ensure trust and scalability, viewing AI as a core driver for future growth and an elevated client experience.

Wealth Management Advisors

Randy Bean

AI is reshaping the global wealth management industry. From client advice to advisor productivity, AI is augmenting the role of financial advisors across the industry.

I recently discussed how AI is transforming wealth management with Andy Sieg, Citi’s Head of Wealth, and Joe Bonanno, Head of Wealth Intelligence, at Citi (Citigroup, NYSE: C), one of the big four U.S. banking institutions. Sieg brings a long history in wealth management to his role, having led the wealth management function at Merrill Lynch for over a decade. Bonanno previously spent over a decade at Morgan Stanley, where he led wealth management analytics and data.

Citi has a long and illustrious history. Founded in 1812 as City Bank of New York, Citi has been at the forefront of the U.S. and global financial services industry for over 200 years. Today, Citi operates with five core businesses – with Wealth being one. Citi Wealth brings together the entire continuum of wealth clients through three core offerings, Citi Private Bank, U.S. Retail Banking & Citigold, and Wealth at Work.

AI is integrated across Citi’s entire Wealth business, for the benefit of all employees and clients. Sieg explains, “The mandate of Wealth Intelligence, which comprises data, AI, and experience, is to push the business forward – responsibly, decisively, and at a pace we like to call the new ’*CitiSpee*d.’ In fact, our CEO Jane Fraser is the number one advocate for AI innovation across the firm.” Adds Bonanno, “Leadership engagement shows up in how we operate, not just what we say. We measure value through outcomes, not activity. Are insights being used? Are they improving advisor productivity? Are they strengthening relationships, enhancing the client experience, and delivering overall better performance?”

### Using Data and AI to Enhance Wealth Intelligence at Citi

Citi Wealth is focused on rapidly transforming advanced ideas into business tools, using high-quality data, strong governance, and AI built to perform at-scale. “Wealth Intelligence is about anticipating client needs, personalizing advice and enabling advisors to act with precision in real time,” explains Bonanno. “We’ve built a unified *One Wealth* data foundation that connects transactions, holdings, behaviors, and external signals into a single intelligence layer.”

“We view data, analytics, and AI as compounding strategic assets, not infrastructure.” Our advantage comes from connecting a deeply governed data ecosystem – spanning wealth, banking, and payments – into a single intelligence layer. This allows us to see signals others simply can’t, from portfolio activity to real-world behaviors.” Bonanno continues, “What makes this powerful is reuse. The same intelligence that informs an advisor conversation also drives client engagement, personalization, and product strategy. This is where scale meets precision – and where data becomes a true competitive advantage.”

MORE FOR YOU

Sieg elaborates: “In Citi Wealth, intelligence is embedded directly into our platforms, not bolted on, ensuring that innovation translates into action. For us, it’s all about a new layer of intelligence in wealth management that will serve clients and advisors alike.”

### AI Transformation at Citi Wealth

AI transformation within Citi Wealth is manifesting itself through the introduction of a series of new, AI-driven, capabilities. “Our latest innovation – [*Citi Sky*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GhkLgpJCh9Y) – is a great example; we believe it will change the model of wealth management,” says Sieg. “Developed in partnership with Google Cloud and Google DeepMind, *Citi Sky* adds a new ’channel’ to our business, providing U.S. clients with tailored information and insights in an interactive video format. They will be able to ’ask more’ of us.”

Bonanno elaborates: “Our data foundation powers tools like [*Advisor Insights*, *AskWealth*](https://www.citigroup.com/global/news/press-release/2026/citi-wealth-deploys-ai-powered-technology-to-enhance-client-experience), and *Citi Sky* -- moving us from static campaigns to continuous, real-time engagement.” He continues, “*Citi Sky* is a defining example of where we’re going. It brings frontier AI into wealth management at enterprise scale, combining Citi’s data and domain expertise with some of the most advanced AI capabilities in the world. It turns wealth management from a scheduled interaction into a continuous relationship – producing better decisions, deeper relationships, and stronger results for our clients. This isn’t experimental. It’s scaled, integrated, and already having impact.”

### Building an AI-driven Business Culture at Citi Wealth

Success with AI depends on good data, and also on the development of an AI-driven business culture. “It starts with putting powerful AI tools directly into everyday workflows – tools advisors can actually use to improve speed and impact,” notes Sieg. “We think of AI as a high-performing engine that powers our business. That’s why we’re investing aggressively in both talent and execution to support it, and the firm is deploying additional tools as well.”

Bonanno elaborates, “Building on Andy’s point, culture doesn’t change just because you introduce AI – it changes when people see results. Our focus has been embedding AI directly into advisor workflows in ways that are intuitive and immediately valuable. We built this *with* our advisors, not *for* them. Their feedback shaped these platforms end-to-end, always with the goal of improving how we serve clients”

“And we’re not doing it alone,” notes Sieg. “By partnering with world‑class technology leaders like Google Cloud and Palantir, we’re widening and lengthening the runway and accelerating how quickly we bring new capabilities to market.”

### Responsible AI as a Cornerstone for Citi Wealth

Citi Wealth leadership sees the next stage of AI being about scaling intelligence across every meaningful client moment. “We’re moving from interfaces to intelligence, and from transactions to outcomes,” says Bonanno. “This means embedding AI deeper into planning, engagement, and follow-through – so every interaction is informed by real-time context. At the same time, we’re standardizing our data and AI platforms so we can move faster with consistency and control,

Bonanno explains, “Responsible AI enables scale. Our ability to move quickly today is built on a deeply governed data foundation. We apply transparency and human oversight across every use case. Trust is what allows AI to scale in Wealth Management.”

### Looking to an AI Future at Citi Wealth

Looking ahead to what’s next with AI at Citi Wealth, Sieg reflects, “Data, analytics, tech and AI aren’t support functions at Citi – they’re how we propel the business, fuel growth and win.” He adds, “Used responsibly and at-scale, they differentiate us, accelerate growth, and elevate the client experience. And we’re just getting started.”

Citi is transforming its wealth management business through deep integration of AI, as discussed in a Forbes article by Randy Bean featuring interviews with Andy Sieg (Citi's Head of Wealth) and Joe Bonanno (Head of Wealth Intelligence). Citi Wealth operates through three core offerings: Citi Private Bank, U.S. Retail Banking & Citigold, and Wealth at Work. The firm has built a unified "One Wealth" data foundation that connects transactions, holdings, behaviors, and external signals into a single intelligence layer.

Key AI innovations include:
- **Citi Sky**: Developed with Google Cloud and Google DeepMind, providing U.S. clients with tailored information and insights in interactive video format.
- **Advisor Insights** and **AskWealth**: Tools that move from static campaigns to continuous, real-time engagement.
- AI tools embedded directly into advisor workflows, built collaboratively with advisors.

CEO Jane Fraser is described as the "number one advocate for AI innovation across the firm." Citi partners with technology leaders like Google Cloud and Palantir. The company emphasizes responsible AI with transparency and human oversight as cornerstones for trust and scalability. Citi views AI not as a support function but as a core driver for business growth, differentiation, and enhanced client experience.

# Wells Fargo introduces AI Teammate, bringing AI-powered support to the advisor experience

07/15/2026

Share

[Download PDF Format (opens in new window)](https://newsroom.wf.com/news-releases/news-details/2026/Wells-Fargo-introduces-AI-Teammate-bringing--AI-powered-support-to-the-advisor-experience/default.aspx)

**_[Watch a video (01:11)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yNHXAzUo5oY) to see how AI Teammate helps make everyday work simpler for advisors and their teams. [Video transcript available here (PDF).](https://newsroom.wf.com/files/videos/transcript/External\_AI-Teammate\_video-transcript\_A04.pdf)_**

**SAN FRANCISCO** – Wells Fargo today announced the launch of AI Teammate, a new artificial intelligence (AI)–powered capability embedded within [Advisor Gateway](https://newsroom.wf.com/news-releases/news-details/2026/Wells-Fargo-launches-Advisor-Gateway-for-financial-advisors/default.aspx) that helps streamline how financial advisors, client associates, and support teams access information and complete everyday work.

AI Teammate marks a milestone in Wells Fargo’s broader effort to apply AI in practical, high-impact ways for the benefit of advisors. By connecting advisors to the information, tools, and workflows they use every day, AI Teammate helps reduce friction, accelerate decision-making, and enable more time for client engagement.

Over time, capabilities will expand to help advisors uncover new opportunities, prepare for client conversations with personalized insights, and focus on the actions that can strengthen client relationships and support practice growth. AI Teammate will be available to financial advisors across all Wealth & Investment Management (WIM) advisor channels, including independent advisors who are part of Wells Fargo Advisors Financial Network, “FiNet.”

“We are making significant investments in AI and technology to empower advisors, grow client relationships, and gain market share,” said Sol Gindi, head of the WIM Client Relationship Group and Wells Fargo Advisors. “AI Teammate builds on the foundation of Advisor Gateway and represents an important step in our broader vision for AI. We have a pipeline of additional AI tools in development that are all geared to helping our people focus on clients, deepen relationships, and deliver everything Wells Fargo has to offer more effectively.”

## Bringing information, tools, and workflows together

AI Teammate introduces a chat-based experience embedded within the firm’s central technology platform, Advisor Gateway. It enables users to ask questions in plain language, retrieve answers quickly, and take action.

In its initial phase, AI Teammate helps teams search and summarize information from WFA’s core resource center to:

*   Find answers faster with plain-language search
*   Quickly summarize product, process, and workflow information
*   Move work forward with guided workflows and clear next steps
*   Spend less time navigating multiple pages by bringing relevant information together in one place

This approach reflects a broader industry shift toward simplifying the advisor experience by applying AI to remove friction from high-frequency tasks and improve day-to-day productivity.

“By embedding AI into natural workflow entry points, we can help our teams work more efficiently and make better use of the insights available to them,” said Andre Mansour, head of WIM AI.

“AI Teammate advances the progress we’ve made in delivering a more seamless and intuitive advisor experience,” said Eve Varner, head of the WIM Chief Product Office. “It’s about making the tools advisors use every day more connected, more useful, and ultimately more effective in helping them serve clients.”

Wealth & Investment Management (WIM) offers financial products and services through bank and brokerage affiliates of Wells Fargo & Company and is one of the largest wealth managers in the U.S., with $2.4 trillion in client assets.
