Bank if America tower in Miami. Credit: Getty/ Art Wager

Bank of America’s wealth management arm launches an integrated AI suite to automate meeting prep and follow-up for Merrill and Private Bank teams

[Bank of America (BofA)](https://fintechmagazine.com/top10/top-10-global-banks) has announced the full-scale launch of AI-Powered Meeting Journey, a new digital ecosystem designed to overhaul the administrative lifecycle of client interactions.

Rolled out across Merrill Wealth Management and [Bank of America Private Bank](https://fintechmagazine.com/company/bank-of-america), the solution aims to eliminate the manual “heavy lifting” that is traditionally associated with high-touch financial advising.

By integrating AI directly into the advisor workflow, the firm is looking to reclaim lost hours spent on prep and documentation.

The platform provides a streamlined experience that allows wealth teams to pivot away from administrative overhead and towards strategic planning.

Merrill Lynch is the investment arm of Bank of America. Credit: Getty

## Automating the advisor workflow

The AI-Powered Meeting Journey is built on three core pillars: preparation, summarisation and follow-up.

During the prep phase, the system aggregates client relationship insights and recent activity into ready-to-use materials.

This ensures advisors enter conversations with a comprehensive view of the client’s current position without needing to manually hunt through disparate datasets.

For the meeting itself, the tool acts as an AI notetaker during virtual sessions – provided the client gives consent – to capture highlights. Post-meeting, it generates summaries and automatically drafts follow-up tasks and documentation based on the discussed decisions.

Patricio Diaz, Chief Operating Officer at [Merrill](https://fintechmagazine.com/company/merill-lynch) notes: “AI‑Powered Meeting Journey represents a meaningful advancement in how the wealth management industry uses AI.

“This latest solution empowers advisors to shift capacity toward activities that drive business growth and strengthen how we serve clients.”

Patricio Diaz, Chief Operating Officer at Merrill

## Driving operational excellence

The rollout comes at a time when the broader fintech sector is under pressure to prove the ROI of generative AI investments. Early data from the pilot phase suggests that the tech is already making a dent in advisor workloads.

“Early users of the Meeting Prep and Meeting Summarization capabilities are already seeing [significant improvements in their workflows,](https://fintechmagazine.com/news/how-bossware-in-banking-is-tracking-finance-talent-health)” says Shimna Sameer, Head of Products, Solutions & Platforms at Bank of America Private Bank.

“This is time our teams are reinvesting into client engagement, with even more proactive guidance and meaningful support.”

The regained capacity is being funnelled directly back into the relationship side of the business, where human intuition remains the primary driver of value.

Shimna Sameer, Head of Products, Solutions & Platforms at Bank of America Private Bank

## A decade of disciplined investment

While many institutions are currently scrambling to define their AI strategy, Bank of America’s latest move is part of a long-term capital commitment.

The bank invests US$13.5bn annually on technology, with US$4bn of that dedicated specifically to new initiatives.

The firm’s approach to AI is rooted in a “high-tech, high-touch” philosophy. This began in earnest with the 2018 launch of Erica, the virtual assistant that has since seen over 3.2 billion client interactions.

The underlying architecture used for Erica was subsequently adapted for internal tools like ask MERRILL and ask Private Banking, demonstrating a strategy of reusable, scalable technology.

![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/jvuAlhbDac0/hqdefault.jpg)

## The future of the human advisor

Despite the aggressive push into automation, the bank remains firm on the boundary between machine efficiency and human judgment.

The strategic priority for AI in wealth management is to increase an advisor's capacity for "long-term relationship building" rather than replacing the advisor entirely.

The bank maintains that while AI can provide proactive guidance and data-driven insights, AI “cannot replace the valuable judgment, empathy, understanding and personal connection advisors bring to clients.”

Future developments will focus on further accelerating efficiency and enhancing personalisation, ensuring that the technology acts as a co-pilot to the human expert.

args.summary:
This FAQ page summarizes Bank of America's AI strategy and 10 principal AI agent use cases as of 2025, based on an in-depth analysis by Dany Kitishian of Klover.AI. The content highlights BofA's infrastructure-first approach to AI, treating it as a foundation rather than a project, with ~$13 billion annual technology investment ($4B+ for new initiatives in 2025). The core principle is "invest once, reuse everywhere."

**BofA's 10 AI Agent Use Cases:**
1. **Erica® Virtual Assistant** – Consumer banking NLP assistant with 2.7B+ interactions, 98% containment rate, and proactive alerts (60% of interactions are proactive).
2. **Ask Merrill / Ask Private Bank** – Wealth management AI for high-net-worth clients, built on Erica's NLP engine.
3. **AI Digital Mortgage** – Consumer lending with ML automation while preserving human touchpoints.
4. **Erica for Employees** – Internal generative AI assistant for 210,000+ employees, resulting in 50% fewer IT calls.
5. **GenAI for Software Development** – 17,000+ developers using AI, boosting productivity by 20%.
6. **AI Conversation Simulators** – Employee training with 1M+ simulations/year.
7. **CashPro® AI Suite** – Corporate banking with predictive analytics, forecasts, and chat.
8. **AI Fraud/Risk Management** – Real-time behavioral ML for fraud detection and credit risk.
9. **Intelligent Receivables®** – B2B payment automation and invoice reconciliation.
10. **Global Markets AI Assistant** – GenAI for research summarization and trading queries.

Key strategic elements include: a proprietary NLP engine reused across multiple platforms, 1,400+ AI/ML patents (most in finance), a bifurcated governance approach (conservative for client-facing, rapid for internal), and a "data moat" built on years of aggregation and proprietary models. External tech partners include Microsoft Azure, but most AI is built in-house.

# WealthStack Roundup: Wells Fargo Rolls Out AI Teammate for Advisors

And in other news, Envestnet on interval funds research, Vanilla adds concierge services, BondWave enhances trade oversight and SmartRIA introduces AI-driven archiving capabilities.

![Picture of Davis Janowski](https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/bltabaa95ef14172c61/blt4c1307d3e78a5f9b/68f0d8f12954899b92c790dc/01702.jpeg?width=100&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale "Picture of Davis Janowski")

July 17, 2026

![Wells Fargo Advisors sign](https://eu-images.contentstack.com/v3/assets/bltabaa95ef14172c61/blt0233fa7ff6a0e5ed/672b1dc9c43ccf40445cc538/wells-fargo-advisors-sign-new-Smith_20Collection-Gado.jpg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=80&disable=upscale "Wells Fargo Advisors sign")

Wells Fargo has launched AI Teammate, an artificial intelligence-powered capability embedded within the firm’s [Advisor Gateway (launched in May)](/advisor-support-platforms/wealthstack-roundup-news-from-wells-fargo-advisors-advisor360-smarsh-redblack) that is meant to help advisors, client associates and support teams access information and complete everyday work and administrative tasks.

The tool will be available to financial advisors across all Wealth & Investment Management advisor channels, including independent advisors who are part of Wells Fargo Advisors Financial Network.

"We are making significant investments in AI and technology to empower advisors, grow client relationships and gain market share," said Sol Gindi, head of the WIM Client Relationship Group and Wells Fargo Advisors.

AI Teammate introduces a chat-based experience that enables users to ask questions in plain language, retrieve answers quickly and take action.

In its initial phase, AI Teammate helps teams search and summarize information from the firm’s core resource center to find answers faster with plain-language search. It quickly summarizes product and process information, moves work forward with guided workflows and allows advisors to spend less time navigating multiple pages, according to the company.

Related:[FINNY AI Rolls Out 'Pay-as-You-Grow' Pricing Model](/artificial-intelligence/finny-ai-rolls-out-pay-as-you-grow-pricing-model)

Over time, capabilities will be expanded to help advisors uncover new opportunities, prepare for client conversations with personalized insights and focus on actions that can strengthen client relationships and support practice growth, according to the company.

## Envestnet Launches Research-Approved Interval Funds List

Envestnet has released its first list of research-approved interval funds that have completed the firm’s due diligence process by the manager research team at Envestnet PMC, expanding the company’s alternative investment capabilities.

The interval funds are available through Envestnet's Unified Managed Account platform, where the firm’s manager research team covers and selectively expands an approved list of interval funds, just as it does for separately managed accounts, mutual funds, exchange traded funds and fund strategist portfolios, according to the company.

“Interval funds are a relatively new investment vehicle wrapper, and advisors and investors placing money into these products for private markets exposure understandably need assurances that everything looks good, and that risks or concerns are addressed,” said Todd Rais, head of investment products and services at Envestnet, in a statement.

[Envestnet](/financial-technology/envestnet-to-launch-platform-aimed-at-speeding-advisor-client-prep) first announced the accessibility of interval funds through its UMA platform in March 2026.

Related:[The WealthStack Podcast: Building the Foundation for Enterprise AI with Dynasty’s Leslie Norman](/artificial-intelligence/the-wealthstack-podcast-building-the-foundation-for-enterprise-ai-with-dynasty-s-leslie-norman)

The firm provides account administration, trading, rebalancing and tax management capabilities.

“It's important you invest with the right manager if you’re going to invest in private markets, but most interval funds have short track records,” said Dana D’Auria, co-chief investment officer and group president at Envestnet Solutions.

Additional information can be accessed via [Envestnet’s Alternatives Research Center](https://go.envestnet.com/Unlocking-Alts-with-Envestnet).

[In June, SUBSCRIBE, a fintech that provides an enterprise operating system for alternative investments, announced a strategic partnership with Envestnet](/alternative-investments/subscribe-partners-with-envestnet-on-alts) meant to allow advisors to incorporate alternative investments made through SUBSCRIBE’s Altscape Marketplace within Envestnet’s UMA and Tamarac platforms.

## Vanilla Launches Concierge Service for Estate Planning Support

Vanilla, the estate planning platform for wealth management firms, launched Vanilla Concierge, providing advisors with direct access to the company’s team of trust and estate professionals.

The service’s first category is Abstraction Services, which includes document abstraction work that [Vanilla's in-house team has performed](/estate-planning/the-rise-of-the-estate-advisor-) since 2019, now expanded to include guided sessions where the firm walks an advisor through a client’s plan and multi-session training for practices building their own profiles.

Related:[Most Financial Advisors Are Thinking About AI All Wrong](/artificial-intelligence/most-financial-advisors-are-thinking-about-ai-all-wrong)

“Advisors have always been able to call on our team, not just our software,” said Gene Farrell, chief executive officer of Vanilla. “Vanilla Concierge gives that a name and makes it easier to access. As more firms bring us more complex work, we’re building out the ways we can provide them with the support they need.”

Julia Santullano, director of abstraction services at Vanilla, leads the work, bringing more than two decades of trust and estate experience, including over 10 years as a practicing attorney and five years directing estate and tax planning for a national broker/dealer's advanced planning team.

According to the company, Vanilla employs a team of more than 15 trust and estate professionals, including 10 non-practicing attorneys.

Vanilla Concierge is available to all Vanilla subscribers as an added service.

[Vanilla was launched in 2019](/estate-planning/betterment-bringing-vanilla-s-estate-planning-tools-to-rias) by long-time advisor Steve Lockshin and has to date raised more than $80 million in funding, with [the latest $35 million](/advisor-support-platforms/vanilla-closes-on-35m-in-funding) being an extension of its Series B round in late 2024.

BondWave Expands Trade Oversight Capabilities in Effi Platform

BondWave LLC released an updated version of its [Effi platform](/financial-technology/bondwave-rolls-out-effi-for-rias) that adds 14 configurable attributes to its Trade Oversight module and enhances its Transaction Quality Analysis capabilities, according to the company.

The company, which focuses on fixed income technology, now offers 23 total configurable reviews that firms can customize, including new attributes for Execution Yield, Base Price, Minimum Denomination, Increments, Muni Limited Offering, De Minimis and Sales Credit/Markup Variance.

“Fixed income compliance and trading teams are under constant pressure to do more with greater precision,” “With this release, we’re giving our clients deeper, more configurable tools to oversee trade activity along with richer insight into execution quality, helping teams pinpoint the exceptions that matter and better understand what’s driving their trading costs,” said Michael Ruvo, chief executive officer of BondWave, in a statement.

The new attributes can generate exceptions for internal review and resolution, according to the company.

Entitled users can now view trade information directly from their trade file, searchable by security ID and date.

The Transaction Quality Analysis solution now allows users to break out transaction cost and quality by side of the market.

The platform also upgraded to .NET 10 and expanded right-click context menu functionality across all pages.

## SmartRIA Launches AI-Powered Communications Archiving Tool

Cloud-based compliance management platform SmartRIA has launched SmartArchive, an AI-powered digital communications archiving and surveillance capability that allows registered investment advisors and independent broker/dealers to capture, monitor and review business communications across multiple channels from a single platform.

SmartArchive is the third addition to SmartRIA’s AI-powered compliance suite, joining SmartReview and SmartAssist, both introduced earlier this year.

The new product is built on technology licensed from Presults, a specialized archiving technology provider and competitor.

Specifically, SmartArchive enables firms to archive text messages, social media messages, emails and websites from one centralized system.

Founded in 2015, the company has raised two rounds of seed funding from [MarketCounsel and Dynasty Financial Partners in 2021](/financial-technology/marketcounsel-dynasty-make-strategic-investment-in-smartria) and 2023.

# WealthStack Roundup: Wells Fargo Rolls Out AI Teammate for Advisors

**Date:** July 17, 2026
**Author:** Davis Janowski, Senior Technology Editor, Wealth Management

This article covers several key developments in wealth management technology:

## 1. Wells Fargo Launches AI Teammate
Wells Fargo has introduced "AI Teammate," an AI-powered tool embedded within its Advisor Gateway platform (launched May 2026). The tool helps advisors, client associates, and support teams access information and complete administrative tasks via a chat-based interface using plain language. Available across all Wealth & Investment Management advisor channels, including independent advisors. The initial phase focuses on searching/summarizing information from the firm's core resource center, with future expansions planned for uncovering opportunities and preparing for client conversations.

*Quote:* "We are making significant investments in AI and technology to empower advisors, grow client relationships and gain market share," said Sol Gindi, head of the WIM Client Relationship Group and Wells Fargo Advisors.

## 2. Envestnet Launches Research-Approved Interval Funds List
Envestnet released its first list of research-approved interval funds that have completed due diligence by Envestnet PMC's manager research team. These interval funds are available through Envestnet's Unified Managed Account (UMA) platform. The firm provides account administration, trading, rebalancing, and tax management capabilities.

*Quote:* "Interval funds are a relatively new investment vehicle wrapper, and advisors and investors placing money into these products for private markets exposure understandably need assurances that everything looks good," said Todd Rais, head of investment products and services at Envestnet.

## 3. Vanilla Launches Concierge Service for Estate Planning
Vanilla launched "Vanilla Concierge," providing advisors direct access to its team of trust and estate professionals. The first category is Abstraction Services, including document abstraction work (performed since 2019), guided sessions, and multi-session training. Vanilla employs over 15 trust and estate professionals, including 10 non-practicing attorneys. Available to all Vanilla subscribers.

*Quote:* "Advisors have always been able to call on our team, not just our software," said Gene Farrell, CEO of Vanilla.

## 4. BondWave Expands Trade Oversight in Effi Platform
BondWave released an updated Effi platform version adding 14 configurable attributes to its Trade Oversight module (now totaling 23 configurable reviews), including Execution Yield, Base Price, Minimum Denomination, and others. Enhanced Transaction Quality Analysis allows users to break out transaction cost and quality by side of the market.

## 5. SmartRIA Launches AI-Powered Communications Archiving Tool
SmartRIA launched SmartArchive, an AI-powered digital communications archiving and surveillance capability for RIAs and independent broker/dealers. It captures, monitors, and reviews business communications across text messages, social media, emails, and websites from a single platform. Built on technology licensed from Presults. This is the third addition to SmartRIA's AI-powered compliance suite, joining SmartReview and SmartAssist (launched earlier in 2026).

# Wells Fargo debuts AI-powered teammate for financial advisers

![](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/853C0AB8A20F07D61A44FC223657E7333904A576F7FD1E41D78278D9CBE977BA/subgraphmysterio/resizefit_w960_h540;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fcio_dive_389%2Fa818f1b9b0ccd9fb0300d56faea7dccb)

Makenzie Holland

  +0.33%](/quote/WFC/ "WFC")

*This story was originally published on CIO Dive. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily* [*CIO Dive newsletter*](https://www.ciodive.com/signup/?utm_campaign=Yahoo-Licensed-Content&utm_source=yahoo&utm_medium=referral)*.*

### **Dive Brief:**

* Wells Fargo is equipping its financial advisers, support teams and client associates with [AI Teammate](https://newsroom.wf.com/news-releases/news-details/2026/Wells-Fargo-introduces-AI-Teammate-bringing--AI-powered-support-to-the-advisor-experience/default.aspx), an AI-powered chat capability that connects to the bank's modernized central technology platform, according to a Wednesday announcement.
* AI Teammate allows users to query the bank's Advisor Gateway platform in plain language and provides product, workflow and process summaries. The chat feature aims to reduce the amount of time employees spend searching for information and navigating resources, according to Evelyn Varner, chief product officer for wealth and investment management, at Wells Fargo.
* "In the short time that AI Teammate has been available, users have created thousands of prompts and hundreds of conversations — with the end goal of helping advisers be more connected, more useful, and ultimately more effective in delivering client advice," Varner told CIO Dive in an email.

# Wells Fargo touts AI Teammate to streamline advisors’ workloads

![Wells Fargo touts AI Teammate to streamline advisors’ workloads](https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cdn-cgi/image/w=1000,h=600,f=auto/https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/in/jame_639199052822184355.jpeg)

[Wells Fargo](/companies/wells-fargo/262903) has bolstered its AI-powered advisor platform with the debut of a capability that it says will streamline work for advisors.

Launched this week, AI Teammate is embedded within Wells Fargo’s [Advisor Gateway](https://www.investmentnews.com/wirehouses/wirehouse-watch-wells-fargo-debuts-ai-powered-advisor-platform/266496) desktop platform. Officially launched in May, the Advisor Gateway is the result of $1 billion technology investment made by Wells Fargo’s wealth and investment management division over several years. The Advisor Gateway also consolidates Wells Fargo proprietary systems and third-party investment software, along with research tools and a centralized investment hub.

Using a chat-based interface, AI Teammate lets advisors ask questions in plain language and quickly retrieve and summarize information, as well as accessing guidance on next steps, according to Wells Fargo. AI Teammate is available across all Wealth & Investment Management (WIM) advisor channels, including Wells Fargo Advisors Financial Network (FiNet), the company said.

Over time, AI Teammate capabilities will expand to help advisors prepare for client conversations with personalized insights.

“AI Teammate builds on the foundation of Advisor Gateway and represents an important step in our broader vision for AI,” said Sol Gindi, head of Wells Fargo Advisors and the WIM Client Relationship Group, in a statement. “We have a pipeline of additional AI tools in development that are all geared to helping our people focus on clients, deepen relationships, and deliver everything Wells Fargo has to offer more effectively.”

The advisory industry is [riding the AI wave](https://www.investmentnews.com/opinion/ai-is-no-longer-a-side-story-for-the-advisory-industry-it-is-the-story/266604). Orion's latest [annual Advisor Wealthtech Survey](https://orion.com/2026-wealthtech-outlook) underscored just how central AI is becoming: more than half of respondents said AI and automation will have the biggest impact on firm success in 2026 and beyond. However, the study cited concerns about accuracy and client [trust](/glossary/trust/263305), uncertainty about compliance/regulation, and limited internal expertise or training as the key obstacles to expanding AI use.

Set against this backdrop, independent broker dealer giant [Raymond James](https://www.investmentnews.com/companies/raymond-james/263040) recently [extended its push into AI](https://www.investmentnews.com/fintech/raymond-james-launches-ai-academy-extends-its-advisor-tech-push/266479) with the launch of an AI Academy for the company’s army of advisors.

Earlier this year Osaic [CEO Jamie Price said that two of the company’s AI tools](https://www.investmentnews.com/independent-broker-dealers/osaics-ai-tools-have-had-the-fastest-ever-adoption-among-advisors-ceo-jamie-price/266375) have enjoyed the fastest-ever takeup among its giant network of broker-dealers and registered investment advisors. Elsewhere, [Franklin Templeton](https://www.investmentnews.com/companies/franklin-templeton/263194) has described its [push to tap into internal talent](https://www.investmentnews.com/fintech/hackathons-ai-champions-and-pain-point-controls-how-franklin-templeton-is-riding-the-ai-wave/266331) through hackathons and AI champions.

AI is also having a massive impact on the broader financial industry, echoing the technology revolution seen in most parts of society. Major banks in the U.S., for example, are [harnessing agentic AI](https://www.investmentnews.com/fintech/wall-street-banks-promoting-ai-agents-from-research-aids-into-digital-coworkers/267388) in a myriad of roles, from trading, to treasury, and [wealth management](/glossary/wealth-management/265660).

# Best AI Financial Planning Apps in 2026

The best AI financial planning apps in 2026 ranked and reviewed. See what each app actually does, what it costs, and which one fits your situation right now.

![Planned](/_next/image?url=%2Fplanned-icon.png&w=64&q=75)Planned Team·

The best AI financial planning apps in 2026 do more than track your spending. They analyze your full financial picture, surface specific gaps, and tell you what to do next, without requiring a $300/hour advisor appointment.

**Quick Answer:** The top AI financial planning apps in 2026 are Planned, Copilot, Monarch Money, Cleo, and Quicken Simplifi. Each targets a different type of user. Planned is built for people at a financial inflection point who want a complete coaching system. Copilot and Monarch are strong for budgeting power users. Cleo is best for building basic habits. Quicken Simplifi excels at cash flow visibility.

## What Makes an AI Financial Planning App Actually Worth Using?

A genuinely useful AI financial planning app goes beyond a dashboard of charts. It needs to connect your accounts, understand your goals, and generate specific, actionable guidance based on your actual numbers.

The apps that deserve a spot on this list meet four criteria:

* **Account aggregation:** Pulls data from your bank, 401(k), brokerage, and loan accounts automatically, so the AI has a complete picture, not just your checking account.
* **Personalized recommendations:** Surfaces insights based on your specific situation, not generic tips like "spend less on coffee."
* **Goal tracking with real numbers:** Connects what you do today to a concrete outcome, like retiring at 62 or building a $20,000 house down payment in 3 years.
* **Transparent costs:** No hidden upsells to investment products or advisors you did not ask for.

The apps below are ranked by how well they serve someone who is new to managing money with intention. They are not ranked by feature count.

## The Best AI Financial Planning Apps in 2026, Ranked

### 1. Planned: Best for People at a Financial Inflection Point

Planned is built specifically for the moment when your financial life gets complicated: a first real salary, a significant raise, or the point where "just track your spending" is no longer enough of a system.

The core product is a Financial Health Score that evaluates your situation across multiple dimensions, including savings rate, retirement trajectory, debt structure, and cash flow, and then coaches you on what to address first. Instead of showing you a pie chart and leaving you to figure out what it means, Planned tells you exactly what your next move should be.

At Planned, we built the app around the insight that income alone does not create financial clarity. What you need is a system tailored to where you actually are. If you are 28, earning $95,000, contributing 6% to your 401(k), carrying $30,000 in student loans, and have no idea whether you should be investing more or paying down debt faster, that is the exact question Planned is designed to answer.

Pricing starts at $14.99/month or $99/year. No upsells to managed portfolios or commissioned products.

### 2. Copilot: Best for Budgeting Power Users (Apple Ecosystem)

Copilot uses AI to auto-categorize transactions and surface spending trends, with a level of customization that goes well beyond most budgeting apps. If you care deeply about tracking every dollar and want granular control over categories, Copilot is the best pure-budgeting experience on iOS.

The AI layer in Copilot learns your patterns over time. After 2-3 months of data, it flags anomalies, spots subscriptions you may have forgotten, and projects your end-of-month position based on recurring charges. Subscription is $13/month or $95/year. Android support is limited as of mid-2026, so this is primarily an iOS play.

Where Copilot falls short: it is a budgeting and cash flow tool, not a comprehensive financial planning system. It does not evaluate your retirement trajectory, advise on debt payoff sequencing, or connect your day-to-day spending to long-term goals.

### 3. Monarch Money: Best for Couples and Shared Finances

Monarch Money stands out for shared financial management. Two users can connect accounts, set shared goals, and view a unified financial picture, which makes it the strongest option for couples who are actively trying to coordinate their money.

The AI features in Monarch include automated transaction categorization, net worth tracking, and goal-based savings projections. At $14.99/month (or $99.99/year), it is competitively priced for what it offers. The interface is clean, and account syncing is reliably fast.

The limitation is the same as Copilot's: Monarch is an excellent tracker and organizer, but it does not tell you what to do. If you already have a clear financial plan and want a great tool to execute and monitor it, Monarch works well. If you need the plan itself, you will need something more.

### 4. Cleo: Best for Building Foundational Money Habits

Cleo takes a conversational AI approach, letting you ask questions about your spending via a chat interface and receive plain-English answers. It is best suited for someone who is just beginning to pay attention to their money and wants a low-friction, even playful, introduction to tracking.

Cleo's free tier covers basic spending summaries. Cleo Plus at $5.99/month adds budgeting tools, savings automation, and a "Roast Mode" that calls out your worst spending habits with humor. It is not a comprehensive financial planning tool, but for someone building the habit of looking at their finances regularly, it removes most of the friction.

If you relate to the feeling of [avoiding your bank account because the number feels like a verdict](/blog/why-you-avoid-looking-at-your-bank-account), Cleo's tone can be genuinely disarming. The AI is approachable rather than clinical.

### 5. Quicken Simplifi: Best for Cash Flow Visibility

Quicken Simplifi focuses on real-time cash flow, showing you what is coming in, what is going out, and what you will have left over at the end of the month. Its "Spending Plan" feature automatically accounts for recurring bills and irregular income, which is useful if your paycheck varies or you have significant monthly fixed expenses.

At $3.99/month (promotional pricing) to $5.99/month standard, it is the most affordable full-featured option on this list. The AI is less conversational than Cleo and less sophisticated than Planned, but the cash flow forecasting is accurate and well-presented.

Simplifi is best as a complement to a broader financial plan, not a replacement for one. It answers "where is my money going?" very well. It does not answer "what should I be doing with my money?"

## How Do These Apps Compare Side by Side?

Here is a direct comparison of the five apps across the dimensions that matter most for someone early in their financial journey.

* **Planned:** Full financial coaching system with a personalized health score. $14.99/month. Best for inflection-point planning.
* **Copilot:** Deep budgeting with AI categorization. $13/month or $95/year. Best for iOS budgeting power users.
* **Monarch Money:** Shared finances and net worth tracking. $14.99/month or $99.99/year. Best for couples.
* **Cleo:** Conversational AI spending tracker. Free to $5.99/month. Best for habit-building beginners.
* **Quicken Simplifi:** Cash flow forecasting. $3.99 to $5.99/month. Best for monthly cash flow visibility.

## What Should You Actually Look for in an AI Financial Planning App?

The right app depends on where you are right now. Not every tool is the right tool for every moment.

If you have never tracked your spending and the goal is to build that habit, start with Cleo or Simplifi. The barrier to entry is low, the cost is minimal, and getting comfortable looking at your numbers is genuinely the first step.

If you already track spending and want to connect it to a larger system, whether that means [building a financial plan](/blog/why-you-need-a-financial-plan) for the first time, figuring out how to allocate a new income, or understanding whether your 401(k) contribution rate is right, you need something that goes deeper than categorization.

According to the [CFPB's financial well-being research](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/financial-well-being/), having a clear financial plan is one of the strongest predictors of financial well-being, regardless of income level. An app that helps you build that plan, rather than just track its outputs, is worth the price premium.

The question to ask before choosing: do I need a tracker, or do I need a coach? They are different products solving different problems.

## Are AI Financial Planning Apps Safe to Use?

Account aggregation for financial apps is handled by third-party data providers, most commonly Plaid and Finicity, which use read-only connections to your accounts. This means the app can see your transaction data but cannot move money or make changes.

Look for apps that use 256-bit encryption, two-factor authentication, and do not store your bank login credentials directly. All five apps listed above use read-only aggregation through established providers. [Plaid's security model](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/p/plaid.asp) is well-documented and widely used by major financial institutions.

The more meaningful risk is not security, it is data use. Read the privacy policy of any app you connect to your accounts and check whether your transaction data is sold to third parties or used to serve you ads. The cleaner the business model (subscription-only, no data monetization), the cleaner the incentive structure.

## How Does AI Financial Planning Compare to Working With a Human Advisor?

AI financial planning apps and human financial advisors solve different problems at different price points. Understanding that distinction helps you decide when you need one, the other, or both.

A human [financial advisor vs. an AI financial planning app](/blog/ai-financial-advisor-vs-human-whats-the-difference) comes down to complexity and cost. A CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER® professional typically charges $200 to $400 per hour or 0.5% to 1% of assets under management annually. That is the right investment for complex situations: multi-state tax planning, estate work, business ownership, or managing a significant asset event like a stock option exercise.

For someone who is 27 and has a salary, a 401(k), an emergency fund question, and a student loan to think through, an AI financial planning app covers the vast majority of what they need at a fraction of the cost. The two are not mutually exclusive, and the best apps are designed to prepare you to make better use of a human advisor when you eventually need one.

For a deeper look at how [AI financial coaching actually works](/blog/what-is-ai-financial-coaching-and-how-does-it-work) under the hood, that post walks through the mechanics.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Are AI financial planning apps worth paying for?

For most people at a financial inflection point, yes. A $14 to $19/month subscription is worth it if it helps you optimize your 401(k) contribution, catch a cash flow problem early, or build the first real financial plan you have ever had. The cost of a single missed opportunity, like not capturing a full employer match, typically exceeds the annual subscription cost many times over.

### Can an AI financial planning app replace a financial advisor?

For most people in their 20s and early 30s without significant asset complexity, an AI financial planning app handles the majority of day-to-day planning needs. A human CFP® professional adds the most value for complex, high-stakes decisions: equity compensation, estate planning, tax strategy across multiple income sources, or major asset events. The two work well together rather than as direct replacements.

### What information do AI financial planning apps need access to?

Most apps request read-only access to your checking, savings, credit card, and investment accounts via a secure aggregation provider like Plaid. Some also allow manual entry for accounts that do not connect automatically. The AI needs transaction history, account balances, and ideally your income and recurring bills to generate meaningful recommendations. No app on this list requires access to move money.

### How is AI financial planning different from just using a budgeting app?

A budgeting app tracks where your money went. An AI financial planning app analyzes where your money went, compares it against your goals and financial benchmarks, and tells you what to change. The difference is the "so what." Knowing you spent $1,200 on dining last month is information. Knowing that your current savings rate puts you $180,000 short of your retirement goal is guidance you can act on.

### Do any of these apps offer investing features?

Some AI financial planning apps include investment tracking and portfolio analysis, but most do not manage investments directly. Planned tracks your investment accounts and evaluates your allocation as part of your overall financial health score. Apps like Betterment or Wealthfront offer AI-driven investing but focus narrowly on portfolio management. For a full financial planning system that also includes [guidance on how to start investing](/blog/investing-101-a-beginners-guide-to-growing-wealth), look for an app that covers both cash flow and long-term goals together.

The best AI financial planning app for you is the one that matches where you actually are right now. If you need a full system for the first time, a coaching-focused app like Planned gives you the most actionable starting point. If you are already tracking well and want deeper budgeting tools, Copilot or Monarch fill that gap. Start with the problem you are actually trying to solve, not the feature list.

--- SOURCE 1: Artificial Intelligence at Edward Jones - Two Use Cases - Emerj Artificial Intelligence Research ---
URL: https://emerj.com/artificial-intelligence-at-edward-jones-two-use-cases

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from Emerj Artificial Intelligence Research explores two business use cases of AI at Edward Jones, a U.S.-based financial services firm with $16 billion in revenue (2024), 20,000+ financial advisors, and $2.2 trillion in client assets. The firm's strategic investment arm, Edward Jones Ventures (launched 2025), funded Grantd, an AI-powered equity compensation planning platform, in September 2025.

**Use Case 1: Scaling Modernization Efforts with GenAI**
Edward Jones partnered with EPAM Systems to integrate GenAI into software engineering workflows. CIO Kevin Adams (quoted via The Wall Street Journal) described challenges with legacy mainframe systems and cloud migration. GenAI was used to automate code migration, refactoring, unit test generation, documentation, and to analyze legacy codebases. A notable example involved using GenAI to examine a legacy fee-billing system for retirement invoicing, extract business rules, and generate technical documentation. AI-generated unit tests validated that new systems behaved consistently with original applications. The company reported measurable productivity gains, faster modernization cycles, and cost savings.

**Use Case 2: Delivering Real-Time Advisor Intelligence**
Edward Jones faced data silos across hundreds of systems that prevented advisors from accessing real-time insights during client conversations. Key challenges included fragmented data, inability to deliver real-time insights, complex infrastructure, and scalability issues. The firm invested in an "advisor intelligence" strategy using AI-powered systems to surface relevant insights within advisor workflows, with key elements including real-time data integration, AI-powered recommendations, contextual insights, and scalable infrastructure. MuleSoft's Director of Financial Services noted that Edward Jones connected data across 900+ applications using MuleSoft. The article references MIT Sloan Management Review research indicating wealth management firms using AI for advisors have seen measurable improvements in efficiency, client engagement, and decision-making.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"Kevin Adams, Edward Jones's chief information officer and head of digital, described the complex environment in which the company's engineering teams operate. He attributed this complexity to the firm's long-standing reliance on legacy mainframe systems and its ongoing cloud migration efforts.", "The company reported that the use of GenAI translated directly into measurable productivity gains, faster modernization cycles, and meaningful cost savings.", "Lindsey Turner, Principal in Data Science, Analytics, and BI at Edward Jones, took to her LinkedIn to share some insights from the panel. AI usage has shifted from simple Q&A to sustained, agentic workflows. Reasoning models now account for over half of AI usage (up from near zero at start of 2025). The length of tasks AI can complete autonomously has doubled roughly every three months since 2024, with the most capable models now sustaining multi-hour coding and research tasks. "Vibe coding" is accelerating business creation, with new iOS app store submissions up ~140% year-over-year and U.S. business applications near record highs of ~500,000/month. However, agentic AI requires 100x more compute than anticipated (Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang).

## 2. Financing the AI Buildout
Hyperscaler capital spending surpassed $400B in 2025 and is on track to approach $800B in 2026 (~10x 2019 levels). Over 70% of data center capacity under construction is already leased. Cloud revenue across major platforms grew 44% YoY in Q1 2026. The four largest hyperscalers held ~$430B in cash but capex is absorbing 90-100% of operating cash flow in 2026. ## 3. Energy and AI Infrastructure
Data centers account for ~4% of U.S. electricity consumption, a share that could triple by 2030. A single large campus can draw >1 gigawatt (equivalent to Boston). Power-per-server rack has climbed from 5-20kW to 600kW for latest systems. New data centers take 2-3 years to build, but new power generation takes 5-10+ years. An estimated $720B in grid investment is needed through 2030. Data center vacancy is at a record low of 1.4%. Local opposition stalled or blocked >$150B of projects in 2025. ~70% of Americans oppose a data center near them.

## 4. Business Adoption
~20% of firms report using AI (Census Bureau survey), but a spend-based measure (RAMP) shows much higher adoption. Key barriers: People (78% of AI users bring their own tools to work, creating fragmentation), Processes (only ~1 in 5 firms have redesigned a workflow), and Price (Uber blew through its full-year 2026 AI coding budget in April). Firms are raising AI spending per employee ~50% to ~$2,000. The generative AI market is on track to reach ~$2.3 trillion by 2032.

## 5. AI and the Labor Market
U.S. employers announced 97,006 job cuts in May 2026, with AI cited most often. AI accounts for ~1/5 of all 2026 layoff announcements but only 0.08% of the labor market. AI-related hiring has created 1.3 million new global roles (LinkedIn). Stanford research estimates a 16% relative decline in employment for young workers in most AI-exposed roles. AI Engineer is the fastest-growing job title (postings up 143% YoY). AI skills command a ~28% wage premium. Potential AI exposure of tasks far exceeds current actual usage, particularly in high-skill occupations.

## 6. Productivity Potential
Nonfarm business productivity rose 2.8% over four quarters through Q1 2026, accelerating from the 1.8% ten-year average. J.P. Morgan estimates plausible productivity gains of 1.4-2.7% from AI technologies. Past general-purpose technologies took 15-20 years to show up in productivity statistics. AI's early phases may add to inflation rather than reduce it, as capital floods scarce infrastructure before efficiency gains materialize.

## 7. The Private Market Landscape
AI companies captured ~2/3 of venture capital deployed in 2025. Anthropic raised $65B at a $965B post-money valuation; OpenAI at $852B. AI-native startups reach hundreds of millions in ARR in <2 years (vs. 8-10 years historically). Private markets total ~$20 trillion in assets. 40% of private unicorns are >10 years old. J.P. SUMMARY:
<summary>
# Bank of America's AI Agent Ecosystem: Summary

This in-depth analysis by Dany Kitishian of Klover.AI examines how Bank of America has strategically deployed AI agents across its enterprise. The bank's approach is defined by a decade-long, infrastructure-first philosophy rather than chasing short-term AI trends.

## Strategic Foundation
- BofA spends approximately **$13 billion annually** on technology, with ~$4 billion directed toward new initiatives in 2025.
- Core principle: "Invest once, reuse everywhere" — the proprietary NLP engine developed for Erica® now powers specialized agents across wealth management and corporate banking.
- The bank holds **nearly 1,400 AI and machine learning patents**, the most of any financial services company (a 94% increase since 2022).
- AI is treated as foundational infrastructure ("the basement, not just the branch").

## Key Results
- 20% productivity increase for **17,000 software developers** using generative AI coding tools.
- 50% reduction in IT service calls via "Erica for Employees."
- Erica has managed **2.7 billion+ interactions** with a **98% containment rate** (queries resolved without human escalation).
- 60% of Erica interactions are now proactive insights (not reactive responses).
- $6 billion in expense savings through process improvements; 14.4 million hours of employee capacity freed up.

## The 10 AI Agent Use Cases

### Client-Facing Agents
1. **Erica® Virtual Assistant** — Consumer banking flagship; 20 million active users; handles balance checks, transfers, card management, and proactive alerts.
2. **"Ask Merrill" & "Ask Private Bank"** — Wealth management assistants for high-net-worth clients, built on Erica's engine.
3. **AI-Enhanced Digital Mortgage** — Blends AI-driven back-end automation with strategically placed human expert touchpoints.

### Internal & Operational Agents
4. **Erica for Employees** — Internal gen AI assistant for HR, IT, and administrative tasks across 210,000+ employees.
5. **GenAI for Software Development** — Coding assistants for 17,000 programmers yielding 20% efficiency gains.
6. **AI Conversation Simulators** — Training tool for client-facing staff; over 1 million simulations completed annually.

### Specialized Financial Agents
7. **CashPro® AI Suite** — Corporate treasury tools including CashPro Forecasting (reduces cash forecasting from a week to minutes), CashPro Chat, and CashPro Insights.
8. **AI Fraud & Risk Management** — Behavioral profiling, real-time transaction scoring, and network analysis to detect fraud and assess credit risk.
9. **Intelligent Receivables®** — Automates B2B invoice matching and reconciliation using AI and OCR.
10. **Global Markets AI Assistant** — Internal gen AI platform for sales and trading teams to search, summarize, and synthesize proprietary research.

## Risk Management Approach
BofA employs a **bifurcated strategy**: Erica explicitly avoids generative AI/LLMs, using proprietary supervised machine learning with pre-defined answers for reliability. Meanwhile, cutting-edge generative AI is deployed aggressively in controlled internal environments (coding, research synthesis).

## Strategic Outlook
The bank is "deep into evaluating" more advanced agentic AI but emphasizes the need for proper controls. Future deployment is expected to follow the established pattern — starting in controlled internal environments before any client-facing use.

## Key Lessons for Industry
1. Prioritize foundational infrastructure (data unification) over flashy applications.
2. Build reusable platforms, not isolated projects.
3. Stratify AI risk by use case.
4. Use AI to augment and empower humans, not replace them.
</summary>

Key evaluation criteria include fees, portfolio construction quality, financial planning tools, and transparency. The assessment scored providers on a five-point scale across four dimensions: total price (30% weighting), investment process (30%), organization (20%), and service breadth (20%), assuming a $15,000 account balance for comparison.

**Top Robo-Advisors:**
- **Vanguard Digital Advisor** (Overall: High) — Minimum $100, fees from 0.15%-0.20% annually, uses Life-Cycle Investing Model with glide paths. Clients with $50K+ get CFP access.
- **Fidelity Go** (Overall: Above Average) — Minimum $10, free for accounts under $25K, then 0.35% annually. Uses zero-expense-ratio Fidelity Flex funds.
- **Betterment/Betterment Premium** (Overall: Above Average) — No minimum, 0.25% annual fee (0.65% for Premium with CFP access). Offers glide paths and crypto ETF investing.
- **Schwab Intelligent Portfolios** (Overall: Above Average) — Minimum $5,000, no advisory fee (Premium $30/month). Uses 12 risk profiles but cash holdings of 6%-30% can hamper returns.
- **Wealthfront** (Overall: Above Average) — Minimum $500, 0.25% annual fee. Uses behavioral economics in risk assessment, offers 20 risk levels, and provides tools for spending, savings, retirement, and tax planning.

**Lower-Rated Providers:** SigFig, SoFi Wealth, Wells Fargo Intuitive Investor, Ally Invest, Empower Personal Wealth, Citi Wealth Builder, UBS Advice Advantage (0.75% fee), and Titan (1.87% for $15K account) were rated Below Average or Low due to high costs, poor transparency, or limited features.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 1: Artificial Intelligence at Edward Jones - Two Use Cases - Emerj Artificial Intelligence Research ---
URL: https://emerj.com/artificial-intelligence-at-edward-jones-two-use-cases

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from Emerj Artificial Intelligence Research explores two business use cases of AI at Edward Jones, a U.S.-based financial services firm with $16 billion in revenue (2024), 20,000+ financial advisors, and $2.2 trillion in client assets. The firm's strategic investment arm, Edward Jones Ventures (launched 2025), funded Grantd, an AI-powered equity compensation planning platform, in September 2025.

**Use Case 1: Scaling Modernization Efforts with GenAI**
Edward Jones partnered with EPAM Systems to integrate GenAI into software engineering workflows. CIO Kevin Adams (quoted via The Wall Street Journal) described challenges with legacy mainframe systems and cloud migration. GenAI was used to automate code migration, refactoring, unit test generation, documentation, and to analyze legacy codebases. A notable example involved using GenAI to examine a legacy fee-billing system for retirement invoicing, extract business rules, and generate technical documentation. AI-generated unit tests validated that new systems behaved consistently with original applications. The company reported measurable productivity gains, faster modernization cycles, and cost savings.

**Use Case 2: Delivering Real-Time Advisor Intelligence**
Edward Jones faced data silos across hundreds of systems that prevented advisors from accessing real-time insights during client conversations. Key challenges included fragmented data, inability to deliver real-time insights, complex infrastructure, and scalability issues. The firm invested in an "advisor intelligence" strategy using AI-powered systems to surface relevant insights within advisor workflows, with key elements including real-time data integration, AI-powered recommendations, contextual insights, and scalable infrastructure. MuleSoft's Director of Financial Services noted that Edward Jones connected data across 900+ applications using MuleSoft. The article references MIT Sloan Management Review research indicating wealth management firms using AI for advisors have seen measurable improvements in efficiency, client engagement, and decision-making.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"Kevin Adams, Edward Jones's chief information officer and head of digital, described the complex environment in which the company's engineering teams operate. ~20% of firms report using AI (Census Bureau survey), but a spend-based measure (RAMP) shows much higher adoption. Morgan estimates plausible productivity gains of 1.4-2.7% from AI technologies. Past general-purpose technologies took 15-20 years to show up in productivity statistics. AI's early phases may add to inflation rather than reduce it, as capital floods scarce infrastructure before efficiency gains materialize.

AI companies captured ~2/3 of venture capital deployed in 2025. Anthropic raised $65B at a $965B post-money valuation; OpenAI at $852B. JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, BlackRock, Microsoft, Google Cloud, Salesforce, Mastercard, Klarna, Bloomberg, Broadridge, Temenos.

Generative AI will become as embedded in financial services as spreadsheets, trading terminals, and core banking systems. Agentic AI will define the next phase. <summary>
# Bank of America's AI Agent Ecosystem: Summary

This in-depth analysis by Dany Kitishian of Klover.AI examines how Bank of America has strategically deployed AI agents across its enterprise. The bank's approach is defined by a decade-long, infrastructure-first philosophy rather than chasing short-term AI trends.

## Strategic Foundation
- BofA spends approximately **$13 billion annually** on technology, with ~$4 billion directed toward new initiatives in 2025.
- Core principle: "Invest once, reuse everywhere" — the proprietary NLP engine developed for Erica® now powers specialized agents across wealth management and corporate banking.
- The bank holds **nearly 1,400 AI and machine learning patents**, the most of any financial services company (a 94% increase since 2022).
- AI is treated as foundational infrastructure ("the basement, not just the branch").

## Key Results
- 20% productivity increase for **17,000 software developers** using generative AI coding tools.
- 50% reduction in IT service calls via "Erica for Employees."
- Erica has managed **2.7 billion+ interactions** with a **98% containment rate** (queries resolved without human escalation).
- 60% of Erica interactions are now proactive insights (not reactive responses).
- $6 billion in expense savings through process improvements; 14.4 million hours of employee capacity freed up.

## The 10 AI Agent Use Cases

### Client-Facing Agents
1. **Erica® Virtual Assistant** — Consumer banking flagship; 20 million active users; handles balance checks, transfers, card management, and proactive alerts.
2. **"Ask Merrill" & "Ask Private Bank"** — Wealth management assistants for high-net-worth clients, built on Erica's engine.
3. **AI-Enhanced Digital Mortgage** — Blends AI-driven back-end automation with strategically placed human expert touchpoints.

### Internal & Operational Agents
4. **Erica for Employees** — Internal gen AI assistant for HR, IT, and administrative tasks across 210,000+ employees.
5. **GenAI for Software Development** — Coding assistants for 17,000 programmers yielding 20% efficiency gains.
6. **AI Conversation Simulators** — Training tool for client-facing staff; over 1 million simulations completed annually.

### Specialized Financial Agents
7. **CashPro® AI Suite** — Corporate treasury tools including CashPro Forecasting (reduces cash forecasting from a week to minutes), CashPro Chat, and CashPro Insights.
8. **AI Fraud & Risk Management** — Behavioral profiling, real-time transaction scoring, and network analysis to detect fraud and assess credit risk.
9. **Intelligent Receivables®** — Automates B2B invoice matching and reconciliation using AI and OCR.
10. **Global Markets AI Assistant** — Internal gen AI platform for sales and trading teams to search, summarize, and synthesize proprietary research.

## Risk Management Approach
BofA employs a **bifurcated strategy**: Erica explicitly avoids generative AI/LLMs, using proprietary supervised machine learning with pre-defined answers for reliability. Meanwhile, cutting-edge generative AI is deployed aggressively in controlled internal environments (coding, research synthesis).

## Strategic Outlook
The bank is "deep into evaluating" more advanced agentic AI but emphasizes the need for proper controls. Future deployment is expected to follow the established pattern — starting in controlled internal environments before any client-facing use.

## Key Lessons for Industry
1. Prioritize foundational infrastructure (data unification) over flashy applications.
2. Build reusable platforms, not isolated projects.
3. Stratify AI risk by use case.
4. Use AI to augment and empower humans, not replace them.
</summary>

# Generative AI in Financial Services Market Summary

## Market Overview
The generative AI in financial services market was estimated at **USD 2,792 million in 2025** and is projected to reach **USD 32,413 million by 2032**, growing at a **CAGR of ~39% from 2026 to 2032** (the report cites ~42% CAGR in some sections). ## Key Market Dynamics
The market is driven by production deployment at major financial institutions rather than pilots or proofs of concept. Key statistics include:
- **JPMorgan Chase** runs 400+ AI use cases, generating USD 1.5–2 billion in measurable value annually; its LLM Suite is available to 200,000+ employees.

## Key Trends
1. **Big bank AI arms race** — G-SIBs deploying GenAI at scale with varying architectures (build vs. buy, single-model vs. multi-model).
2. **Transition from copilot to autonomous agent** — Phase 1 (2023-2024): chatbots; Phase 2 (2024-2025): copilots; Phase 3 (2025-2026): agentic AI (e.g., Cognition's Devin AI at Goldman and Citi, BlackRock's Aladdin Copilot).
3. **Multi-model architectures** replacing single-vendor LLM dependency.
4. **AI-native fintechs** (Revolut, Klarna, Nubank) operating at 5–10x staff-to-customer efficiency ratios, forcing legacy banks to accelerate.
5. **Internal-first adoption pattern** — employee productivity first, assisted client interactions second, autonomous client-facing applications third (12–18 month lag).

## Market Segmentation
- **By Application Domain**: Compliance/regulatory reporting/document review leads; code generation/software engineering is fastest-growing.
- **By Sub-Vertical**: Banking (retail, commercial, corporate) leads; payments/fintech is fastest-growing.
- **By Deployment Model**: Private/on-premises leads for regulated institutions; hybrid is fastest-growing.
- **By Region**: North America (largest), Asia Pacific (fastest-growing), Europe, Rest of World.

## Key Challenges
- Hallucination risk in regulated applications
- Model risk management at LLM scale (traditional SR 11-7 frameworks don't fit LLMs)
- Regulatory fragmentation (EU AI Act, US Federal Reserve/OCC guidance diverging)
- PII exposure through external API calls

## Key Players
JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, BlackRock, Microsoft, Google Cloud, Salesforce, Mastercard, Klarna, Bloomberg, Broadridge, Temenos.

## Future Outlook (Through 2032)
Generative AI will become as embedded in financial services as spreadsheets, trading terminals, and core banking systems. Agentic AI will define the next phase. The competitive landscape will bifurcate between institutions that build proprietary AI stacks (multi-model architectures integrated with internal data) and those that bolt on generic AI tools — the latter will struggle to compete with AI-native fintechs.

<summary>
# Bank of America's AI Agent Ecosystem: Summary

This in-depth analysis by Dany Kitishian of Klover.AI examines how Bank of America has strategically deployed AI agents across its enterprise. The bank's approach is defined by a decade-long, infrastructure-first philosophy rather than chasing short-term AI trends.

## Strategic Foundation
- BofA spends approximately **$13 billion annually** on technology, with ~$4 billion directed toward new initiatives in 2025.
- Core principle: "Invest once, reuse everywhere" — the proprietary NLP engine developed for Erica® now powers specialized agents across wealth management and corporate banking.
- The bank holds **nearly 1,400 AI and machine learning patents**, the most of any financial services company (a 94% increase since 2022).
- AI is treated as foundational infrastructure ("the basement, not just the branch").

## Key Results
- 20% productivity increase for **17,000 software developers** using generative AI coding tools.
- 50% reduction in IT service calls via "Erica for Employees."
- Erica has managed **2.7 billion+ interactions** with a **98% containment rate** (queries resolved without human escalation).
- 60% of Erica interactions are now proactive insights (not reactive responses).
- $6 billion in expense savings through process improvements; 14.4 million hours of employee capacity freed up.

## The 10 AI Agent Use Cases

### Client-Facing Agents
1. **Erica® Virtual Assistant** — Consumer banking flagship; 20 million active users; handles balance checks, transfers, card management, and proactive alerts.
2. **"Ask Merrill" & "Ask Private Bank"** — Wealth management assistants for high-net-worth clients, built on Erica's engine.
3. **AI-Enhanced Digital Mortgage** — Blends AI-driven back-end automation with strategically placed human expert touchpoints.

### Internal & Operational Agents
4. **Erica for Employees** — Internal gen AI assistant for HR, IT, and administrative tasks across 210,000+ employees.
5. **GenAI for Software Development** — Coding assistants for 17,000 programmers yielding 20% efficiency gains.
6. **AI Conversation Simulators** — Training tool for client-facing staff; over 1 million simulations completed annually.

### Specialized Financial Agents
7. **CashPro® AI Suite** — Corporate treasury tools including CashPro Forecasting (reduces cash forecasting from a week to minutes), CashPro Chat, and CashPro Insights.
8. **AI Fraud & Risk Management** — Behavioral profiling, real-time transaction scoring, and network analysis to detect fraud and assess credit risk.
9. **Intelligent Receivables®** — Automates B2B invoice matching and reconciliation using AI and OCR.
10. **Global Markets AI Assistant** — Internal gen AI platform for sales and trading teams to search, summarize, and synthesize proprietary research.

## Risk Management Approach
BofA employs a **bifurcated strategy**: Erica explicitly avoids generative AI/LLMs, using proprietary supervised machine learning with pre-defined answers for reliability. Meanwhile, cutting-edge generative AI is deployed aggressively in controlled internal environments (coding, research synthesis).

## Strategic Outlook
The bank is "deep into evaluating" more advanced agentic AI but emphasizes the need for proper controls. Future deployment is expected to follow the established pattern — starting in controlled internal environments before any client-facing use.

## Key Lessons for Industry
1. Prioritize foundational infrastructure (data unification) over flashy applications.
2. Build reusable platforms, not isolated projects.
3. Stratify AI risk by use case.
4. Use AI to augment and empower humans, not replace them.
</summary>

---

## Fully Comprehensive Findings

### Section 1: JPMorgan Chase & Co.

JPMorgan Chase & Co., one of the world's largest financial institutions ($4.425 trillion in assets, $57B net income, $182.4B revenue in 2025), has invested heavily in AI with an annual technology budget exceeding $18 billion. The bank ranks at the top of the Evident AI Index for AI maturity in banking, with over 450 AI use cases in production and plans to expand to 1,000 by 2026. The firm's technology budget reached $17 billion in 2024, with approximately $1.3 billion dedicated specifically to advancing AI capabilities and another $3.1 billion for modernizing cloud infrastructure and data platforms. JPMC has assembled over 2,000 AI/ML specialists and targets $1.5-2 billion in annual business value from AI. [1][4][5][29]

#### 1A. IndexGPT (Client-Facing Thematic Investment Baskets)

- **Product Name:** IndexGPT
- **Launch Month:** May 2024 (announced May 3, 2024, following a trademark filing in May 2023)
- **Product Type:** Client-facing AI-powered thematic investment basket creation tool
- **Customer Tier:** Available to J.P. Morgan's institutional and wealth management clients
- **Geography/Languages:** Global (launched by J.P. Morgan Asset Management); available in English initially
- **Core AI Stack:** OpenAI's GPT-4 model for keyword generation, combined with a proprietary Natural Language Processing (NLP) model that scans news articles to identify companies involved in a given theme
- **Description:** IndexGPT creates thematic investment baskets by generating a list of keywords associated with a particular theme. These keywords are then analyzed using a natural language processing model that scans news articles to identify companies involved in that space. Unlike traditional indexes based on industry sectors or company fundamentals, IndexGPT identifies investments based on emerging trends using AI-generated keywords extracted from news articles. The tool allows for the selection of a broader range of stocks, going beyond the obvious choices that are already well-known.
- **Safety & Compliance:** Built within JPMorgan's controlled environment; proprietary data is not used to train the model. The bank has protocols restricting employees from using consumer AI chatbots, and IndexGPT was developed internally with the bank's data security protocols.
- **Integrations:** Part of J.P. Morgan's broader index offering; integrates with the bank's existing investment platforms
- **Access/Pricing:** Available to J.P. Morgan clients; specific pricing not publicly disclosed
- **KPIs:** According to Rui Fernandes, J.P. Morgan's head of markets trading structuring, IndexGPT is seen as "a first step in a long-term process of integrating AI across the bank's index offering." Thematic investing gained popularity in 2020-2021 but waned due to poor performance and higher interest rates; IndexGPT aims to reignite interest by providing a more accurate approach.
- **Executive Quote:** "IndexGPT creates these thematic indexes by generating a list of keywords associated with a particular theme that are then analyzed using a natural language processing model that scans news articles to identify companies involved in that space" — Rui Fernandes, J.P. Morgan's head of markets trading structuring. [2][3][4][6][7][29]

#### 1B. Connect Coach (Wealth Advisor Copilot)

- **Product Name:** Connect Coach (also referred to as "Coach AI")
- **Launch Month:** In production by early 2025; recognized by Euromoney award on March 28, 2025
- **Product Type:** AI-powered advisor copilot embedded in JPMorgan's Connect platform for wealth management advisors
- **Customer Tier:** Wealth management advisors serving high-net-worth clients (JPMorgan Private Bank)
- **Geography/Languages:** North America initially; English
- **Core AI Stack:** Multiple AI agents and large language models (LLMs) integrated; uses NLP and predictive AI
- **Description:** An advanced AI-powered co-pilot embedded in the firm's Connect platform, which integrates multiple AI agents and large language models (LLMs) to enhance adviser capabilities. It allows 95% faster information retrieval, contributed to 20% YoY gross sales growth, and enables advisors to potentially expand client rosters by 50%.
- **Safety & Compliance:** Built within JPMorgan's secure, proprietary environment with data protection controls
- **Integrations:** Embedded in JPMorgan's Connect platform (the private bank's core advisory platform)
- **Access/Pricing:** Available to JPMorgan Private Bank advisors; specific pricing not publicly disclosed
- **KPIs:** 
  - 95% faster information retrieval for advisors
  - 20% year-over-year gross sales growth attributed to the tool
  - Advisors expected to grow their client base by 50% over the next three to five years, driven by these gains in speed and efficiency
  - During recent market turmoil, the AI tools helped teams scale service without sacrificing quality
- **Executive Quote:** "AI isn't just helping banks work faster, it's helping them show up better for clients in moments of volatility" — Michael Abbott (Global Banking Lead at Accenture, referencing Mary Callahan Erdoes). "It's about giving our people the ability to make stronger, faster and smarter decisions" — head of the investment platform on the Spectrum tool. [29][30][31]

#### 1C. SpectrumGPT (Portfolio Manager Nudge Engine)

- **Product Name:** Spectrum (also referred to as SpectrumGPT)
- **Launch Month:** In production by 2024
- **Product Type:** Internal investing platform with embedded LLMs that sends "nudge" alerts to portfolio managers

# Cleaned Research Findings: Canadian Banks' AI Portfolio-Management & Financial-Planning Copilots (2023–2026)

---

## List of Queries and Tool Calls Made

The following searches were conducted to gather information:

1. **Broad search:** "Canadian bank AI portfolio management copilot 2024 2025"
2. **RBC search:** "RBC Royal Bank AI financial planning assistant copilot launch 2024"
3. **TD Bank search:** "TD Bank AI portfolio management advisor copilot 2024 2025"

---

## Fully Comprehensive Findings

### 1. RBC Royal Bank

**NOMI (AI-powered personal finance suite)**
- **Launch:** NOMI was launched in 2017 (pre-dates the 2023–2026 timeframe for *new* launches, but the suite has been continuously expanded during the 2023–2026 period with new features).
- **Description:** RBC launched AI-powered personal finance services called NOMI (a play on "know me"), powered by Personetics Cognitive Banking applications. These services are built directly into RBC's existing mobile app, giving all RBC customers access. [6]
- **Features:**
  - **NOMI Insights:** Provides personalized, timely tips to help customers manage day-to-day finances. It offers daily insights into spending patterns, identifies unusual transactions, issues automatic reminders based on past activity, and predicts potential issues. Unlike US bank alerts which require manual setup, RBC's alerts are generated automatically. The system learns as it interacts with users, becoming more accurate over time. Over 2 billion insights delivered since 2017. [8]
  - **NOMI Find & Save:** An automated savings program. Based on predictive analysis of individual behavior and spending patterns, it determines the minimum cash needed in checking for monthly expenses and automatically transfers excess cash to an interest-bearing savings account. The auto-save can be suspended at any time, and money can be moved back to checking. Customers have saved over $1.9 billion (average $415/month or ~$5,000/year). [8]
  - **NOMI Budget:** Suggests customized budgets based on spending habits; over 2 million budgets suggested since 2019. [8]
  - **NOMI Forecast** (newest addition): Uses ML/AI to provide 7-day cash-flow forecasts based on preauthorized payment withdrawals, helping customers avoid overdrafts and manage short-term finances. Uses technology from Borealis AI, RBC's research center. [8]
  - **Ask NOMI:** Multilingual chatbot that has responded to 4 million text and voice inquiries. [8]
- **Customer tier:** All RBC personal banking customers (mass market). NOMI now serves 12.8 million personal banking customers and has about 1.5 million active users. [8]
- **Geography/Languages:** Canada, multilingual (Ask NOMI supports multiple languages). [8]
- **Core AI stack:** Powered by Personetics Cognitive Banking applications; NOMI Forecast uses technology from Borealis AI (RBC's research center). [8] RBC also developed a proprietary AI foundation model for financial services called **ATOM**, trained on asynchronous event sequences (transactions, client interactions) to enable personalized banking solutions. [7]
- **Safety & Compliance:** RBC's Responsible AI principles: Privacy & Security, Accountability, Fairness, and Transparency & Responsible Disclosure. [10]
- **Integrations:** Built into RBC's existing mobile app. [6]
- **Access/Pricing:** Available to all RBC customers within the mobile app; no additional cost. [6]
- **KPIs:**
  - 53% of NOMI users say it's a game changer for their finances. [8]
  - Customer attrition among NOMI users is less than 1%. [8]
  - Average visit time on the RBC mobile app has more than doubled from 3.5 minutes to 7.5 minutes since NOMI launched. [8]
  - One in nine Canadians had access to NOMI features on their phones within weeks of launch. [6]
  - RBC ranks #1 in Canada and #3 globally for AI maturity in financial services (fourth straight year, per Evident AI Index). [7]

**RBC Borealis (AI research & platform team)**
- RBC Borealis is RBC's AI research and data platform team, comprising architects, engineers, scientists, and product experts focused on revolutionizing finance through AI research, solutions, and a resilient data platform. [7]

- **RESPECT AI™:** A responsible AI platform providing knowledge, algorithms, and tooling for ethical AI development. [7]

- RBC and RBC Borealis are members of FinTechAI@CSAIL at MIT. [7]

- A first for the industry, Aiden is a revolutionary AI electronic trading platform using deep reinforcement learning and advanced AI algorithms to learn and adapt to changing market conditions in real time. [10]
- **Note:** This is a capital markets tool, not a client-facing portfolio-management copilot for retail/wealth management clients.
